choices.explanation: Transforming a value does not determine whether processing should start.

choices.explanation: The storage class cannot substitute for an event pattern that selects processing events.

learning.reason: An EventBridge event pattern can use the event type, bucket name, and object-key prefix as conditions.
learning.concept: When processing results are written back to the bucket, excluding the result path from the event conditions avoids recursive triggering.

title: Separating Compute Cluster Lifetime from Input Storage
prompt: A weekly Spark aggregation runs on Amazon EMR. The input and output must remain available for use the following week, but the cluster should be terminated after processing to reduce compute costs. Which architecture should be used?

choices.text: Store the input and output in Amazon S3 and launch an EMR cluster only when a run is needed.
choices.explanation: The data remains available while compute resources are used only during processing.

choices.text: Store the input and output only in the EMR cluster's HDFS and continue to reference the same HDFS after termination.
choices.explanation: The local distributed storage cannot continue to be used after the cluster is terminated.

choices.text: Store only the input in Amazon S3 and keep the final output only in temporary node-local storage.
choices.explanation: The output cannot be retained until the following week.

choices.text: Keep the cluster running 24 hours a day to preserve the data.
choices.explanation: This preserves the data but violates the requirement to incur compute costs only when needed.

learning.reason: Data stored in Amazon S3 remains available even after the Amazon EMR cluster is terminated.
learning.concept: Distinguish local or distributed storage used during processing from data that must be retained outside the cluster.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Resending Large Files by Part
prompt: A single large file must be ingested into S3 over a connection that fails intermittently. Without resending the entire file, retry only the failed ranges and assemble them into one object. Which operations should be combined? Select two.

choices.text: Store each part as a separate object and assume that GetObject with the same key will concatenate them.
choices.explanation: Separate objects are not automatically combined into one object.

choices.text: When a failure occurs, repeatedly restart PutObject to the same key from the beginning.
choices.explanation: A single-request upload does not resend only the specified range.

choices.text: Initiate a multipart upload, upload the required parts using the same upload ID, and resend only failed parts.
choices.explanation: Independent part uploads avoid resending parts that already succeeded.

choices.text: Do not resend anything; have S3 Object Replication ingest the missing data.
choices.explanation: Object replication does not recover incomplete input on behalf of the client.

choices.text: Once all required parts are present, complete the upload by specifying the part numbers and their corresponding ETags.
choices.explanation: This assembles the received parts into one object.

learning.reason: With an S3 multipart upload, each part is uploaded separately and the parts are assembled into one object at the end.
learning.concept: Retain the upload ID and part information, and also plan to clean up incomplete uploads that are left unfinished.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Running an Existing Kafka Connector with a Managed Service
prompt: For ingestion from an Amazon MSK topic to S3, use a compatibility-verified Kafka Connect S3 Sink plugin. You do not want to operate the Kafka Connect workers yourself. Connectivity and S3 permissions are already provided. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Use S3 bucket event notifications as the MSK sink.
choices.explanation: S3 object events do not retrieve existing data from Kafka and store it.

choices.text: Register the compatible plugin as an MSK Connect custom plugin and configure a Connector.
choices.explanation: This uses the supported implementation on managed Kafka Connect workers.

choices.text: Place the Kafka Connect JAR directly on the MSK brokers.
choices.explanation: Brokers and connector workers are separate execution environments.

choices.text: Send only the connector configuration to the Kafka topic.
choices.explanation: Configuration alone does not start workers.

learning.reason: MSK Connect allows Kafka Connect plugins to be registered as custom plugins.
learning.concept: A plugin defines the actual data integration process and is managed separately from the worker execution environment.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Exporting a Result Set in a Reusable Columnar Format
prompt: An aggregate result from Amazon Redshift will be reused later by Athena or another service. Export the consolidated result to S3 in a columnar format that supports scan-column pruning, without transferring the entire result to the client for storage. What should you do?

choices.text: Create only a Redshift snapshot.
choices.explanation: Athena cannot directly scan Parquet files containing the specified aggregate from a snapshot.

choices.text: Pass the SELECT result to Redshift COPY and write it to S3.
choices.explanation: COPY loads data into Redshift; it does not export results.

choices.text: UNLOAD the aggregate query result as a standard CSV file.
choices.explanation: This can store the result in S3, but it is not the specified columnar format.

choices.text: Specify the aggregate query and use UNLOAD with Parquet as the format to write the result to S3.
choices.explanation: This creates a columnar dataset without streaming the entire result to the client.

learning.reason: Redshift UNLOAD writes query results to S3 and supports specifying the Parquet format.
learning.concept: COPY loads data from S3 into a cluster, whereas UNLOAD exports results from the cluster; the two operations run in opposite directions.

category: データストア管理

title: Resolving Daily Partitions Without Registering Them
prompt: S3 output paths are determined regularly by date, and Athena is the only engine that reads the corresponding table. You want to eliminate Glue partition registration whenever data arrives and have Athena calculate the location matching the date condition in the SQL query. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Run the crawler every hour.
choices.explanation: This only registers partitions more frequently; it does not eliminate registration.

choices.text: Add the paths for every date with ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION each time.
choices.explanation: This still requires operationally registering individual partitions.

choices.text: Make the table nonpartitioned and remove the date condition from the SQL query.
choices.explanation: This loses the ability to narrow the daily scan range using the regular path pattern.

choices.text: Enable partition projection by specifying the date type, range, and format, together with an S3 location template.
choices.explanation: Athena can calculate locations from the date condition, eliminating individual registration for each date.

learning.reason: Athena partition projection calculates partition values and storage locations from configured ranges and rules.
learning.concept: Distinguish projection, which is useful for regularly organized data, from actual partition metadata that can be shared with other engines.

category: データストア管理

title: Move to a New Partitioning Scheme While Retaining Existing Files
prompt: An Iceberg-compatible engine is using daily partitioning, and you want to change it to hourly partitioning. There is no capacity to rewrite the historical data files immediately, and records from earlier dates must remain readable with the same SQL. Which design should you choose?

choices.text: Update the Iceberg partition specification in a compatible engine and write subsequent data using the new specification.
choices.explanation: Existing files can remain under the old specification, while reads can handle both specifications.

choices.text: As with the traditional Hive format, require queries to specify the new and old physical columns separately.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for transparent pruning from logical columns.

choices.text: Only rename the existing file paths in S3 to use hourly paths.
choices.explanation: This does not update the catalog specification or Iceberg metadata.

choices.text: Stop reading the table's complete history until the new specification is in place.
choices.explanation: This fails the requirement to continue reading older data with the same SQL.

source.label: Apache Iceberg公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Iceberg partition evolution allows old and new data files to be read in one table under the applicable partition specifications.
learning.concept: Because the query engine maps filters on logical columns to each specification, users do not need to embed physical paths in their SQL.

category: データストア管理

title: Apply Storage Cleanup Only to Unneeded Table History
prompt: Athena updates an Iceberg table, and the period during which past snapshots may be used has been set to 7 days. You want to retain rows referenced by the current table while cleaning up unnecessary files referenced only by older snapshots. What should you run?

choices.text: Delete the table from the Glue Data Catalog and register it again at the same location.
choices.explanation: This is not a procedure for safely removing unnecessary files while preserving the required history.

choices.text: Run OPTIMIZE after every update and assume that past snapshots will always be deleted as well.
choices.explanation: File compaction is separate from expiring snapshots according to the configured retention history.

choices.text: Use a lifecycle rule to delete every S3 object under the table location that was created more than 7 days ago.
choices.explanation: This could also delete old files still in use by the current snapshot.

choices.text: Set the retention period and minimum number of snapshots, then run Athena VACUUM.
choices.explanation: This preserves the required history and current data while managing references that are no longer needed.

learning.reason: Athena VACUUM expires Iceberg snapshots according to the retention settings and cleans up the corresponding files that are no longer needed.
learning.concept: The age of an object alone cannot determine whether it is referenced by current metadata.

category: データストア管理

title: Reduce Block Reads for Queries Filtered by Time
prompt: A large Redshift fact table receives daily inserts. The primary queries filter on a short range of event_time, and the distribution key is already optimized for joins. Which physical table design change encourages block skipping for time predicates?

choices.text: Use a sort key with event_time as its leading column.
choices.explanation: This makes it easier to narrow the blocks relevant to a time range.

choices.text: Change event_time to the distribution key and do not define a sort key.
choices.explanation: Changing distribution does not directly specify a layout in which nearby times are stored in nearby blocks.

choices.text: Only order the displayed query results by event_time.
choices.explanation: ORDER BY does not change the physical layout of stored blocks.

choices.text: Replicate the entire large fact table to every node with DISTSTYLE ALL.
choices.explanation: Replicating the data does not configure block skipping for time predicates.

learning.reason: Redshift can use the minimum and maximum values in blocks for sorted columns to skip blocks that cannot satisfy a predicate.
learning.concept: Distinguish the role of a sort key in narrowing blocks from the role of a distribution key in placing rows across the cluster.

category: データストア管理

title: Index Only Unprocessed Records
prompt: Every DynamoDB order has the customer ID as part of its primary key. Staff members need to list unprocessed orders by department. Unprocessed orders account for less than 1% of all orders, and completed records should not be stored in the index. Which modeling approach should you use?

choices.text: Set the GSI's ProjectionType to KEYS_ONLY and do nothing else.
choices.explanation: This reduces the number of projected attributes, but index membership is still determined by the presence of the key.

choices.text: Set an unprocessed or completed status attribute on every order and use an attribute present on every order as the GSI key.
choices.explanation: Completed items would remain indexed.

choices.text: Display unprocessed items with a table-wide Scan and FilterExpression.
choices.explanation: This filters the displayed results but does not create an index limited to unprocessed items.

choices.text: Set the index key attributes only on unprocessed items and remove them when an order is completed, using a sparse GSI.
choices.explanation: Only the required items remain in the index used for department-based searches.

learning.reason: Only items that have the GSI key attributes are included in the index.
learning.concept: Distinguish filtering completed items after a query from a design that excludes completed items from the index itself.

category: データストア管理

title: Designing an Expiration Attribute for Temporary Data
prompt: A session token's reference information will be stored in DynamoDB for only a few days. It is sufficient to delete it asynchronously after the expiration time, and no separate job should be managed. The application receives the time in milliseconds. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Write the time value in milliseconds directly to the TTL attribute and have the unit detected automatically.
choices.explanation: DynamoDB treats the value as seconds, so it will not reach the intended time.

choices.text: Convert milliseconds to seconds, write the result to a numeric expiration attribute, and specify that attribute in the table's TTL configuration.
choices.explanation: This deletes expired items without requiring a new scheduled job.

choices.text: Store an ISO 8601 date-time string in the TTL attribute.
choices.explanation: TTL expiration requires a numeric Unix time in seconds.

choices.text: Set the PITR retention period to expire the session item.
choices.explanation: The recoverable period for backups does not expire individual active data items.

learning.reason: DynamoDB TTL stores a numeric value representing seconds since the Unix epoch in the specified attribute.
learning.concept: Physical deletion by TTL is asynchronous. If read availability must be controlled exactly until expiration, the application must also enforce that behavior.

category: データストア管理

title: Reducing Storage Costs for Variable Access Patterns
prompt: S3 objects of a few megabytes will be retained for a long time. Which objects are accessed changes from month to month, normal reads must be immediate, and retrieval charges should not be incurred. Optional asynchronous archive tiers will not be enabled. Which option should be used?

choices.text: Store all objects in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
choices.explanation: The objects must be restored before retrieval, so this does not meet the immediate-read requirement.

choices.text: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering and disable the optional Archive Access and Deep Archive Access tiers.
choices.explanation: Objects move between tiers according to access frequency, while the standard tiers support immediate reads without retrieval charges.

choices.text: Move all objects to S3 Standard-IA and leave them there even if reads increase.
choices.explanation: Immediate retrieval is available, but retrieval charges apply.

choices.text: Move the objects to Glacier Deep Archive regardless of access frequency.
choices.explanation: This reduces long-term storage costs, but restoring objects for normal reads takes time.

learning.reason: The standard access tiers of Intelligent-Tiering support movement based on access patterns and immediate reads.
learning.concept: Per-object monitoring and automation charges are different from retrieval charges incurred when reading data.

category: データストア管理

title: Reducing Only Historical Versions After a Set Period
prompt: An S3 bucket has versioning enabled, and the current version is needed for long-term reference. The historical versions from before updates should be deleted after 90 days to reduce costs. What should be configured to do this without creating a delete marker that removes the current key?

choices.text: Set the noncurrent days for NoncurrentVersionExpiration to 90, and do not configure expiration for the current version.
choices.explanation: This removes historical versions after the specified period while retaining the current version.

choices.text: Set the current version's Expiration to 90 days.
choices.explanation: The current key might become hidden by a delete marker, and this does not clean up only the previous versions.

choices.text: Change only the current version's storage class without controlling the number of noncurrent versions.
choices.explanation: This does not specify how long historical versions should be retained.

choices.text: Suspend versioning and assume that existing historical versions will be deleted automatically.
choices.explanation: Suspending versioning does not automatically delete existing historical versions.

learning.reason: NoncurrentVersionExpiration deletes historical versions based on the time elapsed since they became noncurrent.
learning.concept: Current-version Expiration targets a different set of objects, so both lifecycle-rule behaviors must be distinguished.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Changing a Schema So a New Consumer Can Read Older Records
prompt: In an Avro stream managed by Glue Schema Registry, consumers started after a change must also read records generated with the previous schema. When a field added to the new schema is absent from older records, a default value should be used. Which combination should be used? Select two.

choices.text: Set a type-compatible default value for the added Avro field.
choices.explanation: A new reader can supply that value even when the field is absent from an older record.

choices.text: Set the compatibility mode to FORWARD.
choices.explanation: This direction checks whether previous readers can read new data.

choices.text: Set compatibility to NONE to skip validation.
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee the required direction of compatibility when the schema is registered.

choices.text: Specify BACKWARD as the compatibility mode.
choices.explanation: Comparing with the previous schema evaluates whether a new reader can read data written with the previous schema.

choices.text: Make the added field required without a default value.
choices.explanation: A new reader cannot resolve a field that is absent from older records.

learning.reason: Backward compatibility checks whether a new schema can read data created with an earlier schema.
learning.concept: In Avro, a default value lets a new reader supply a field that was not present in the old writer's schema.

category: データストア管理

title: Protecting an approved schema from a crawler
prompt: A Glue Data Catalog table uses a fixed, explicit schema. You want to continue using the same crawler to inspect data locations in S3, but you do not want the crawler to automatically replace the existing catalog definition when it detects an incorrect column type on the write side. What should you configure?

choices.text: Use a setting that merges only new columns instead of allowing any changes to the existing schema.
choices.explanation: This makes replacing existing types less likely, but it still adds newly detected columns without approval.

choices.text: Change only the catalog table name while keeping the crawler's update settings.
choices.explanation: Using a new name does not control the behavior that automatically changes the definition.

choices.text: Set UpdateBehavior to UPDATE_IN_DATABASE.
choices.explanation: This allows updates to the existing catalog, so it does not provide the required type protection.

choices.text: Set the SchemaChangePolicy UpdateBehavior to LOG.
choices.explanation: Detected updates to the existing table schema can be recorded without being applied automatically.

learning.reason: The crawler's schema change policy can log update behavior for an existing table.
learning.concept: This separates reviewing collected candidates from automatically applying them to finalized catalog entries.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Querying a shared table from your account's SQL environment
prompt: The provider account has shared a table using Lake Formation, and the recipient has accepted the required shared invitation. An analyst in the recipient account wants to access the table from Athena in that account by using a local name. What should be created without copying the source data?

choices.text: Only add an Athena workgroup.
choices.explanation: This manages query execution but does not create an alternate reference to the shared catalog table.

choices.text: Synchronize all files to the recipient's S3 location and register only the copy in the catalog.
choices.explanation: Although queries could run, this violates the requirement to avoid copying the source data.

choices.text: Grant SELECT permission directly on a nonexistent table in the recipient account.
choices.explanation: This does not create the catalog reference used by Athena in the recipient account.

choices.text: Create a resource link to the shared table in the recipient's Data Catalog, and provide both permission to access the link and permission to access the shared table's underlying data.
choices.explanation: The table can be used from the local namespace without duplicating the data.

learning.reason: A Lake Formation resource link is a catalog object that references a shared resource.
learning.concept: Permission to access the link and permission to read data from the linked table are evaluated separately.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Replacing monthly data by generation
prompt: A large batch of events is loaded into Amazon Redshift every month. When all months are needed, they must be aggregated with one SQL statement, but the oldest month past its retention period should be removed quickly as a table rather than deleted from a huge table with DELETE. Queries can be optimized to include the month. Which design should be used?

choices.text: Put all data in one table and delete the oldest month with DELETE each time.
choices.explanation: This requires the large row-level deletion that the design is intended to avoid.

choices.text: Split only the dimension tables by month and keep the fact data in one table as before.
choices.explanation: The large number of fact rows to remove would still remain in one table.

choices.text: Create one table per month and maintain a view that uses UNION ALL for the required period.
choices.explanation: An expired month can be removed and deleted at the table level.

choices.text: Create only monthly views over one huge table.
choices.explanation: Removing a view does not physically delete the rows in the underlying table.

learning.reason: Splitting time-series data into tables by period allows an old period to be handled by dropping its table while querying across periods through a view.
learning.concept: The question evaluates the difference between repeatedly performing large deletions and reclaiming space versus managing data by time period.

category: データストア管理

title: Joining warehouse data with S3 data in one SQL statement
prompt: A persistent Redshift table contains a small amount of customer information. You want to join it in the same query with a large Parquet history in S3 without copying the history into an internal table in the cluster. The data is already defined in the Glue Data Catalog. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: COPY the Parquet data into an internal table every day and join the internal tables.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid copying the data into the cluster.

choices.text: Create a database snapshot and run a JOIN against the S3 history and the snapshot.
choices.explanation: A database snapshot cannot be used in that way as a table referenced by a query.

choices.text: Set the internal table's DISTSTYLE to ALL so that unreferenced data in S3 is also added to SQL.
choices.explanation: A distribution style does not expose the schema of external storage.

choices.text: Connect a Spectrum external schema to the Glue Data Catalog and join the external table with the internal table.
choices.explanation: The cluster's customer table can be used while the files remain stored in S3.

learning.reason: Redshift Spectrum uses an external schema to access an external table in S3 and join it with an internal table in the same query.
learning.concept: Loading data internally and reading data in place impose different storage requirements.

category: データストア管理
