title: Controlling CSV Column Name Detection
prompt: The first row of every CSV file is always a header, but with the AWS Glue crawler's default inference, the first row of some files is also identified as data. The file producers cannot be changed. How should the crawler be configured to reflect this convention?

choices.text: Enable date partition projection.
choices.explanation: This changes how partition values are discovered, but it does not specify how file headers are handled.

choices.text: Create a custom CSV classifier that identifies the first row as the header and give it priority in the crawler.
choices.explanation: This leaves the input unchanged while applying the specified rule to derive column information.

choices.text: Only change the Spark write mode to overwrite.
choices.explanation: This controls output behavior and does not change how the crawler interprets its input.

choices.text: Update only the catalog table's storage location to the same S3 path.
choices.explanation: Changing the storage location does not modify the header-detection rule.

learning.reason: A Glue custom CSV classifier can specify how delimiters and headers are handled.
learning.concept: A classifier affects how data is interpreted during cataloging, but it does not modify the S3 input.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Verifying That a Foreign Key Exists in Another Dataset
prompt: AWS Glue is validating order and customer datasets in the same batch. In addition to measuring that order customer_id values are not NULL, the team wants to measure the percentage of values that exist in the customer table's unique key set. It wants to avoid repeatedly performing simple row-count checks by changing the table names. Which DQDL rule should be used?

choices.text: Apply IsUnique to the order customer_id column.
choices.explanation: Multiple orders for the same customer are possible, so this cannot replace a referential-integrity check.

choices.text: Apply only IsComplete to customer_id for all orders.
choices.explanation: This detects missing values, but it does not evaluate whether the customer actually exists.

choices.text: Use ReferentialIntegrity and specify the customer table's key as the reference dataset.
choices.explanation: This directly evaluates whether the order keys are included in the reference set.

choices.text: Use RowCountMatch only to verify that the order and customer tables have the same number of rows.
choices.explanation: The row counts can match even when unknown customer keys are present.

learning.reason: ReferentialIntegrity checks whether values in the specified column exist in the corresponding column of the reference dataset.
learning.concept: Checking for NULLs, checking duplicate rates, and checking consistency with another dataset represent different conditions.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Monitoring Glue Failures by Error Classification
prompt: Several Glue batch jobs are in operation. Monitoring only the number of failed job runs is not enough to create a dedicated alarm for Spark driver or executor out-of-memory errors. Which information should be emitted to CloudWatch by the relevant Glue jobs?

choices.text: Monitor only the job success rate using the same threshold.
choices.explanation: This cannot distinguish executor out-of-memory errors from other errors.

choices.text: Use the number of registrations in the Glue Data Catalog instead of memory usage.
choices.explanation: The number of catalog updates does not directly correspond to Spark resource exhaustion.

choices.text: Enable Glue job Observability and monitor the error metrics corresponding to out-of-memory conditions.
choices.explanation: This allows monitoring a selected error classification among the failures.

choices.text: Alarm only on the total number of S3 objects.
choices.explanation: Changes in input or output counts do not measure the classification of executor out-of-memory errors.

learning.reason: Glue Job Observability reliability metrics can record job-run errors using predefined classifications.
learning.concept: The total number of failures and metrics that identify the type of failure serve different notification purposes.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Stopping a High-Scan-Volume Query While It Is Running
prompt: In an Athena workgroup that uses pay-per-query pricing, a single exploratory query sometimes continues scanning beyond the permitted number of bytes. A notification for total usage is not sufficient; the team wants to stop an individual query after it exceeds the threshold. What should be configured?

choices.text: Encrypt query results and set the maximum scan volume with the encryption key.
choices.explanation: Encryption settings do not limit a query's data usage.

choices.text: Set a per-query data usage limit on the workgroup.
choices.explanation: The workgroup can cancel a query that exceeds the threshold.

choices.text: Delete results sooner through the query-results bucket lifecycle configuration.
choices.explanation: This changes the retention period for stored results but does not stop input scanning.

choices.text: Set only a workgroup-wide daily scan-volume alarm.
choices.explanation: This can notify the team about usage, but it does not stop the specified individual query.

learning.reason: Athena can apply a scan-volume limit to each query in a workgroup.
learning.concept: A notification for total workgroup usage must be distinguished from a limit that terminates individual queries.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Identify the Column and Row of a COPY Error
prompt: A COPY operation from Amazon S3 to Amazon Redshift failed for some files because the input value types did not match. The query ID for the load on Redshift Serverless is known. Where should you look to determine the column name, row number, and reason for the error?

choices.text: Filter SYS_LOAD_ERROR_DETAIL by the query ID and inspect the results.
choices.explanation: It provides information about the columns and load errors associated with failed input.

choices.text: Look only at the row-count summary in SYS_LOAD_HISTORY.
choices.explanation: It shows the load status, but it is not the view for directly identifying the failed column and row requested here.

choices.text: Use LISTAGG to list all successfully loaded values.
choices.explanation: It cannot trace input that failed and was not stored.

choices.text: Check the last-used time of the IAM role used by COPY.
choices.explanation: It does not show the input row that caused the error or the value-type mismatch.

learning.reason: SYS_LOAD_ERROR_DETAIL contains information such as the column and row for records that failed during COPY.
learning.concept: Filter the system monitoring view, including for serverless environments, by the target query to distinguish it from other jobs running at the same time.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Measure Stream Read Lag
prompt: A consumer aggregates data from Kinesis Data Streams by using GetRecords. There is ample time remaining before the records expire, but the operator wants to identify shards where the delay from delivery to processing continues to grow. Write bandwidth utilization alone cannot identify this. Which monitoring metric should be used?

choices.text: Check only the average IncomingBytes value.
choices.explanation: It measures the amount of incoming data but does not show whether old records are continuing to be read.

choices.text: Determine read lag using only WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded.
choices.explanation: It represents throttling on the write side and is not the same as consumer lag.

choices.text: Use the amount of time by which the retention window was extended as the lag metric.
choices.explanation: The retention duration does not show how far the consumer has progressed through the data.

choices.text: Check IteratorAgeMilliseconds with shard-level enhanced monitoring.
choices.explanation: It can detect read lag for each shard.

learning.reason: For GetRecords, IteratorAgeMilliseconds measures the elapsed time since the returned records were written to the stream.
learning.concept: Combining the maximum lag with the number of records processed makes it easier to identify shards where a backlog is accumulating.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Reuse Repeated Queries Within an Allowed Freshness Window
prompt: A dashboard frequently runs the same SELECT in the same Athena workgroup. The source data can remain unchanged for about 30 minutes, and the conditions for using an existing result are satisfied. What should be configured to reduce a full-table rescan for each execution?

choices.text: Set a long query timeout for the workgroup.
choices.explanation: It changes how long processing may run, but it does not enable result reuse.

choices.text: Enable result reuse and set the maximum age to the period allowed by the business.
choices.explanation: While an eligible existing result is available, Athena can use it without rescanning the input.

choices.text: Move the source data to Glacier and rescan it at the same frequency.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to use a result cache or the usual access-time requirement.

choices.text: Use the same output path for query results without any other setting.
choices.explanation: Using the same destination does not by itself enable explicit result reuse.

learning.reason: Athena result reuse can reuse an eligible existing query result within the specified maximum age.
learning.concept: How long result files are retained in S3 is not the same as how long they may be reused for a new request.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Prioritize Important Processing During Concurrent Execution
prompt: A provisioned Redshift environment uses automatic WLM to run short interactive BI queries and long-running background aggregations. The aggregations must not be canceled, and when the two workloads compete, resources should be allocated preferentially to the interactive processing. Which setting should be used?

choices.text: Set an execution-time threshold for the aggregation workload and cancel it when the threshold is exceeded.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to let the aggregation continue.

choices.text: Set only a fixed result-retention period for the aggregation queries.
choices.explanation: This does not control resource contention with interactive queries during execution.

choices.text: Set the query priority of the interactive queue higher than that of the aggregation queue.
choices.explanation: It aligns resource allocation during contention with the business importance of the workloads.

choices.text: Shorten the connection timeout for the interactive sessions.
choices.explanation: It does not change the priority that automatic WLM assigns to processing during contention.

learning.reason: With automatic WLM, you can configure query priority for queues and adjust allocation during contention.
learning.concept: Priority-based adjustment differs from a monitoring rule that cancels a query when conditions are met.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Resume from the failed step without repeating successful side effects
prompt: A Standard execution in Step Functions completed the preceding steps successfully but failed at a later step because of a temporary issue. The conditions for redrive are met, and the issue has been resolved. How can you resume from the failed point without rerunning the successful preceding steps?

choices.text: Assume that changing the state machine definition for the failed execution will automatically resume the execution without manual action.
choices.explanation: Changing the definition alone does not resume a previous execution.

choices.text: Delete the failure logs from CloudWatch and reuse the same execution name.
choices.explanation: Log retention and execution state are independent.

choices.text: Specify the failed execution and redrive it.
choices.explanation: This reruns the execution from the relevant step while preserving the information from the failure.

choices.text: Start a new execution with the same input.
choices.explanation: The preceding steps may run again.

learning.reason: The failed Standard execution can be redriven to preserve completed steps and rerun the step where the failure occurred.
learning.concept: When starting a new execution, determine whether the preceding steps will run again instead of reusing their successful results.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Record scheduled requests that could not start processing
prompt: EventBridge Scheduler invokes a batch API overnight. Requests that cannot be delivered within the permitted retries or retention period must be recorded in SQS. Business errors after the batch starts are handled separately. Which configuration is required? Select two.

choices.text: Send only the successful result of the batch task to SQS.
choices.explanation: This does not record cases in which the schedule could not start the task.

choices.text: Only extend the timeout for the target API.
choices.explanation: This does not add a configuration that sends events Scheduler could not deliver to SQS.

choices.text: Grant the schedule's execution role permission to send messages to the queue.
choices.explanation: This allows Scheduler to record notifications in the specified DLQ.

choices.text: Specify the corresponding standard SQS queue as the schedule's DLQ.
choices.explanation: The queue stores events whose delivery was abandoned.

choices.text: Change only the retry interval and create no audit record.
choices.explanation: Changing retry behavior does not preserve requests that ultimately could not be delivered.

learning.reason: A Scheduler DLQ can receive event information when delivery attempts do not succeed within the configured conditions.
learning.concept: Distinguish an event that the caller could not deliver from a failure inside an application that accepted the request for processing.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Reading diagnostic logs during a Glue job run
prompt: A Spark job in AWS Glue 5.0 uses many executors and becomes stuck for a long time with certain inputs. Before canceling the job, you need to investigate the Spark executor logs and the built-in application diagnostic logs together for the same run ID. Which log destination should you use?

choices.text: Inspect only the CloudTrail StartJobRun management event.
choices.explanation: The audit record for the start API does not include diagnostic logs produced by the executors.

choices.text: Wait until the delivery interval for the input's S3 access logs changes.
choices.explanation: S3 requests may be visible, but they do not deliver the internal logs of the Spark executors.

choices.text: Check only the table history in the Glue Data Catalog.
choices.explanation: You cannot determine where the running Spark job became stuck from catalog update history.

choices.text: Open the stream corresponding to the run ID in the CloudWatch Logs group where Glue execution logs are published.
choices.explanation: You can read Spark diagnostics without waiting for the job to complete.

learning.reason: AWS Glue 5.0 can send Glue logger, system, and Spark daemon execution logs to CloudWatch in real time.
learning.concept: The driver and executor log streams corresponding to the run ID are separate, allowing you to trace each part of the processing.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Refresh aggregated results at a defined interval
prompt: A dashboard in Amazon Redshift performs the same large join and aggregation every time. You want it to use preaggregated results and refresh them after ETL finishes, when the responsible team determines that processing is complete. It does not need to follow source changes immediately every time. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Control updates using only the query result cache without explicitly refreshing it.
choices.explanation: This cannot manage materialization at a specific point after ETL.

choices.text: Create only a regular view and assume that aggregated results are always stored before they are queried.
choices.explanation: A regular view stores a SQL query definition and does not provide the same precomputed result.

choices.text: Create an aggregation materialized view and run REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW after ETL completes.
choices.explanation: The dashboard can use precomputed results at query time, while the refresh timing remains under your control.

choices.text: Increase the number of COPY operations for the source data and run the same aggregation from the dashboard.
choices.explanation: This increases loading but still processes the same aggregation for each query.

learning.reason: A materialized view stores results and can be refreshed after changes to its underlying tables.
learning.concept: A regular SQL view stores a definition, but it does not precompute and store the results in the same way.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Identify Stale Data Despite a Normal Row Count
prompt: A scheduled order dataset can pass a row-count check when the previous day's partition is mistakenly republished. In Glue Data Quality, you need to verify that the data processing timestamp column is within the last 12 hours. Which DQDL rule should you use?

choices.text: Set DataFreshness to evaluate whether the processing timestamp column is within 12 hours.
choices.explanation: This checks data freshness independently of the row count or file existence.

choices.text: Evaluate only whether RowCount is within the normal range.
choices.explanation: This cannot distinguish old data with the same row count.

choices.text: Use ColumnDataType only to check that the column has a date-time type.
choices.explanation: Even if the column has a date-time type, the arrived data may be older than required.

choices.text: Use IsComplete only to check whether the processing timestamp is not NULL.
choices.explanation: The check passes as long as a value is present, even if the data is old.

learning.reason: DataFreshness can evaluate a condition on the interval between a date-time column and the evaluation time.
learning.concept: Detect stale information with an independent metric even when the row count is normal.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Set Different Limits for Data-Retention and Temporary-Processing Nodes
prompt: The volume of temporary Spark processing increases on EMR on EC2. You want to keep the maximum number of core nodes with HDFS fixed, but you do not want the addition of task nodes to stop at the same limit. What should you adjust in EMR managed scaling?

choices.text: Change the maximum total capacity to the same value as the core-node limit.
choices.explanation: This removes the room for adding task nodes at the same limit.

choices.text: Set a total maximum capacity and a smaller maximum core capacity for the target cluster.
choices.explanation: This controls core-node growth while allowing additional capacity to be allocated to task nodes.

choices.text: Only lower the HDFS block replication factor.
choices.explanation: This changes storage redundancy but does not set the node scaling range.

choices.text: Only adjust the Spot bid price.
choices.explanation: This does not separate the capacity limits for core and task nodes.

learning.reason: EMR Managed Scaling allows separate settings for the maximum total capacity and the maximum core capacity.
learning.concept: Plan the number of core nodes that also provide storage, and allocate temporary compute capacity to task nodes.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Grant Permissions to Existing and New Tables with Matching Classifications
prompt: Tables for each department are continuously added to a data lake. An administrator wants to identify approved financial tables with classification tags in the Glue Data Catalog and does not want to grant permissions individually by table name to an analytics role. Which combination should be used? Choose two.

choices.text: In Lake Formation, grant the analytics role SELECT permission using a matching LF-Tag expression.
choices.explanation: The permission applies to tables that match the expression without enumerating table names individually.

choices.text: Grant SELECT on the names of all required tables only to the tables that exist now.
choices.explanation: This does not automatically apply the permission to future tables based on an expression.

choices.text: Add IAMAllowedPrincipals to all tables in the account.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to grant access selectively to approved tables.

choices.text: Assign the key and value of the LF-Tag corresponding to the managed classification to the approved tables.
choices.explanation: The resources that should be allowed can then be identified by the tag expression.

choices.text: Apply only S3 bucket tags and expect Glue tables to match LF-Tags.
choices.explanation: S3 tags cannot replace LF-Tags.

learning.reason: LF-Tag-based access control matches LF-Tags on catalog resources with the expression assigned to the principal.
learning.concept: This management unit differs from granting permissions to individual tables or using general AWS resource tags.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Separate Permissions for Creating Tables at a Registered Location
prompt: A data-management role has CREATE_TABLE on a Lake Formation database. Only the creation of a table that points to a different registered S3 location is denied. New tables must reference that location, while permission to read the source data is managed separately. What should be added?

choices.text: Add only permission to DESCRIBE the Data Catalog database.
choices.explanation: Permission to view metadata differs from permission to specify the location.

choices.text: Grant DATA_LOCATION_ACCESS to the management role for the target registered S3 location.
choices.explanation: This supplies the permission required to create a table that points to the location.

choices.text: Grant CREATE_TABLE on another database that is outside the target scope.
choices.explanation: Increasing permissions on a different namespace does not authorize the target location.

choices.text: Add SELECT to any existing table.
choices.explanation: This may allow querying existing data but does not authorize creating a table that uses the specified location.

learning.reason: Lake Formation DATA_LOCATION_ACCESS is required to create a catalog resource that points to a registered S3 location.
learning.concept: Treat permission to specify a location separately from SELECT or permission to read S3 objects.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Auditing the Principal That Retrieved an S3 Object
prompt: The audit rules require recording GetObject requests for the customer-data prefix in S3. CloudTrail management event collection is already active, and object events for other prefixes should be excluded to control audit costs. What should be configured?

choices.text: Use advanced event selectors to choose S3 object data events and match the target prefix and GetObject.
choices.explanation: This collects only the required object reads in the trail.

choices.text: Only include read events for management events.
choices.explanation: GetObject is a data event and is not added by this setting.

choices.text: Retain HTTPS flows in VPC Flow Logs and assume that the target key for GetObject and the IAM principal are recorded at the same time.
choices.explanation: Network flows do not provide S3 API object-level context.

choices.text: Specify only PutObject for the target bucket as a data event.
choices.explanation: This records writes only and does not capture the history of the principal retrieving objects.

learning.reason: S3 GetObject is an event captured by CloudTrail data events, and advanced event selectors can narrow the scope to the required resources and operations.
learning.concept: Specify whether the API is a read or write, the S3 object resource, and the applicable prefix.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Detecting a Custom Customer Number as Sensitive Information
prompt: Internal customer numbers follow rules that differ from common personal identification numbers. You need to inspect the applicable files in S3 with Macie and use business keywords near the number to reduce false positives. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Create a custom data identifier that defines the required regular expression and keywords, and use it in sensitive data discovery.
choices.explanation: This makes it possible to detect data according to the organization’s unique format.

choices.text: Register the customer-number regular expression in GuardDuty S3 Malware Protection.
choices.explanation: Malware inspection is separate from custom sensitive-data classification.

choices.text: Use only built-in identifiers and assume that an identifier with a similar name also includes customer numbers.
choices.explanation: Built-in identifiers cannot specify the unique pattern and keywords required here.

choices.text: Tag the files when customer numbers appear in S3 metadata without examining the file contents.
choices.explanation: This does not match the requirement to compare the format and context within the files.

learning.reason: Macie custom data identifiers can express detection rules using organization-specific regular expressions, keywords, and related criteria.
learning.concept: Built-in identifiers alone cannot precisely define an organization-specific format.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Encrypting ETL Output, Logs, and State Separately
prompt: An AWS Glue Spark job stores results in S3, writes logs to CloudWatch Logs, and uses job bookmarks. You need to explicitly specify the three targets that use an organization-provided KMS key and apply the settings to the job as a consolidated configuration. The execution role can be granted the required KMS permissions. What should be configured?

choices.text: Configure only S3 default encryption.
choices.explanation: This applies to objects in the output bucket and does not include settings for Logs or job bookmarks.

choices.text: Only allow encryption operations in the job’s IAM role.
choices.explanation: Although this can permit key use, it does not specify which encryption settings each target should use.

choices.text: Enable only metadata encryption for the Glue Data Catalog.
choices.explanation: This manages a different scope from the logs and state used by the job.

choices.text: Create a Glue security configuration that specifies encryption and the KMS key for each target, then associate it with the job.
choices.explanation: This explicitly defines the three protection settings used during execution.

learning.reason: A Glue security configuration can specify encryption for S3 targets, CloudWatch Logs, and job bookmarks.
learning.concept: S3 bucket default encryption alone does not define the encryption settings for the job’s logs and bookmarks.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Enforcing a Private Access Path to a Bucket
prompt: A job using the same IAM role as other jobs in the environment must be denied access to a data bucket when the request does not use the designated VPC endpoint. The operator understands that console operations from outside the VPC may also be denied by this policy. Which control should be used?

choices.text: Add a bucket policy condition that denies requests when aws:SourceVpce differs from the specified value.
choices.explanation: The bucket itself can deny requests originating from any endpoint other than the specified one.

choices.text: Only add an Allow statement to the endpoint policy for the designated endpoint.
choices.explanation: Requests reaching the bucket through another path are not evaluated by that endpoint.

choices.text: Only change the S3 encryption setting from SSE-S3 to SSE-KMS.
choices.explanation: This changes protection for data at rest but does not require the designated VPC endpoint.

choices.text: Rely only on S3 Block Public Access to deny every other access path for the permitted IAM role.
choices.explanation: This feature controls public permissions; it does not add connection-path restrictions for an otherwise permitted principal.

learning.reason: A bucket policy condition using aws:SourceVpce can deny requests that do not pass through a specified endpoint.
learning.concept: Distinguish between the resources allowed by the endpoint and the request paths allowed by the bucket.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Prevent deletion of existing evidence versions before their retention deadline
prompt: An audit bucket supports versioning and Object Lock, and each version of evidence must be retained for a specified period. The requirement is that neither regular operators nor administrators can shorten the retention period or delete a protected version before its deadline. Which option should be selected?

choices.text: Restrict deletion operations only by configuring the lifecycle of noncurrent versions.
choices.explanation: This automates expiration but does not reject early deletion by users.

choices.text: Keep versioning enabled and allow explicit deletion of versions.
choices.explanation: Explicitly deleting a version could cause evidence to be lost.

choices.text: Assume that Governance mode alone always prevents authorized administrators from bypassing retention.
choices.explanation: A principal with the required bypass permissions can bypass retention under the applicable conditions.

choices.text: Set a Compliance mode retention period on the required object versions.
choices.explanation: Administrators cannot shorten the retention period or delete a protected version before its deadline.

learning.reason: With S3 Object Lock Compliance mode, shortening retention before the deadline and deleting protected versions are restricted.
learning.concept: Governance mode allows a principal with the necessary permissions to bypass retention, so it provides different protection.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Keep fixed database passwords out of analytics tools
prompt: An analytics tool connects to a provisioned Redshift cluster through an authenticated IAM role. The connection must use temporary database credentials for each connection, without storing a fixed database password locally. What should be configured?

choices.text: Use a compatible IAM-authentication driver or GetClusterCredentials, and allow the role to obtain temporary credentials for the target database user.
choices.explanation: This preserves the database identity while issuing a connection password only for a limited time.

choices.text: Write session information to S3 and use it as the Redshift user's database password.
choices.explanation: Writing to S3 is not linked to database authentication.

choices.text: Expose the Redshift cluster's service role to the workload and omit the password for SQL connections.
choices.explanation: A cluster-side role used for access to resources such as S3 does not directly authenticate a user's database connection.

choices.text: Set the IAM access key secret directly as the fixed Redshift database password.
choices.explanation: This does not use the mechanism for obtaining temporary database credentials through IAM authentication.

learning.reason: Redshift can obtain time-limited database credentials based on IAM authentication.
learning.concept: IAM credentials used to authenticate AWS API operations differ from temporary database credentials used for SQL connections.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Require TLS for analytics connections
prompt: Data in a provisioned Redshift cluster is read over TLS by an approved analytics tool. The cluster must reject plaintext connections, and the analytics tool must verify both the server certificate's trust and the destination hostname. Which settings should be selected? Select two.

choices.text: Select the SSL mode verify-full in the compatible client and configure the certificates required for trust.
choices.explanation: This enables certificate trust verification and hostname matching.

choices.text: Open the SQL port in the security group and allow only the TCP protocol.
choices.explanation: A security group does not determine whether TLS is used on the specified port.

choices.text: Set the client's SSL mode to require only and assume that hostname matching is also performed.
choices.explanation: Requiring an encrypted connection does not guarantee verification of the specified hostname.

choices.text: Set require_ssl to true in the cluster parameter group applied to the cluster.
choices.explanation: This prevents the cluster from accepting unencrypted connections.

choices.text: Enable KMS encryption when the cluster is stored.
choices.explanation: This protects data at rest and does not change the requirement for encrypted connections.

learning.reason: Making SSL mandatory in the Redshift configuration rejects client connections that are not encrypted.
learning.concept: Distinguish optional client-side settings from the conditions enforced by the server.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Distinguish calls from different customers handled by a delegate
prompt: An external analytics service operates AWS accounts for many customers and assumes an IAM role for each customer's target data. The service must prevent the external principal shared by those customers from accidentally assuming a role ARN specified by a different customer. What should be checked in the trust relationship?

choices.text: Shorten the maximum session duration of the customer-facing role.
choices.explanation: This limits how long the role can be used but does not validate the relationship between the requester and the customer.

choices.text: Identify the customer only by the alias of the key used to encrypt the S3 destination.
choices.explanation: Data-encryption settings are not used as the customer condition for AssumeRole.

choices.text: Require the third party to pass a value assigned for the target customer and require a match through sts:ExternalId in the trust policy.
choices.explanation: This validates that the request from the shared external principal corresponds to the specified customer.

choices.text: Allow only the principal from the external account and add no condition identifying the customer.
choices.explanation: When the same principal serves multiple customers, this cannot distinguish which customer's request is being made.

learning.reason: For an IAM principal shared by a third party, a customer-specific external ID can be used as a condition on AssumeRole.
learning.concept: The third party manages a value for distinguishing each customer, while the role trust relationship is also limited to the designated principal.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Change how the same table appears based on the user's role
prompt: In a Redshift member table, authorized business staff must be able to view phone numbers in full. An analytics role uses the same table with the same SQL, but must see only part of each number. Do not create a copy of the data or modify the stored values. What should be used?

choices.text: Apply column-level SELECT denial to the entire table and assume that the analytics role can see partial values.
choices.explanation: This only prevents the column from being read; it does not mask and return the value.

choices.text: Create a masking policy that partially masks phone numbers and associate it with the target column and analytics role.
choices.explanation: The column's displayed value can be changed when it is queried by the analytics role.

choices.text: Use Row-Level Security for the analytics role to exclude every row containing a phone number.
choices.explanation: The rows would be removed, so the requirement to retain a specified partial value would not be met.

choices.text: Update every original value with a partially masked phone number.
choices.explanation: Business staff would also lose access to the original numbers.

learning.reason: Dynamic data masking can change how a column appears at query time based on a specified role or other context.
learning.concept: Separate access control for the rows themselves from the representation of column values when rows are returned.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Migrate variably sized LOBs without data loss
prompt: DMS is migrating attachment data from an internal database. The maximum size of the LOBs cannot be guaranteed in advance, and completeness is more important than migration speed. Which setting should be selected for the applicable engine?

choices.text: Select Full LOB mode and verify throughput with actual data that includes large LOBs.
choices.explanation: LOBs can be migrated without truncating them at an unknown size limit.

choices.text: Use the average observed size as the limit in Limited LOB mode.
choices.explanation: LOBs larger than the average could be truncated.

choices.text: Exclude the LOB column and migrate only the base table.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to migrate the attachment data.

choices.text: Only increase the full-load parallelism.
choices.explanation: This does not change the conditions under which LOBs are truncated.

learning.reason: Full LOB mode transfers LOBs in chunks without truncating them based on size.
learning.concept: Limited LOB mode prioritizes efficiency up to a configured limit, so its size assumptions differ.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Change the target schema name without modifying the application
prompt: DMS is migrating tables from the sales schema, but the target must use the sales_archive schema to comply with an integration convention. Keep the source names and column names unchanged, and apply the same mapping to all target tables in scope. What should be configured?

choices.text: Specify the target name as the source schema in the selection rule.
choices.explanation: A selection rule chooses tables on the source; it does not rename the destination.

choices.text: Rename the source schema before switching over.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to keep using the source application unchanged.

choices.text: Include sales_archive in the replication task ID.
choices.explanation: The task ID does not specify the names of destination tables.

choices.text: In addition to a selection rule for the tables in scope, use a transformation rule that renames the target schema.
choices.explanation: This writes to the specified destination while preserving the names on the source side.

learning.reason: DMS transformation rules can change names in the target namespace.
learning.concept: Combine a rule that selects the objects to copy with a rule that changes their names at the destination.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Exclude only selected inputs from transformed delivery
prompt: Firehose transforms received records with Lambda. For business reasons, some inputs should be ignored and excluded as processed records rather than sent to the failure-isolation output. How should the corresponding records be handled in the Lambda response?

choices.text: Leave the result for each applicable record as Ok.
choices.explanation: It would be treated as a successfully transformed record eligible for delivery.

choices.text: Remove the applicable ID from the response.
choices.explanation: This would break the required correspondence between the records requested by Firehose and the results.

choices.text: Return a response corresponding to the original recordId and set the applicable result to Dropped.
choices.explanation: This tells Firehose to intentionally exclude the record from delivery.

choices.text: Set the applicable record to ProcessingFailed.
choices.explanation: This treats intentional exclusion as a transformation failure.

learning.reason: A Firehose transformation response preserves the original recordId and uses a result code to communicate how each record should be handled during delivery.
learning.concept: Distinguish Dropped, which intentionally discards a record, from ProcessingFailed, which indicates a transformation failure.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Convert JSON to Parquet During S3 Delivery
prompt: Data Firehose is delivering structured JSON to S3. To read only selected columns downstream with Athena, you need to convert the data to Parquet during delivery. Do not add another job or Lambda. Which two settings should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Specify a Glue Data Catalog table that corresponds to the input columns and data types.
choices.explanation: Firehose can retrieve the schema it uses during conversion.

choices.text: Only add the .parquet extension in S3.
choices.explanation: The byte format of the object does not change.

choices.text: Only change S3 compression to GZIP.
choices.explanation: This compresses JSON; it does not convert it to Parquet.

choices.text: Set the catalog output format to Parquet in the Athena workgroup.
choices.explanation: This does not configure conversion before Firehose delivery.

choices.text: Enable record format conversion in the S3 delivery stream and select Parquet as the output format.
choices.explanation: The delivery process converts the data to a columnar storage format.

learning.reason: Firehose record format conversion can deserialize JSON and use the catalog schema to produce Parquet.
learning.concept: Compression and conversion to a columnar format are separate settings.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Transfer Data in Response to a SaaS Event
prompt: Ingest corresponding Salesforce events into S3. Transfer data only when a change event is emitted, without polling the API at regular intervals or running a custom server. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Query Salesforce every minute with a scheduled flow.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to avoid polling.

choices.text: Use an AppFlow event trigger that responds to the target Salesforce event.
choices.explanation: It can transfer data to S3 in response to an event from the source.

choices.text: Start the Salesforce change ingestion from an S3 arrival event.
choices.explanation: Before the transfer, S3 cannot receive the external change event.

choices.text: Create an on-demand flow and start it manually every morning.
choices.explanation: It does not start when the event is emitted.

learning.reason: AppFlow can start a flow when a corresponding Salesforce event triggers it.
learning.concept: Select the event to use first, then determine the S3 output and downstream processing.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Rerun a Standardized Procedure as a Published Version
prompt: An operations team member tested a procedure in the Glue DataBrew interface to standardize column names and fill missing values. The same transformation must be applied to S3 input every time, without including subsequent edits made during development in production. Which operating procedure should be used?

choices.text: Publish the validated recipe and run a recipe job that specifies the corresponding published version.
choices.explanation: This allows the transformation method to be preserved while running it repeatedly.

choices.text: Only append the transformation procedure's version number to the S3 output name.
choices.explanation: A name alone does not fix the recipe that will be executed.

choices.text: Start each production run without saving project changes.
choices.explanation: This does not fix a specific validated version for execution.

choices.text: Schedule only a profile job for the same dataset.
choices.explanation: A profile job can collect statistics, but it does not apply the specified transformation procedure.

learning.reason: A DataBrew recipe can be published and applied by a recipe job.
learning.concept: Distinguish changes made during development from the version executed in production.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Distribute a Small Lookup Table to Each Executor
prompt: A Glue Spark job joins several terabytes of events with a 10 MB lookup table on every run. The lookup table fits in each executor's memory, and you want to reduce the time required to redistribute the large input by the join key. Which method should you use?

choices.text: Specify a join that broadcasts the small lookup table.
choices.explanation: This reduces the need to redistribute the large event table across the network.

choices.text: Broadcast the large event table.
choices.explanation: It does not fit in each executor's memory.

choices.text: Gather both inputs into a single partition and join them.
choices.explanation: Processing becomes concentrated in one place and parallelism is lost.

choices.text: Use key salting and replicate the lookup table for every key.
choices.explanation: This is intended to mitigate skew and does not provide the local lookup procedure for a small table under these conditions.

learning.reason: With a broadcast join of the smaller side, each executor can access the lookup table and the large side's join shuffle can be avoided.
learning.concept: Distinguish the sizes of the large and small sides and verify the memory limit.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Preserving streaming progress across restarts
prompt: A long-running AWS Glue streaming job is restarted during scheduled maintenance. On restart, it must resume the progress of batches already retrieved, while business-level deduplication is handled on the output side. What should be preserved?

choices.text: Keep the same S3 checkpoint location.
choices.explanation: The restarted job can refer to the position that was already processed.

choices.text: Clear all checkpoints every time.
choices.explanation: The streaming progress from before the interruption would be lost.

choices.text: Enable job bookmarks alone and delete the checkpoints.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve streaming progress.

choices.text: Use the same S3 output location and rely on it alone to restore the progress position automatically.
choices.explanation: The output location by itself does not reproduce checkpoint state.

learning.reason: AWS Glue streaming stores progress information in checkpoints.
learning.concept: Batch job bookmarks and streaming checkpoints serve different purposes.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Launching the same processing in parallel for independent inputs
prompt: You need to transform 500 independent input files using the same container. A list of the file names is stored in S3, and each task must be assigned a different file. What should you use in AWS Batch instead of creating 500 job definitions?

choices.text: Include one fixed index in the container configuration and launch it 500 times.
choices.explanation: Every task would select the same input.

choices.text: Submit a job with an array size of 500, and have each child job use its array index to select the corresponding row in the list.
choices.explanation: This reuses one definition and handles the independent inputs in parallel.

choices.text: Pass all inputs to one executor and process them serially.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to process the tasks in parallel.

choices.text: Set the job priority to the number of files.
choices.explanation: A priority value does not create different child jobs.

learning.reason: AWS Batch array jobs pass AWS_BATCH_JOB_ARRAY_INDEX to child jobs.
learning.concept: The same processing definition can be reused while each task selects an individual input from its index.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Reusing an expensive intermediate result across multiple outputs
prompt: A Spark job cleanses a large input and produces three different aggregations from the same transformed result. The transformation can be executed multiple times, but recomputing it is expensive. The intermediate data fits in the applicable persistence area. What should you do?

choices.text: Release the cache immediately after the first aggregation and continue with the others.
choices.explanation: The intermediate result could not be reused for the remaining two aggregations.

choices.text: Split reads from the same source across three jobs and share the cache.
choices.explanation: An in-process cache is not shared between separate Spark applications.

choices.text: Define a separate copy of the same cleansing DataFrame before each aggregation action.
choices.explanation: Each processing path may recompute the transformation.

choices.text: Cache the DataFrame after cleansing, share it across the three aggregations, and then call unpersist.
choices.explanation: This reduces the need to repeat the common transformation for each aggregation.

source.label: Apache Spark公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Spark caching can reduce recomputation of an intermediate result that is used multiple times.
learning.concept: Keep the result after its first evaluation and release it only after all aggregations have read it.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Preventing the same business processing from being repeated after redelivery
prompt: A standard SQS queue is used to process inventory-update events. Each event has an ID that remains unchanged when the event is redelivered, and the result is recorded as one DynamoDB item. Multiple consumers can process messages concurrently. How should you prevent duplicate updates?

choices.text: Use the business event ID as the result key and perform a conditional write only when the key does not yet exist.
choices.explanation: Even with concurrent processing of the same ID, creation of the result can be limited to once.

choices.text: Assume that extending the visibility timeout eliminates duplicate delivery entirely.
choices.explanation: Standard queues require you to account for duplicate delivery.

choices.text: Generate a different UUID for every SQS receive operation and use it as the result key.
choices.explanation: The same business event would be recorded under different keys.

choices.text: Read the result table first and, if the item is absent, write without a condition.
choices.explanation: Two concurrent processes could both determine that the item is absent.

learning.reason: A conditional write can check whether the target key exists and write the item as one atomic operation.
learning.concept: With a two-step read-then-write process, both concurrent executions can observe absence and succeed.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Avoid occupying worker slots while waiting for data to arrive
prompt: In a supported version of Amazon MWAA, many DAGs wait for input in S3. You want to resume processing when the input arrives without continuously holding normal task-worker slots during sensor waiting. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Shorten the DAG schedule interval and add more identical waiting sensors.
choices.explanation: This can increase the number of slots consumed by waiting tasks.

choices.text: Treat the sensor as successful even when the input has not arrived.
choices.explanation: This removes the wait but does not ensure that the input arrives.

choices.text: Use a supported sensor as deferrable and verify the required triggerer configuration.
choices.explanation: The worker slot can be released while the sensor waits.

choices.text: Increase the number of CPUs running the normal polling sensors.
choices.explanation: The sensors still consume worker execution slots while waiting.

learning.reason: A supported deferrable operator or sensor can delegate the wait to a triggerer.
learning.concept: Separate waiting from the normal behavior that keeps a worker occupied through polling.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Proceed when an external load reports completion
prompt: A Standard Step Functions workflow starts an internal ingestion process through SQS, using IAM permissions in the same AWS account. The workflow must wait until the external process reports its result, and you do not want to add periodic status polling. Which two components should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Use splitting the input with Distributed Map as the completion notification.
choices.explanation: Splitting the processing does not notify the workflow of the external result.

choices.text: Use an SQS callback integration in the workflow that includes a task token.
choices.explanation: The workflow does not proceed after only sending the SQS message; it can wait for the completion notification.

choices.text: When the external process completes, call SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure with the token.
choices.explanation: This returns the success or failure result to the original execution.

choices.text: Match a fixed Wait duration to the external process and mark the task successful.
choices.explanation: This cannot determine the actual completion time or outcome.

choices.text: Treat the message ID returned after sending to SQS as proof of a successful external load.
choices.explanation: Message acceptance and processing results are different events.

learning.reason: With a callback integration, the external task receives a token and the state waits until a completion notification using that token arrives.
learning.concept: Treat successful delivery to SQS and receipt of the external result as separate events.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Start ingestion at each office’s local business time
prompt: Start ingestion at 9:00 a.m. at each location on every business day. The time must remain 9:00 a.m. in regions that observe daylight saving time, and you do not want to rewrite UTC rules manually by season. Which specification should you use?

choices.text: Use only a rate expression with a 24-hour period.
choices.explanation: It cannot express both the weekday condition and a fixed local time.

choices.text: Lengthen the flexible time window.
choices.explanation: This does not specify the time zone used for evaluation.

choices.text: Fix one UTC time and share it across all locations.
choices.explanation: The local time shifts when time-zone offsets or daylight saving rules change.

choices.text: Set weekdays at 9:00 a.m. and each location’s IANA time zone in the Scheduler cron expression.
choices.explanation: The schedule can be evaluated using local time and daylight saving rules.

learning.reason: The EventBridge Scheduler cron expression can be evaluated in the specified IANA time zone.
learning.concept: Distinguish a schedule based on elapsed time from one based on local clock time.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Load only the files finalized for a batch
prompt: A shared S3 prefix contains input from multiple batches. With Amazon Redshift COPY, you need to load only the object list finalized by the processing team and must not treat the load as successful when a required file is missing. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Create a manifest that lists each S3 URL and marks the required files, then use MANIFEST with COPY.
choices.explanation: This loads only the finalized list and detects missing required files.

choices.text: Set MAXERROR to a large value and make an incomplete file list an error.
choices.explanation: Allowing row errors is different from selecting required files.

choices.text: Specify the shared prefix in a normal COPY command.
choices.explanation: This can include files from other batches.

choices.text: Assume that adding S3 tags causes a normal COPY command to automatically select objects matching those tags.
choices.explanation: A normal COPY command cannot directly use those tags as a selection condition.

learning.reason: A COPY manifest selects load files individually, and required entries can cause a missing file to produce an error.
learning.concept: A prefix match alone cannot exclude another batch stored in the same location.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Retry only unregistered events
prompt: Multiple records were sent to Kinesis Data Streams with PutRecords, and only some were throttled. What should the producer do to identify the failures and reduce unnecessary sends?

choices.text: Use FailedRecordCount to obtain the count and resend records from the end of the array regardless of their positions in the response.
choices.explanation: This does not correspond to the actual failed input records.

choices.text: Look only at the HTTP success status and treat all records as successful.
choices.explanation: This misses partial failures.

choices.text: Match the response array to the original input order and send only retryable failures with backoff.
choices.explanation: This avoids unnecessary retries of records that already succeeded.

choices.text: Resend all records simultaneously if even one record fails.
choices.explanation: This resends records that already succeeded.

learning.reason: PutRecords returns the success or failure status corresponding to each input record, so only the failed records can be retried.
learning.concept: Overall API success is not the same as successful writing of every individual record.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Run an existing Spark job without managing a cluster
prompt: An existing Spark batch runs only a few days each month and must be moved to AWS. You want to bring the Spark code and required dependencies while letting a managed service configure and provision the workers used for execution. Which option should you choose when using EMR?

choices.text: Start the job by uploading only the Spark archive to S3.
choices.explanation: No environment for running Spark is provided.

choices.text: Run the job in a Spark application on EMR Serverless.
choices.explanation: This runs the existing Spark processing without continuously operating a fleet of instances.

choices.text: Keep an EMR on EC2 cluster running with the same number of instances at all times.
choices.explanation: This requires operating a cluster that is unnecessary for most of the month.

choices.text: Build Kubernetes yourself and operate a Spark operator.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to delegate worker and infrastructure management.

learning.reason: EMR Serverless provides the execution capacity needed to run supported Spark jobs.
learning.concept: Use the application definition separately from individual job runs to manage execution timing and cost.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Reduce the number of small output files
prompt: A Glue Spark process creates many small files in S3. The partitions immediately before writing are balanced, and there is no need to repartition by key. You want to reduce the number of output partitions without shuffling all the data. What should you choose?

choices.text: Write each event to its own partition.
choices.explanation: This creates even more granular output.

choices.text: Keep the same number of files and change only the file extension of the small files.
choices.explanation: Neither the file count nor the actual file size changes.

choices.text: Use repartition to redistribute all the data.
choices.explanation: Although it can change the number of output partitions, it does not meet the requirement to avoid a full shuffle.

choices.text: Before writing, use coalesce to combine the data into an appropriate small number of partitions.
choices.explanation: This reduces the number of output files without shuffling all the data.

learning.reason: When Spark coalesce reduces the number of partitions, it can avoid a full shuffle.
learning.concept: With uniformly distributed input, the growth of small files can be limited without performing a large-scale redistribution.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Preserve transaction order in change files
prompt: DMS sends changes from a relational database to S3 as CSV files. Rather than separating changes from multiple tables by table, you want downstream consumers to read the changes from the same transaction in transaction order. Which S3 target configuration should you use?

choices.text: Treat the lexicographical order of S3 objects as the transaction commit order.
choices.explanation: Commit order cannot necessarily be determined from independent table-specific outputs.

choices.text: Only split the target into Parquet files by table and time.
choices.explanation: File partitioning alone does not produce the required transaction-ordered output.

choices.text: Enable PreserveTransactions and configure CdcPath.
choices.explanation: This stores changes from the same DMS task in transaction order.

choices.text: Rerun only the source full load.
choices.explanation: This is not a CDC configuration for recording the order of ongoing changes.

learning.reason: The DMS S3 target can preserve CDC transaction order by using PreserveTransactions.
learning.concept: Confirm the CDC file path and the CSV configuration conditions that support order preservation.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Do not run downstream steps after a failed transformation
prompt: Register transformation, publication, and audit in sequential EMR steps. If the transformation fails, cancel the waiting publication step but keep the cluster running for log investigation. Which failure action should be used?

choices.text: Choose TERMINATE_CLUSTER.
choices.explanation: Publication stops, but the cluster also terminates.

choices.text: Choose CONTINUE.
choices.explanation: Subsequent processing continues even after the failure.

choices.text: Register the transformation step with CANCEL_AND_WAIT.
choices.explanation: Waiting steps are canceled while the cluster is retained.

choices.text: Lower the cluster's scaling limit.
choices.explanation: This does not change how subsequent steps are handled after a step fails.

learning.reason: A step failure action can cancel waiting steps while retaining the existing cluster.
learning.concept: Distinguish terminating the cluster from canceling only subsequent steps.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Do not aggregate missing keys into one fictional customer
prompt: Perform a left outer join from a Spark event table to a customer table. Events whose customer ID is NULL must remain in the count, but customer attributes must not be attached. Do not create a customer row dedicated to NULL values. Which join should be used?

choices.text: Convert both NULL values to the same fixed value and perform an equijoin.
choices.explanation: The fictional keys created from NULL could match each other.

choices.text: Perform a LEFT OUTER JOIN using the normal equality condition on customer ID.
choices.explanation: NULL events remain, but their customer attributes are NULL because no match exists.

choices.text: Perform an INNER JOIN using the normal equality condition.
choices.explanation: Events without a matching customer are excluded.

choices.text: Use a CROSS JOIN to expand every customer and count the events.
choices.explanation: This changes the correspondence between events and attributes.

source.label: Apache Spark公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: With normal equality comparison, NULL is not equal to NULL, while a left outer join retains rows from the left side.
learning.concept: Replacing NULL with the same default value or using null-safe equality changes the matching condition.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Maintain the same customer's state across events
prompt: Use Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to update a cumulative value for each customer. The design must use a temporary value based on arrival order and process events for the same customer as one logical state even when work is distributed across multiple workers. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Call keyBy with a random key for each record.
choices.explanation: The same customer's history is distributed across separate states.

choices.text: Call keyBy using only the timestamp.
choices.explanation: State is not tracked per customer.

choices.text: Call keyBy with the customer ID and manage the cumulative value in ValueState for each key.
choices.explanation: The state corresponding to the same customer can be updated continuously.

choices.text: Use one global variable shared by all customers.
choices.explanation: This is not customer-specific state and does not account for distributed execution.

source.label: Apache Flink公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Flink keyed state manages an independent value for each key.
learning.concept: Partition the stream by the business key before the operation that accesses the state.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Read a table as of an audit point using SQL
prompt: An Athena Iceberg table was updated, but the snapshot from before the update is still retained. Reproduce an aggregate as of a specific snapshot ID without rolling back the current data. Which method should be used?

choices.text: Add a past-date tag to the S3 objects and read the current table.
choices.explanation: Tags do not switch the Iceberg reference version.

choices.text: Specify the target snapshot ID with FOR VERSION AS OF and run SELECT.
choices.explanation: The aggregate can be read from the specified version without changing the current pointer.

choices.text: Run VACUUM to delete the old history, then read the current table.
choices.explanation: The history required for the query could be lost.

choices.text: Roll back the current table to the historical point and stop user updates.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to preserve current data.

learning.reason: Iceberg version travel can query a retained snapshot by specifying it.
learning.concept: Reading a historical version is different from changing the table's current state.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Querying changing JSON attributes with SQL later
prompt: The JSON events entering Redshift gradually gain more attributes even within the same event type. You want to store each variable object and query nested values with SQL without adding columns every time. How should you design this?

choices.text: Store the event body in a SUPER column and query the required attributes with PartiQL.
choices.explanation: This reduces the need to change the table definition whenever attributes are added.

choices.text: Normalize all events to the same fixed VARCHAR value.
choices.explanation: This loses the original variable object.

choices.text: Store only the number of event attributes as an INTEGER.
choices.explanation: You cannot read the actual nested values.

choices.text: Manually map every attribute to fixed columns and discard undefined attributes.
choices.explanation: New attributes that you may want to query later cannot be retained.

learning.reason: SUPER stores semi-structured data, and PartiQL can reference its attributes and arrays.
learning.concept: Use a design that preserves variable hierarchies when needed, and distinguish it from creating independent SQL columns with a fixed schema.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Retrieving a range within a hierarchy by key condition
prompt: Orders and another type of history are stored in the same customer partition in DynamoDB. You want to list only the orders for a specific month for a customer without reading and then excluding every other month or type. Which key design should you use?

choices.text: Scan the entire table and exclude the month with FilterExpression.
choices.explanation: This reads unnecessary data before excluding it.

choices.text: Use the customer ID as the partition key and a sort key that concatenates the order type, year and month, and ID.
choices.explanation: The Query scope can be narrowed by the order-type and year-month prefixes.

choices.text: Use only the event type as a partition key shared by all customers.
choices.explanation: The customer-specific range is not separated by the key.

choices.text: Use only the customer ID and a random UUID as keys, then determine the month after retrieval.
choices.explanation: The year and month cannot be used as a sort-key condition.

learning.reason: Putting hierarchical prefixes in a composite sort key allows begins_with to be used as a key condition.
learning.concept: Narrowing a read with a key condition within the same partition is different from filtering data after it has been read.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Using a business ID for search and aggregation without splitting it
prompt: You send events to Amazon OpenSearch Service. The customer_code values contain hyphens and alphanumeric characters, and you need exact-match searches and count aggregations by code. You do not want to split them into full-text search tokens. Which field type should you use?

choices.text: Map customer_code only as text and use the standard analyzer.
choices.explanation: Because the string is split into tokens, this does not meet the requirement to treat the entire business ID as one value.

choices.text: Map customer_code as keyword.
choices.explanation: The entire string can be used as an ID for matching and aggregation.

choices.text: Do not index customer_code and do not issue search conditions for it.
choices.explanation: This does not provide exact-match searches or aggregations using the value.

choices.text: Use an integer type for customer_code and store it after removing hyphens and letters.
choices.explanation: This cannot preserve exact matches for the original string.

learning.reason: keyword indexes a string without analysis and can be used for exact-match searches and aggregations.
learning.concept: Distinguish text, which is analyzed for full-text search, from keyword, which treats the value as a single unit.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Reading regenerable temporary data quickly in the same Availability Zone
prompt: Spark workers run intensively in a single Availability Zone, and high request rates for temporary S3 data have become a bottleneck. All files can be regenerated from the source data, and this storage location does not require redundancy in another Availability Zone. How should you combine storage and compute? Select two.

choices.text: Place the workers in the same Availability Zone as the directory bucket.
choices.explanation: This prioritizes response performance by using a data path within a nearby Availability Zone.

choices.text: Assume that specifying S3 One Zone-IA creates an Express directory bucket.
choices.explanation: One Zone-IA is a different storage class from an Express directory bucket.

choices.text: Store the data in the same format and place the workers in another Region.
choices.explanation: This does not use the condition that the workers be placed in the same Availability Zone.

choices.text: Store the data in S3 Glacier Deep Archive in another Region and read it directly with low latency.
choices.explanation: This tier requires restoration and is unsuitable for frequent, low-latency processing.

choices.text: Place the temporary data in a directory bucket that uses S3 Express One Zone.
choices.explanation: This provides low-latency storage within a single Availability Zone for regenerable data.

learning.reason: S3 Express One Zone can provide low latency when compute is placed in the same Availability Zone as the directory bucket.
learning.concept: Check whether the single-Availability-Zone storage characteristic matches the requirements for regenerable intermediate data.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Restore a Previous Table Definition Without Changing the Data
prompt: A previous version of a Glue Data Catalog table update is stored. Queries can no longer run because the column definition is incorrect, but the S3 objects have not changed. Which information should be used for recovery?

choices.text: Clear the Athena query-result cache and revert to the previous table definition.
choices.explanation: Clearing the result cache does not change the catalog definition.

choices.text: Revert all S3 objects to their previous versions.
choices.explanation: This change affected metadata, so the data does not need to be rolled back.

choices.text: Delete the catalog and recreate it with the same incorrect column definition.
choices.explanation: The definition would still be incorrect.

choices.text: Retrieve the previous TableVersion, verify the required columns and storage descriptor, and update the table definition.
choices.explanation: The correct metadata can be applied without copying the data again.

learning.reason: A previous version of a table's metadata can be retrieved from the catalog's table versions.
learning.concept: S3 object versions and Data Catalog versions of column definitions are independent.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Use an Existing External Metastore from the Catalog
prompt: You operate an available Hive metastore and want a compatible Athena workgroup to reference the same catalog information. You do not want to copy the S3 data or table definitions elsewhere and keep them synchronized. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Copy the S3 files every day and use a Glue crawler to infer the tables again.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to use the metadata without synchronizing it.

choices.text: Register a data source for the supported external Hive metastore, and configure the required connection and data-access permissions.
choices.explanation: The metastore can be referenced without replicating it into another catalog.

choices.text: Re-export the existing Hive data to CSV every day.
choices.explanation: This does not use the original data and existing table definitions as required.

choices.text: Use the S3 URI for Athena query results as the name of the Hive metastore.
choices.explanation: A result location is not a metadata connection.

learning.reason: Athena can connect to a supported external Hive metastore as a data source.
learning.concept: The external metadata connection and access configuration for table data in S3 are separate concerns.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Extract a Table from a Snapshot Without Overwriting the Existing Table
prompt: A table in a provisioned Redshift cluster was updated incorrectly. You have a compatible existing snapshot. You want to create a table in the same database as the current cluster so that you can compare its rows with the rows from the historical point in time, without overwriting the original table. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Delete the current table first and restore the table from the snapshot with the same name.
choices.explanation: This would lose the data needed for comparison with the current table.

choices.text: Recreate the entire cluster and restore tables that are not needed for the comparison as well.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to extract only the required table into the original cluster.

choices.text: Use table restore, specify the snapshot and table, and restore it into the current database with a new table name.
choices.explanation: The table can be compared without replacing the table that is currently in use.

choices.text: Change the sort key of the existing table.
choices.explanation: This does not restore the changes to the rows that you want to undo.

learning.reason: Redshift can restore one table contained in a snapshot under a different name.
learning.concept: Restoring an entire cluster and extracting one table for comparison are separate operations.
