title: Automatically Manage Log Indices Past Their Retention Period
prompt: You create daily log indices in Amazon OpenSearch Service. You want to leave the originals stored long term in S3 unchanged while deleting only the daily indices in the cluster after a defined period. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Set a lifecycle policy on the originals in S3 and assume that OpenSearch will also be deleted automatically.
choices.explanation: A lifecycle policy in another service does not automatically apply to indices.

choices.text: Only specify a recent date in the search criteria.
choices.explanation: The old indices would remain.

choices.text: Reduce the number of OpenSearch nodes.
choices.explanation: This only reduces some capacity and does not control the retention period of daily indices.

choices.text: Apply an ISM policy to the daily log indices and move them to the delete state after the specified elapsed period.
choices.explanation: This applies retention management only on the OpenSearch side.

learning.reason: Index State Management can automate index state transitions and deletion based on age and other conditions.
learning.concept: The search-derived indices are managed separately from retention of the source data.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Clean Up Only Incomplete Transfers on a Deadline
prompt: You operate a process that performs large uploads. Incomplete parts from failed transfers are incurring costs, but you do not want to change the retention period for completed data. Which S3 lifecycle action should you use?

choices.text: Suspend versioning.
choices.explanation: This does not configure an expiration period for incomplete transfers.

choices.text: Transition incomplete parts to S3 Glacier.
choices.explanation: Incomplete parts cannot be transitioned as completed objects.

choices.text: Add an Expiration rule for current objects with the same number of days.
choices.explanation: This could also expire completed data.

choices.text: Specify AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload and set a limit based on the time since initiation.
choices.explanation: This cleans up only incomplete parts without deleting completed data.

learning.reason: AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload terminates incomplete uploads after the specified number of days from initiation.
learning.concept: It is a separate action from expiration of successfully completed objects.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Choose the Temporary Availability Period for Restored Content
prompt: The original data remains in S3 Glacier Deep Archive, but you need to read its contents for only a few days for an audit. Immediate availability is not required, and you do not want to retain the temporary copy after the audit. What should you do?

choices.text: Rewrite the storage class name to Standard and read the content before restoring it.
choices.explanation: Archived data cannot be converted directly in this way.

choices.text: Call GetObject directly and retrieve the content immediately.
choices.explanation: With Deep Archive, the object must be restored before retrieval.

choices.text: Use RestoreObject to specify the retrieval tier and the number of days the restored copy should remain available, then read the object after it is ready.
choices.explanation: This preserves the original archive and allows you to set an expiration period for the temporary copy.

choices.text: Specify the temporary-copy period with a Glacier Vault deletion rule.
choices.explanation: This is not the configuration for an S3 object restoration request.

learning.reason: An archive restoration lets you specify how many days the temporary restored copy remains available.
learning.concept: This differs from permanently changing the original storage class.

category: データストア管理

title: Rename a Logical Column While Preserving History
prompt: Using an Iceberg-compatible engine, you need to rename the logical column amount_cents to value_cents. You must not rewrite the historical Parquet files, and you must be able to read historical values through the new name. What should you do?

choices.text: Change only the name string in the Data Catalog without updating the Iceberg metadata.
choices.explanation: This does not constitute an official schema change for the table.

choices.text: DROP the column and add a column with the new name.
choices.explanation: The new column would have a new field ID and would not match the historical column.

choices.text: Rename the existing field through Iceberg schema evolution.
choices.explanation: The values in historical files remain queryable through the same field ID.

choices.text: Delete all historical files and use the new name.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to preserve history.

source.label: Apache Iceberg公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Iceberg identifies columns by internal field IDs during schema evolution.
learning.concept: Dropping a column and adding another with the same logical role differs from renaming an existing field while preserving its field ID.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Identify Organization-Wide Bucket Usage
prompt: You use S3 across multiple AWS accounts. You need an organization-wide view of the number of bytes used and the number of objects, so that you can find usage imbalances without aggregating each bucket separately. What should you configure?

choices.text: Use CloudWatch Lambda invocation counts as a proxy for bucket usage.
choices.explanation: Some objects are not accessed through Lambda, so this cannot measure stored volume.

choices.text: Collect only CloudTrail management events from one bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not aggregate total object counts or organization-wide storage usage.

choices.text: Create an inventory only for one S3 bucket and treat its values as organization-wide totals.
choices.explanation: Buckets in other accounts are not included in the aggregation.

choices.text: Configure an organization-level S3 Storage Lens dashboard.
choices.explanation: It provides trends across multiple accounts and usage information for individual buckets.

learning.reason: S3 Storage Lens can visualize storage usage at the account and organization levels.
learning.concept: Aggregating storage usage is different from collecting per-request audit logs.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Adjusting physical design based on query usage patterns
prompt: A data model has been newly built in Redshift. For a table whose long-term access pattern is not yet known, which setting lets the service choose distribution and sort options based on the queries that are used?

choices.text: Predefine KEY distribution and a fixed sort key using the same columns for every table.
choices.explanation: This does not delegate both choices to the service.

choices.text: Use AUTO for the distribution style and sort key on the table.
choices.explanation: After collecting sufficient usage information, the service can adjust the physical design.

choices.text: Assume that running VACUUM periodically is enough for the distribution method to be selected automatically.
choices.explanation: Table maintenance and the setting that automatically selects a distribution method are different.

choices.text: Change only the workgroup memory limit.
choices.explanation: This does not delegate the table's physical design choices to the service.

learning.reason: With automatic table optimization, Redshift can adjust distribution and sort design based on AUTO settings.
learning.concept: Choose between explicitly defining a design based on business keys and delegating the choice to automatic tuning.

category: データストア管理

title: Updating two related items together
prompt: In DynamoDB, place the order and inventory items under different keys. Create the order only when inventory remains, and do not allow a state in which only one item is updated. Which API should be used?

choices.text: Combine the conditional inventory decrement and order creation in a single TransactWriteItems operation.
choices.explanation: If the inventory condition is not met, the order is not created either.

choices.text: Combine the two items with BatchWriteItem and allow one of them to succeed.
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee atomicity for all items or the inventory condition.

choices.text: Write the order first and wait for the inventory to decrease through TTL.
choices.explanation: TTL deletes expired items; it does not perform an atomic inventory update.

choices.text: Read the inventory first, then write both items unconditionally in sequence.
choices.explanation: A conflict or an intermediate failure could change only one item.

learning.reason: TransactWriteItems can apply conditional updates to multiple items atomically.
learning.concept: A parallel batch write differs from a transaction that treats success and failure as one unit.

category: データストア管理

title: Handling unpredictable request volumes without preprovisioning capacity
prompt: A DynamoDB ingestion management table is for a new project, and its weekly read and write volumes vary. The adaptation requirements and limits for large spikes have been confirmed in advance. The operations team wants to avoid setting read and write capacity values beforehand and pay according to request volume. Which mode should be used?

choices.text: Use provisioned mode, reserve high capacity continuously, and assume that billing is based only on the number of requests.
choices.explanation: This selects billing based on the capacity reserved.

choices.text: Add only a read cache and leave writes in provisioned mode without specifying capacity.
choices.explanation: This does not eliminate operational management of the table's write capacity.

choices.text: Use provisioned mode with fixed, small read and write capacity values.
choices.explanation: Requests exceeding the specified values could be throttled.

choices.text: Put the table in on-demand capacity mode.
choices.explanation: This allows payment based on requests used without setting provisioned capacity.

learning.reason: On-demand mode does not require read and write capacity to be specified in advance and charges according to the number of requests.
learning.concept: Actual scaling characteristics and account quotas must be checked separately from whether capacity units are configured regularly.

category: データストア管理

title: Providing the planner with information about very different table sizes
prompt: Using the corresponding Athena engine, you run SQL that joins multiple tables. What should you prepare in the catalog, while preserving the source data, so that the planner can use table record counts and value distributions to choose the join order and other decisions?

choices.text: Generate the corresponding column statistics from the table's actual data and store them in the Data Catalog.
choices.explanation: The planner can reference value distributions and other information for the joined columns.

choices.text: Write only “large table” or “small table” in the table comments.
choices.explanation: This does not provide cost-based statistics.

choices.text: Ingest only the S3 bucket access logs.
choices.explanation: This does not provide column NULL counts or value distributions.

choices.text: Change all target columns to VARCHAR.
choices.explanation: This does not create distribution information and could change the meaning of comparisons.

learning.reason: The corresponding service can use column statistics in the Data Catalog to perform cost-based query optimization.
learning.concept: Statistics describe data distributions; permissions and storage formats cannot substitute for them.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Identify the Segment Where CDC Is Delayed
prompt: CloudWatch was checked for DMS change replication. Source-side capture latency is only a few seconds, but target-side latency continues to increase for a long time. Which segment should be investigated first?

choices.text: Rename the DMS task and add both metrics together.
choices.explanation: This would make it impossible to identify where the delay occurs.

choices.text: Suspect only that the source is not producing change logs.
choices.explanation: This does not match the low capture latency and the increase limited to apply latency.

choices.text: Assume that the initial load is complete because the target metric is large.
choices.explanation: The value indicates a delay in applying changes.

choices.text: Investigate application to the target, first checking processing capacity, locks, and apply backlogs.
choices.explanation: Because capture-side delay is small, the increase can be isolated to the downstream processing stage.

learning.reason: CDCLatencySource represents capture-side latency, while CDCLatencyTarget represents the latency until changes are applied to the target.
learning.concept: When capture is keeping up, check target-side application processing and waits.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Do Not Let a Condition Satisfied by Another Row Make an Invalid Row Pass
prompt: You are inspecting contact information with Glue Data Quality. Each row must contain either a phone number or an email address, and values present in different rows must not substitute for one another when evaluating the dataset as a whole. How should the corresponding composite rule be evaluated?

choices.text: Evaluate completeness for each column and combine the results with OR.
choices.explanation: This does not determine whether each row contains at least one of the two values.

choices.text: Require both the phone and email columns to be populated in every row.
choices.explanation: This would reject valid rows that contain only one of the two values.

choices.text: Check only the dataset's RowCount.
choices.explanation: This cannot determine whether individual contacts are missing information.

choices.text: Connect the corresponding completeness rules with OR and set the composite rule evaluation method to ROW.
choices.explanation: This determines whether each row contains at least one of the two values.

learning.reason: Glue Data Quality composite rules can evaluate the corresponding rules at the row level.
learning.concept: Evaluating column-wide rules against each other differs from checking an OR condition within the same row.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Find Disk Spills in a Slow Query at the Step Level
prompt: Only one query in Redshift Serverless is slow. The query ID is known, and you need to determine which join or aggregation execution step exceeded memory and spilled to disk. Which information should you use?

choices.text: Filter SYS_QUERY_DETAIL by query ID and compare spilled_block_local_disk and spilled_block_remote_disk for each step.
choices.explanation: This identifies the processing steps where disk spilling occurred.

choices.text: Look only at the statement cache settings.
choices.explanation: This cannot measure spill volume at each step during execution.

choices.text: Use SYS_LOAD_ERROR_DETAIL to look for type errors during an S3 load.
choices.explanation: This view does not show spill activity for query steps.

choices.text: Use SYS_QUERY_HISTORY to obtain only the total query duration.
choices.explanation: This does not show which individual step spilled to disk.

learning.reason: SYS_QUERY_DETAIL contains query-step attributes and the number of blocks spilled to local and remote storage.
learning.concept: Move from the total query duration to an analysis that identifies the step where spilling occurred.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Inspect the Planned Read Range Before Scanning Real Data
prompt: Before changing a production Athena SQL statement, you want to confirm that selecting date partitions is included in the plan. You want to avoid actually executing the SQL and scanning the input data. What should you use?

choices.text: SELECT from the target table and inspect only the dates returned.
choices.explanation: This is not a method for inspecting the plan without executing the query.

choices.text: Change only the workgroup alarm for the number of scanned rows.
choices.explanation: This does not show which partitions the current SQL selects.

choices.text: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE and scan the production input.
choices.explanation: This executes the target query and scans the input, contrary to the requirement.

choices.text: Run EXPLAIN for the target SQL and inspect the partition predicates in the plan.
choices.explanation: This lets you inspect the planned filtering without scanning the input data.

learning.reason: EXPLAIN displays the execution plan. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the target query and also provides runtime statistics.
learning.concept: When diagnosing a query, distinguish planned scanning from runtime consumption.

title: Retaining Pre-Transformation Input for Reprocessing
prompt: Data Firehose formats records with Lambda and delivers them to the corresponding destinations. To prepare for future corrections, you want to retain the pre-transformation input in a separate S3 location, including records that were transformed successfully as well as those that failed. What should you configure?

choices.text: Enable S3 backup for source records in the delivery stream.
choices.explanation: This preserves the input so the transformation can be rerun later.

choices.text: Back up data from the post-transformation destination and treat it as identical to the original.
choices.explanation: Information discarded during transformation may not be recoverable.

choices.text: Return ProcessingFailed for every Lambda response.
choices.explanation: This stops successful delivery and therefore violates the requirement.

choices.text: Save only the transformation-failure prefix.
choices.explanation: The original input for successful records is not sent there.

learning.reason: The relevant Firehose delivery configuration can back up records before transformation to S3.
learning.concept: Distinguish the path for recording transformation failures from a configuration that stores every original record.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Investigating Why a DAG Is Not Created at Its Scheduled Time
prompt: The daily MWAA DAG Run for the scheduled time is not being created at all. The target task has never started. Before investigating communication with the target service, which logs about DAG management and scheduling should you examine?

choices.text: Check only the Athena SQL execution history.
choices.explanation: It does not show whether the DAG Run was created.

choices.text: Look only for the Task log of the task that has not started.
choices.explanation: The problem occurs before task execution.

choices.text: Use only the Airflow Web Server log to look for the data-processing completion result.
choices.explanation: What is needed here is the scheduler-side planning information.

choices.text: Check the Airflow Scheduler log for the time and schedule evaluation.
choices.explanation: It provides information about the stage at which the DAG Run is not being created.

learning.reason: MWAA can send Airflow logs for components such as tasks and the scheduler to CloudWatch.
learning.concept: When a task has not started, prioritize logs from the planning and evaluation side.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Periodically Checking Metadata for a Large Number of Objects
prompt: There are hundreds of millions of objects in S3. You want to analyze each object's encryption status and storage class daily, but you do not want a job to list every object and repeatedly issue an individual HEAD request. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Run HeadObject only on a single S3 object.
choices.explanation: This cannot obtain information for the entire bucket.

choices.text: Create an S3 Inventory containing the required metadata and query its output with Athena.
choices.explanation: This enables object-level analysis without maintaining custom full-inventory query processing.

choices.text: Use only S3 event notifications to obtain the metadata of all existing objects from the first run.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a periodic inventory of all data that already exists.

choices.text: Use S3 Storage Lens to view only the bucket's total capacity.
choices.explanation: The aggregate does not provide the encryption status of each object.

learning.reason: S3 Inventory can store periodic reports containing the metadata fields you specify.
learning.concept: Distinguish aggregate information such as total bucket bytes from records for individual objects.

title: Controlling Load After Write Rejections During Ingestion
prompt: During log delivery to OpenSearch, 429 responses are increasing, and the rejection metric for the corresponding write queue is also rising. The network and authorization are functioning normally. After recording input-side concurrency and retries, how should you mitigate the issue first?

choices.text: Reduce the bulk request size and limit concurrency, then apply backoff to rejected operations.
choices.explanation: This reduces pressure on the write queue while allowing retries.

choices.text: Only shorten the retention period for the S3 archive.
choices.explanation: This does not relieve congestion in the OpenSearch write queue.

choices.text: Only update the authentication token for the search index.
choices.explanation: This does not mitigate load-related rejections.

choices.text: Resend all rejected batches simultaneously.
choices.explanation: This increases the write load while the system is congested.

learning.reason: When the available write capacity is exhausted, requests are rejected, so the sending parallelism and retry behavior must be adjusted.
learning.concept: Combine capacity relief with input control so that simultaneous resubmission does not increase the same load.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Queue jobs that cannot start temporarily because of the concurrency limit
prompt: Multiple AWS Glue jobs start during the same period. The Spark batch should start when concurrency capacity becomes available, and the caller should not have to maintain its own retry timer. What should be configured in the execution method?

choices.text: Increase the number of read replicas for the database.
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to the execution capacity for Glue jobs.

choices.text: Only increase the timeout for processing that is already running.
choices.explanation: This does not configure the request to wait until execution can begin.

choices.text: Enable job queuing for the target job run.
choices.explanation: Glue can handle waiting to start when the relevant concurrency limit has been reached.

choices.text: When no capacity is available, add the same number of start requests concurrently.
choices.explanation: This does not increase the concurrency limit or manage the waiting period.

learning.reason: The Glue job execution queue can hold runs that cannot start because of temporary resource constraints.
learning.concept: This is a different control from rerunning a job after it fails during execution.

category: データ運用とサポート

choices.explanation: This does not provide stage-level history.

learning.reason: The EMR persistent application UI allows the Spark History Server to be used after termination when the supported logs are available.
learning.concept: The access path after termination differs from the screen used to connect to a running cluster.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Automatically notify operations about quality-rule violations
prompt: A Glue Data Quality run completes without a failure condition, but the rule evaluation produces a number of failures. You want to send an SNS notification based on the evaluation result without waiting for a job-failure alert. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Publish the evaluation result, and configure an EventBridge rule to process the failure condition and send an SNS notification.

learning.reason: Glue Data Quality evaluation results and completion events can be handled with EventBridge.
learning.concept: The state of the job execution itself differs from the quality state of the evaluated data.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Run the same operation on many targets and track the results
prompt: You need to perform a lightweight metadata inspection with an existing Lambda function on a large number of approved S3 objects. choices.text: Use an S3 Batch Operations job with a manifest to invoke Lambda and produce a completion report.

choices.text: Specify the Lambda function name in the bucket lifecycle configuration.

choices.text: Do not provide a list; have a single Lambda function scan the entire bucket.

choices.text: Add only notifications for object-creation events.
choices.explanation: This does not select and process the complete set of objects that already exist.

learning.reason: S3 Batch Operations can invoke a supported Lambda function for objects specified in a manifest and produce a completion report.
learning.concept: Events for newly arriving objects differ from processing a finalized, large list of existing objects.

category: データ運用とサポート

prompt: Glue logs exist in multiple accounts. The operations team must analyze logs across accounts from a central CloudWatch in the same Region without copying existing logs to another destination. Which two components should be combined on the monitoring-account side and the source-account side? Select two.

choices.text: From the source account, create a link to the sink that shares the required logs.
choices.explanation: This allows the target logs to be searched from the monitoring account.

choices.explanation: This does not provide a continuously queryable central operation.

choices.text: Create log groups with the same names in the central account.

choices.text: Create an observability sink for the monitoring account.
choices.explanation: This provides the central destination that accepts links from source accounts.

choices.text: Export the logs to S3 on the source side and copy them to another account.
choices.explanation: This creates a new stored copy even though the requirement is only to provide access.

learning.reason: CloudWatch cross-account observability allows a central monitoring account to access shared logs and other observability data.
learning.concept: Distinguish sharing access to data from sending logs elsewhere to create a copy.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Receive forecast notifications before monthly analysis costs exceed the threshold

choices.text: Create a cost budget filtered to the target service and configure a notification threshold for the monthly forecasted amount.

choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for an advance forecast notification.

learning.concept: Forecast cost notifications and temporary scan limits for individual queries control different things.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス

title: Replicate KMS-protected objects to another Region
prompt: S3 CRR replicates input encrypted with SSE-S3, but input encrypted with SSE-KMS in the source must also be included. A dedicated KMS key is available in the destination. What should be configured for replication? Select two.

choices.text: Specify in the destination a key identifier that exists only in the source Region.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for a key usable in the destination.

choices.text: Specify the KMS key in the destination Region and grant the replication role the permissions required to decrypt at the source and encrypt at the destination.
choices.explanation: The role can perform the required cryptographic operations for both the source and destination.

choices.text: Add only decrypt permission to the destination key and omit encrypt permission.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス

title: Reduce KMS requests while preserving the encryption method
prompt: A bucket using SSE-KMS receives a large number of small objects. The team wants to reduce the cost of KMS requests without changing the symmetric KMS key in use. Which S3-side setting should be applied to new writes?

choices.text: Create unencrypted objects and overwrite the same keys.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the requirement to protect objects with KMS.

choices.text: Rotate the KMS key's key material at a short interval.
choices.explanation: The key-update interval does not reduce the per-object call frequency.

choices.text: Replace the KMS key in use with SSE-S3.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve use of the specified KMS key.

choices.text: Enable S3 Bucket Key for the SSE-KMS configuration.
choices.explanation: This reduces requests to KMS while preserving the bucket's selected encryption method.

learning.reason: S3 Bucket Key can reduce KMS requests made when encrypting objects with SSE-KMS.
learning.concept: Reduce the frequency of individual KMS calls while preserving data encryption.

title: Control Which Rows Are Returned by Department in the Same Table
prompt: A Redshift customer table is managed centrally. Based on an analyst’s role, return only the rows for the departments that analyst may view while preserving SELECT access to the same table. Which feature should be used without copying the data for each department?

choices.text: Set a retention period in the S3 output bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not control which rows an internal Redshift table returns.

choices.text: Configure only dynamic data masking for the department column.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent rows from other departments from being included in the result.

choices.text: Associate a row-level security policy containing department conditions with the roles, and enable RLS on the table.
choices.explanation: The shared table can return only the rows that satisfy the applicable conditions.

choices.text: Ask each analyst to add a WHERE clause voluntarily.
choices.explanation: An analyst could read rows from other departments with SQL that omits the condition.

learning.reason: Redshift row-level security filters the rows available to users or roles according to policies.
learning.concept: Masking column values at display time does not prevent access to the rows belonging to other departments.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス

title: Apply a Common Storage Policy to Analysis Results
prompt: For all analysts in the same Athena workgroup, enforce result storage under an administrative S3 prefix using a specified KMS key. Even if the SDK supplies a different output location, the administrative settings must be used. Which two actions should be combined? Select two.

choices.text: Configure encryption only for the input bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not specify the location or encryption operation for the output result files.

choices.text: Specify an S3 URI in the query data usage limits.
choices.explanation: Managing scan volume is separate from configuring the result location.

choices.text: Enable the workgroup setting to override client-side settings.
choices.explanation: The administrative settings can take precedence even when a client specifies a result location.

choices.text: Configure the specified S3 output location and KMS encryption in the workgroup.
choices.explanation: This defines the administrative storage location and encryption requirements.

choices.text: Write the recommended S3 path in the SDK usage example, but disable workgroup overrides.
choices.explanation: A client that supplies different settings cannot be forced to use the recommended configuration.

learning.reason: An Athena workgroup can override client-specified settings to standardize the result location and encryption.
learning.concept: Encrypting only the input data does not determine where each query's result files are stored.

title: Keep JDBC Credentials Out of Job Code
prompt: A Glue JDBC connection requires database credentials. The password must not be placed in the script or job arguments; only the authorized execution role should retrieve the managed credentials. Which two actions should be combined? Select two.

choices.text: Put the plaintext password in the job arguments instead of the secret ID.
choices.explanation: The secret value remains in the arguments even if it is moved out of the source code.

choices.text: Reference a Secrets Manager secret containing the database credentials from the Glue connection.
choices.explanation: The secret value does not need to be written in the job source.

choices.text: Assume that writing only the Glue service name in a tag grants retrieval permission.
choices.explanation: This does not grant the IAM permission required to retrieve the secret.

choices.text: Make the secret public to all users regardless of the target.
choices.explanation: Access cannot be restricted to the specified execution role.

choices.text: Grant the execution role permission to retrieve the target secret and, when applicable, permission to decrypt with KMS.
choices.explanation: The secret can be used only for the required connection with the necessary permissions.

learning.reason: A Glue connection can reference a Secrets Manager secret.
learning.concept: Separate where the secret value is stored from the access permissions granted to the execution role.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Migrate Per User While Preserving Existing Access
prompt: Several production Glue Data Catalog tables are currently used by existing jobs through the traditional IAM model. Only new analysis roles should be controlled by Lake Formation for now; migration of the existing jobs will occur later. Which migration method should be used?

choices.text: Immediately remove the existing IAM-compatible setting from all tables and grant permissions only to the new roles.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement that existing jobs continue to work.

choices.text: Register the target S3 location in hybrid mode, grant Lake Formation permissions to the new roles for the target resources, and opt those roles in.
choices.explanation: Control can be applied incrementally to the selected roles.

choices.text: Copy all data to another bucket and stop the old bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to preserve existing access.

choices.text: Deregister the resources from Lake Formation and operate using IAM only.
choices.explanation: This does not apply Lake Formation controls to the new roles.

learning.reason: Hybrid access mode allows selected principals to be opted in to Lake Formation management for a resource.
learning.concept: This migration method does not require all existing IAM users to switch at once.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス

title: Managing team-specific entry points to the same bucket
prompt: Several application groups use the same S3 bucket. You need to manage different access policies and named entry points for each team prefix without listing all application requirements in one bucket policy. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Set each team’s IAM role in an S3 lifecycle filter.
choices.explanation: Lifecycle rules do not define access permissions.

choices.text: Change the bucket name to the same value for each team.
choices.explanation: This does not create multiple access entry points for a shared bucket.

choices.text: Create an S3 Access Point for each team, and configure delegation in the bucket and a dedicated policy for each Access Point.
choices.explanation: This keeps one shared bucket while managing conditions at the entry-point level.

choices.text: Copy the results to the same prefix and make them public without a policy.
choices.explanation: This cannot enforce the required access conditions.

learning.reason: S3 Access Points provide named entry points and allow separate access policies.
learning.concept: Access is evaluated using consistent delegation from the bucket and permissions from the Access Point.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Protecting data locations and column definitions at rest
prompt: An audit requires metadata such as the databases, tables, and partitions in Glue Data Catalog to be protected with an organization-designated KMS key. Encryption of the S3 data itself is already complete. What else should you configure?

choices.text: Configure only encryption for Athena query results.
choices.explanation: This protects result files and does not apply to the catalog.

choices.text: Configure metadata encryption for Glue Data Catalog with the organization-designated KMS key, and provide the permissions required by the method.
choices.explanation: Catalog metadata can be encrypted separately from the protection of the S3 data itself.

choices.text: Change only the default encryption of the data bucket to use the same key.
choices.explanation: This does not change the metadata encryption settings for Data Catalog.

choices.text: Configure only encryption for Glue job bookmarks.
choices.explanation: This protects job progress state and does not cover all catalog metadata.

learning.reason: The Glue Data Catalog encryption setting applies to catalog metadata.
learning.concept: Data files, job logs, and catalog metadata have different protection scopes.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Reducing the transfer of direct identifiers to analytical data
prompt: A Glue DataBrew preparation pipeline contains datasets with identifiers such as email addresses. The restricted S3 source data must be retained, but derived output for analytics must not directly identify individuals. Analysts do not have permission to access the source data. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Only detect identifiers in a profile and leave the plaintext derived output unchanged.
choices.explanation: Detection does not protect the contents of the source data or its copies.

choices.text: Encrypt the analytical output in S3 and allow analysts to decrypt all of it.
choices.explanation: Direct identifiers remain in the analytical data after decryption.

choices.text: Apply a recipe that deletes or masks the necessary identifiers, and write the result as separate data under an analytical prefix.
choices.explanation: This reduces direct identifiers in the data analysts can read while retaining the source data.

choices.text: Grant analysts access to the source data and ask them to hide it in the tool’s display.
choices.explanation: Analysts could still view direct identifiers if they retrieve the data individually.

learning.reason: DataBrew recipes can specify transformations that mask or delete PII columns.
learning.concept: Transform derived data before delivery while separately preserving the S3 permissions for the source data.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス

title: Sharing the latest tables with another account without replication
prompt: In a compatible Redshift configuration, an analysis team in another AWS account must read specified tables. Avoid delays from periodic exports and avoid copying the data, while allowing the consumer to use its own compute resources. Which method should you use?

choices.text: Share a snapshot daily.
choices.explanation: This does not directly expose changes made between snapshots.

choices.text: Periodically UNLOAD to S3 and have the consumer use COPY.
choices.explanation: Replication and the delay between transfers remain.

choices.text: Create a data share containing the required tables, authorize the consumer, and have the consumer use the shared database.
choices.explanation: The consumer can access updates from the provider without creating extract files.

choices.text: Share the provider cluster’s credentials with all analysts.
choices.explanation: This does not use the consumer’s compute resources or isolate sharing to the required objects.

learning.reason: With Redshift data sharing, the consumer can query the same data through a share of the specified objects.
learning.concept: The consumer’s compute resources can be separated from the data store managed by the provider.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Separating Access to Reused Query Results
prompt: Lake Formation manages the input tables, and different departments see different rows or columns in Athena. Prevent users in one department from directly retrieving another department’s S3 result files. What should be controlled?

choices.text: Encrypt the input with the same KMS key and leave all departments able to read the same result path.
choices.explanation: This does not impose department-specific read restrictions on the output files.

choices.text: Treat the Lake Formation filter attached to the input table as also applying to GetObject for the output files.
choices.explanation: Permissions on the input table do not automatically apply to result files in S3.

choices.text: Only set the query-result retention period to one week.
choices.explanation: This does not restrict who can directly retrieve the files while they are stored.

choices.text: Use managed workgroups and result locations for each department, and protect the result paths with IAM and S3 policies.
choices.explanation: This can limit the ability to directly retrieve another department’s output from S3.

learning.reason: Lake Formation permissions on input data do not by themselves control Athena’s S3 result locations.
learning.concept: Query permissions and direct reads of result files are separate access paths.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス

title: Owning Objects Created by Another Account
prompt: A job in another account writes to an S3 bucket used as a shared data lake. The bucket-owning account must own all objects, and operations will not grant object-level ACLs. The writer can be configured not to send any ACL. Which mode should be used?

choices.text: Set Object Ownership to Bucket owner enforced, and grant write permissions through the bucket policy and IAM.
choices.explanation: The bucket owner can manage objects created by another account without relying on ACLs.

choices.text: Enable bucket encryption and use an encryption key owned by the bucket owner.
choices.explanation: The owner of the key and the owner of an S3 object are not determined by the same setting.

choices.text: Use Bucket owner preferred and have the writer omit the ACL it sends.
choices.explanation: This does not ensure the conditions required for the bucket owner to own objects for all writes.

choices.text: Keep Object writer and grant read permission only to the bucket-owning account.
choices.explanation: Granting read permission does not change the object owner.

learning.reason: With Bucket owner enforced, ACLs are disabled and the bucket owner owns the objects.
learning.concept: Grant the policies required for writes and configure clients not to send unsupported ACLs.

title: Parallelizing Ingestion While Preserving Order for the Same Key
prompt: Data is sent from Kinesis Data Streams to Lambda. Record order for each user must be preserved, but each shard contains many keys and latency increases when only one execution is used. What should be adjusted in the event source mapping?

choices.text: Only increase the Lambda timeout.
choices.explanation: This does not change the parallelism of batches processed within a shard.

choices.text: Keep the existing keys and increase the event source mapping’s ParallelizationFactor.
choices.explanation: This allows different keys to be processed concurrently while preserving order within each key.

choices.text: Lengthen the downstream write buffer and assume that concurrency within the shard will increase.
choices.explanation: This does not affect the number of concurrent executions controlled by polling settings.

choices.text: Issue a new random key for every event.
choices.explanation: The key for the same user would change, so the ordering requirement would not be met.

learning.reason: Increasing ParallelizationFactor allows multiple batches in a shard to be processed in parallel while preserving order per partition key.
learning.concept: Write-time distribution and consumer parallelism within a shard are separate concerns.

title: Retrieving Aggregation Results Without a Persistent Database Connection
prompt: A short-running pipeline starts a SELECT statement on a Redshift cluster that supports the Data API. It must verify completion without keeping a connection open and retrieve all results, which are returned in JSON pages. Which two actions should be combined? Select two.

choices.text: Read the results with GetStatementResult and retrieve subsequent pages as long as NextToken is present.
choices.explanation: This makes all rows available even when the results do not fit in one response.

choices.text: Use the ExecuteStatement acknowledgment response as the complete result for all rows.
choices.explanation: The acknowledgment response does not contain the SELECT results.

choices.text: Skip checking SQL completion and issue every SELECT again from the beginning every few seconds.
choices.explanation: This repeats the processing instead of checking the result of the original execution.

choices.text: Use the ID returned by ExecuteStatement and confirm successful completion with DescribeStatement.
choices.explanation: This avoids mistaking asynchronous SQL acceptance for completion.

choices.text: Issue a separate SQL statement unconditionally for each page.
choices.explanation: This does not page consistently through the result set of one execution.

learning.reason: The Data API returns a statement ID, which can be used to retrieve execution status and results through separate operations.
learning.concept: Distinguish acknowledgment from completion and follow pagination when more results exist.

title: Passing Data Between Steps in the Same Run
prompt: A Glue workflow is started multiple times concurrently, and each run has a different batch ID required by the first job. Downstream jobs must use the batch ID from the same run without allowing another run to overwrite it. Where should the value be stored?

choices.text: Rewrite the Glue job's default arguments for each run.
choices.explanation: The job configuration is shared, so runs can conflict with one another.

choices.text: Update the workflow run properties upstream, and read the properties for the same run ID downstream.
choices.explanation: This keeps the value separate from values in concurrently running executions.

choices.text: Append the date to the downstream job name and treat the value as retrieved.
choices.explanation: Multiple runs on the same day would not have individually stored values.

choices.text: Have every run write its batch ID to the same single S3 key.
choices.explanation: The value written by each run cannot be isolated.

learning.reason: Glue workflow run properties are associated with a workflow run ID.
learning.concept: Distinguish fixed default values shared by all runs from values passed between steps within an individual run.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Publish After Both Transformations Finish
prompt: Two Glue jobs for customer data and transaction data are started from the same trigger chain. The publishing job should start only when both jobs succeed. Because their completion times vary, a fixed wait must not be used. What should be specified?

choices.text: Use a condition based on either job reaching SUCCEEDED.
choices.explanation: The publishing job could start while only one input is available.

choices.text: Connect a conditional trigger to the publishing job that monitors both jobs reaching SUCCEEDED with an AND condition.
choices.explanation: The workflow proceeds only after both required inputs are ready in the same flow.

choices.text: Check only the starting state of the job most likely to finish first.
choices.explanation: The result of the other job is not evaluated.

choices.text: Start publishing unconditionally 15 minutes after the scheduled time each time.
choices.explanation: This cannot account for variable run times or failures.

learning.reason: Glue conditional triggers can evaluate whether monitored jobs have reached specified states by using AND or OR logic.
learning.concept: Distinguish one job having finished from both required inputs being available.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Prevent Concurrent Requests from Multiple DAGs from Concentrating
prompt: Multiple DAGs running on MWAA use an external data API that permits up to 10 simultaneous connections. Other tasks are not subject to this limit. How can only the target tasks be controlled collectively across DAGs?

choices.text: Set the external API retry count to a maximum of 10.
choices.explanation: The retry count does not limit the number of simultaneous connections.

choices.text: Set a concurrency limit of 10 separately in each DAG.
choices.explanation: Each DAG could still run 10 requests, exceeding the cross-DAG limit.

choices.text: Assign all tasks to a single worker only.
choices.explanation: This also constrains tasks unrelated to the API and does not isolate the required target tasks.

choices.text: Define a shared pool with 10 slots and assign each task that connects to the API to it.
choices.explanation: The limit can be applied across all target tasks even when multiple DAGs run concurrently.

learning.reason: Airflow pools limit the available slots for tasks assigned to the same pool.
learning.concept: Use DAG-specific concurrency separately from a cross-DAG limit for an external resource.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Prevent Excess Concurrency from Saturating a Downstream System
prompt: A Lambda function transforms batch input and uses one connection slot in a downstream database per execution. The maximum concurrent executions assigned to this function must be fixed at 25. Cold-start mitigation is handled separately. Which setting should be used?

choices.text: Set the log retention period to 25 days.
choices.explanation: This does not control concurrent database connections.

choices.text: Set the function timeout to 25 seconds.
choices.explanation: This controls the duration of one invocation but does not determine the number of concurrent executions.

choices.text: Set only the provisioned concurrency to 25.
choices.explanation: This determines the number of initialized environments but does not, by itself, set the total concurrency limit.

choices.text: Set this function's reserved concurrency to 25.
choices.explanation: The function's concurrency cannot exceed this limit.

learning.reason: Reserved concurrency can both reserve capacity for a function and serve as its concurrency limit.
learning.concept: Provisioned concurrency prepares initialized environments but does not establish the same maximum concurrency by itself.

title: Parallelize JDBC Reads at the Input
prompt: In a partitionable Glue JDBC ingestion job, the columns and rows to transfer are already limited to the necessary minimum. choices.text: Select the uniformly distributed column as the hashfield and set hashpartitions according to the number of connections allowed.
choices.explanation: This distributes the load across multiple JDBC reads.

choices.text: Collect all individual query results in a single driver first.
choices.explanation: Input processing would not be parallelized.

choices.text: Only increase the number of DataFrame partitions after reading.
choices.explanation: This occurs after ingestion from the source has finished.

choices.text: Use the uniformly distributed column only in the prefix of the final S3 output.
choices.explanation: This does not change the parallel JDBC read settings.

learning.reason: Glue can split JDBC input using a hash expression and read the partitions in parallel.
learning.concept: Optimizing the total range to read and configuring parallel processing of that range are different tasks.

title: Reflect Operational Database Changes in Analytics Through Managed Integration

choices.explanation: Changes can be followed without the application running a separate continuous synchronization process.

choices.text: Manually export a CSV once a week and load it into Redshift.
choices.explanation: Operational work would remain necessary for continuous updates.

choices.text: Run all analytical SQL on the Aurora writer instance.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to use Redshift as the analytics destination.

choices.explanation: This does not continuously reflect updates in the analytics destination.

learning.reason: A compatible Aurora zero-ETL integration can replicate change data to Redshift.
learning.concept: Verify support for the integration source and the reference database on Redshift.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Align Columns by Name When Their Order Differs
prompt: Two Spark input datasets have the common columns in different orders, and only one contains an optional source_region column. You want to retain every row and set that column to NULL in the input where it is missing. Which method should you use?

choices.text: Use an inner join to retain only rows whose common-column values match.
choices.explanation: This does not retain all rows.

choices.text: Delete all columns that are not common to both inputs.
choices.explanation: This would discard source_region where it is available.

choices.text: Use unionByName with allowMissingColumns enabled.
choices.explanation: This aligns columns even when their order differs and fills missing columns with NULL.

choices.text: Use the ordinary position-based union without checking the order.

learning.reason: unionByName matches columns by name rather than position, and allowMissingColumns treats missing columns as NULL.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Calculate the Change from the Previous Record
prompt: You query consecutive measurements for each device with Athena engine version 3. choices.text: Aggregate COUNT for each device.
choices.explanation: This cannot retain both the previous row's value and the measurement details.

choices.text: Combine all devices and calculate the difference between MAX and MIN.
choices.explanation: This does not produce the difference from the previous measurement for each record.

choices.text: Partition by device ID, order by time and sequence number, use LAG, and calculate the difference from the current value.

choices.text: Apply LAG to all data without ORDER BY.
choices.explanation: The time-series order within each device would not be defined.

learning.reason: Window functions can define an order within each group and reference the value from an adjacent row.
learning.concept: Aggregating rows into one result differs from retaining detail rows and adding a comparison value.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Correctly ingesting quoted multiline input
prompt: A Python function on Lambda reads CSV data. The header column names should be used, and quoted descriptions contain commas and line breaks. The entire string should be structured before processing. Which reading approach should be used?

choices.text: Remove commas from the entire input and pass it to a JSON parser.
choices.explanation: This loses the distinction between data values and CSV structure.

choices.text: Remove the description column and split the string unconditionally.

choices.text: Change the S3 storage class and assume that inference starts automatically.

prompt: An AWS SAM project manages a Lambda transformation with Python dependencies. The dependencies must be included in an artifact built by CI, and the transformation must be deployed reproducibly from the same template. Do not manually place a ZIP file in the console. What should be done?

category: データの取り込みと変換
