title: Handling large reference data as shared Lambda files
prompt: A Lambda transformation reads a multi-GB reference table from an existing library using a POSIX file path. The data cannot be bundled in the ZIP, and the same data should not be fully copied into each environment's temporary directory every time. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Put only the S3 bucket name in an environment variable and open the data transparently by path.
choices.explanation: An S3 object is not automatically mounted as a POSIX path for the existing library.

choices.text: Copy all the data to /tmp on every cold start.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid per-environment duplication.

choices.text: Embed the multi-GB files in environment variables.
choices.explanation: Environment variables do not provide shared POSIX files.

choices.text: Store the reference data in EFS, connect Lambda to the appropriate VPC, and mount an EFS access point.
choices.explanation: The data can be accessed through a shared path without including it in the ZIP.

learning.reason: Lambda can mount a shared file system through a compatible EFS access point.
learning.concept: Provide the VPC connection, connectivity to the mount targets, and execution-role permissions required to access the data as files.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Delivering by Department Through the Same Notification Path
prompt: All locations' arrival notifications are sent to one SNS topic. All notifications should go to the operations queue, while each regional queue should receive only notifications with its corresponding region attribute. Which approach avoids requiring the publisher to manage destinations for each queue?

choices.text: Add a region-attribute filter to each regional queue subscription and leave the operations queue subscription without a filter.
choices.explanation: The message is published once, while the delivery conditions can differ for each queue.

choices.text: Have the same sender call SendMessage for each regional queue and publish to SNS every time.
choices.explanation: The publisher still has to manage the destinations.

choices.text: Replace the operations and regional queues with one queue and have each department compete for messages.
choices.explanation: The full set and the subsets cannot be received separately.

choices.text: Set one regional filter for the entire topic.
choices.explanation: This would also restrict the operations queue, which must receive all notifications.

learning.reason: SNS subscription filter policies select delivery targets for each subscription based on message attributes or message bodies.
learning.concept: Distinguish the permission to publish to the topic from the notifications delivered to each subscription.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Ingesting Events in Order Within Each Business Key
prompt: Events for each customer must remain in order within that customer. No ordering is required between customers, and independent groups should be processed in parallel. What should be specified for the SQS queue and sender? Select two.

choices.text: Use the same customer ID as the MessageGroupId for all events belonging to that customer.
choices.explanation: This preserves ordering per customer while allowing parallel processing between customers.

choices.text: Use an SQS FIFO queue for input that requires ordering guarantees.
choices.explanation: This enables ordered processing within each group.

choices.text: Treat the receive order of a standard queue as the customer's send order.
choices.explanation: A standard queue does not provide the required ordering guarantee.

choices.text: Use one common group ID for all customers in the queue.
choices.explanation: This would prevent parallel processing between customers.

choices.text: Assign a different random group ID to every message.
choices.explanation: The order of messages for the same customer could not be managed within one group.

learning.reason: SQS FIFO preserves order within a message group and supports concurrent processing of different groups.
learning.concept: The message deduplication ID and the message group that determines ordering serve different purposes.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Preventing Invalid Input from Triggering a Downstream Lookup
prompt: A REST API in API Gateway uses Lambda to look up data. If the request body does not contain the required datasetId, the API must return a 4xx response immediately after the client submits the request and must not invoke Lambda. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Enable only stage throttling.
choices.explanation: This controls the request rate but does not check whether the body contains the required field.

choices.text: Configure a request model that requires datasetId and enable request-body validation for the corresponding method.
choices.explanation: Requests with an invalid format can be rejected before Lambda is invoked.

choices.text: Validate the required value only in the Lambda code.
choices.explanation: Although the request can be rejected, Lambda is still invoked, which does not meet the requirement.

choices.text: Only define required datasetId in the API Gateway response model.
choices.explanation: A response model defines the response and does not configure pre-validation of the incoming body.

learning.reason: Method request validation for a REST API checks the request body against a model for the applicable content type and rejects nonconforming requests.
learning.concept: Validating the input before the integration prevents invalid input from starting the lookup process.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Including a Large Native-Dependency Utility in Lambda
prompt: Lambda transforms data one item at a time. The required native dependencies do not fit within the ZIP limits but do fit within the limits for the applicable container image. All executions must use the same dependencies. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Create a Lambda-compatible image that includes the dependencies, register it in ECR in the same Region, and deploy it to an image-type function.
choices.explanation: Each execution can run from the same deployed image.

choices.text: Move the dependencies that exceed the ZIP limit into a Lambda layer and treat the combined unzipped limit as no longer applicable.
choices.explanation: For ZIP-based functions, the combined limit for the function and layers still applies.

choices.text: Download the latest binaries from the internet during every execution.
choices.explanation: Downloads can fail and versions can differ, so the same dependencies are not guaranteed.

choices.text: Assume that placing the container in ECR is sufficient for an existing ZIP-based function to use it automatically.
choices.explanation: The function's package type and deployment must be configured.

learning.reason: Lambda can deploy compatible container images from Amazon ECR.
learning.concept: Include verified runtime dependencies in the artifact instead of downloading them from an external repository during every execution.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Distribute common rule changes to all stream processing tasks
prompt: Orders partitioned by customer key are processed in Flink. The decision rules are small and updated occasionally, and the same rule content must be distributed to all customer-processing tasks. The external service must not be queried for every order, and the rules and orders must be handled as two inputs. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Broadcast the rule stream and connect it to the customer-keyed order stream.
choices.explanation: Each task can refer to the shared rule state.

choices.text: Assign all orders the same key, eliminate parallelism, and place the rules in a single variable.
choices.explanation: This loses the operational benefits of key-based distributed processing.

choices.text: Update the decision rules using only the watermarks of the order stream.
choices.explanation: Information representing time progress does not distribute the rule content.

choices.text: Assign the rules only to one arbitrary customer key.
choices.explanation: The rules do not reach tasks processing the other keys.

source.label: Apache Flink公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Broadcast state can distribute a small rule stream to all parallel operators.
learning.concept: Separate the customer keys used for events from the method used to distribute rules shared by the entire stream.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Advance downstream processing as each corresponding transformation unit finishes
prompt: Two same-sized AWS Batch array jobs perform transformation and publication for each partition. A child of the publication array must proceed only when the transformation child with the same index succeeds, without waiting for transformations in other partitions. Which dependency type should be used?

choices.text: Make the dependency always wait for the entire preceding array to complete.
choices.explanation: This also waits for the other partitions.

choices.text: Start the publication array without any dependency condition.
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee completion of the corresponding transformation.

choices.text: Make one array SEQUENTIAL and expect it to wait for the corresponding child in the other array.
choices.explanation: Execution order within one array differs from a corresponding dependency between two arrays.

choices.text: Set the publication array to depend on the transformation array using N_TO_N.
choices.explanation: Success of the child with the corresponding index becomes the condition for starting the downstream child.

learning.reason: An N_TO_N dependency makes each child job wait for the child with the corresponding array index.
learning.concept: This differs from waiting for the entire transformation array because the condition for starting parallel processing is different.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Prevent stale unprocessable records from blocking a shard during retries
prompt: A single unprocessable record blocks the same shard in a Lambda function that reads from Kinesis. There is a business limit on acceptable record age, and a destination is needed for investigating discarded failures. Which two settings should be combined? Select two.

choices.text: Only intentionally shorten the retention period for the entire stream.
choices.explanation: This also changes the reread period for successful records and does not add a destination for failed records.

choices.text: Add an OnSuccess destination to record the failed processing.
choices.explanation: This is not the setting that sends a record of a batch whose processing was abandoned after failure.

choices.text: Set the allowed age to unlimited and continue retrying.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to stop retrying items that have become too old.

choices.text: Specify the maximum record age for business purposes in the event source mapping.
choices.explanation: This configures the function not to retry stale records indefinitely.

choices.text: Specify the corresponding destination for failures and grant permission to record the failures.
choices.explanation: The discarded failure can then be investigated from its record.

learning.reason: A Kinesis event source mapping can specify the maximum record age and a failure destination for discarded records.
learning.concept: The path for retries by the event source and the path for recording a consumer's abandoned processing are different.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Migrate only the target tables from a shared schema
prompt: AWS DMS is used to migrate business tables in the sales schema. Work tables in the same schema whose names begin with tmp_ must not be migrated. The source tables cannot be deleted or renamed. What should be configured?

choices.text: Manually delete the target tables after the transformation.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement not to transfer the work tables.

choices.text: Add a selection rule targeting the tables in sales and exclude tables whose names begin with tmp_.
choices.explanation: This narrows the DMS transfer scope without changing the source.

choices.text: Select all tables and rename the work-table names with transformation rules.
choices.explanation: Renaming a table does not make it excluded from the selection.

choices.text: Perform only the initial load and disable CDC.
choices.explanation: This changes when data is transferred but does not select which tables are included.

learning.reason: Table-mapping selection rules can define included and excluded tables by pattern.
learning.concept: Selecting the tables to transfer is separate from settings that transform the destination schema name or columns.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Narrowing reads for a high-cardinality column
prompt: An Athena Hive-format table is already partitioned by date. There are millions of distinct device_id values per day, and most queries inspect only one device. How can you narrow the reads without creating a separate S3 partition for each ID?

choices.text: Keep the date partitions and bucket the data by device_id using the corresponding format.
choices.explanation: A fixed number of buckets allows the matching read range to be selected for an equality lookup.

choices.text: Make every device_id combined with the date an S3 partition.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to limit the number of partitions.

choices.text: Without transforming the data, put only device_id at the beginning of each file name.
choices.explanation: The table's bucket layout and metadata would not be provided.

choices.text: Consolidate all dates and devices into one small file.
choices.explanation: This would not preserve date partitioning or device-specific selection.

learning.reason: Bucketing distributes a high-cardinality column across a fixed number of file groups, so an equality lookup can narrow the data range to read.
learning.concept: There is no need to create device-level directories at the same granularity as the date partitions.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Perform immediately consistent reads in a different order with the same hash key
prompt: Create a new DynamoDB table. You want to query customer IDs using the same partition key, but sort by priority rather than time. You require strongly consistent reads from the index, and the item collection size limit is satisfied. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: When creating the table, define an LSI that uses priority as its sort key, and specify strong consistency for Query.
choices.explanation: This supports both the existing partition key and consistent reads in an alternative order.

choices.text: Keep the customer key in the base table and use only a filter to change the Query sort order.
choices.explanation: A filter cannot create a sort order based on another attribute.

choices.text: Use DynamoDB Streams and Query the stream for current index results with strong consistency.
choices.explanation: A stream cannot be Query-ed as an alternative index for a table.

choices.text: Use a GSI with priority as its sort key and enable ConsistentRead.
choices.explanation: You cannot choose strongly consistent reads for a GSI.

learning.reason: An LSI uses the same partition key as the base table with a different sort key and supports strongly consistent reads.
learning.concept: Define an LSI when creating the table, and verify its usage limits.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Removing only the delete marker to reveal the valid version
prompt: An object was accidentally deleted from a versioning-enabled bucket. It is not visible through a normal GET, but the immediately preceding valid object version remains. Without uploading a new body, which operation will make the same key visible again?

choices.text: Only suspend versioning on the bucket.
choices.explanation: The existing delete marker is not removed.

choices.text: Run DeleteObject again on the same key without specifying a version ID.
choices.explanation: This does not remove the existing marker and may create another delete marker.

choices.text: Delete the immediately preceding valid version by specifying its version ID.
choices.explanation: This would remove the body that should be preserved.

choices.text: List the versions for the key and delete the current delete marker by specifying its version ID.
choices.explanation: The retained preceding object version can then become readable through a normal GET.

learning.reason: Deleting the current delete marker with its version ID can cause the previous version to appear again as the current version.
learning.concept: Avoid repeating an unversioned key deletion, which would add another delete marker.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Creating independent catalog tables from a folder hierarchy
prompt: In S3, each dataset name has year and month levels beneath it. You want a Glue crawler to create separate tables for multiple datasets with similar schemas, rather than putting them into one table as partitions. Which additional setting is required?

choices.text: Configure the dataset-name level as the table level.
choices.explanation: Each dataset at that level can be created as a separate table.

choices.text: Run the crawler more frequently.
choices.explanation: This would only repeat the same hierarchy recognition.

choices.text: Specify every year-and-month level as the root of a separate table.
choices.explanation: This would split one dataset into many tables by year and month.

choices.text: Only give the tables the same prefix in their names.
choices.explanation: This does not define how different datasets are classified.

learning.reason: The crawler's table-level setting specifies where in the absolute S3 hierarchy to create tables.
learning.concept: Keep year-and-month partitions separate from the table roots for independent datasets.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Use Delta native metadata
prompt: An Athena-compatible engine reads a Delta Lake table on S3. The current view of additions and deletions is managed by the Delta transaction log. You do not want to regenerate static symlink manifests after every update. What should you select in the crawler?

choices.text: Enable creation of a native Delta table for the corresponding Delta target.
choices.explanation: The compatible engine can use the Delta log without generating a separate manifest.

choices.text: Create a static symlink manifest once initially and assume that subsequent updates will be reflected automatically.
choices.explanation: Without updating the manifest, it will not represent the current data listing.

choices.text: Read all files as a regular Parquet external table and ignore the Delta log.
choices.explanation: Files that were replaced or deleted could be treated as current data.

choices.text: Assume that enabling bucket versioning will automatically make the catalog type Delta.
choices.explanation: Storage versioning does not specify the catalog format.

learning.reason: A Glue crawler can register a native table for Delta Lake.
learning.concept: Distinguish between having the engine read Delta metadata directly and relying on a traditional manifest.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Switch the write destination at a fixed size
prompt: An OpenSearch log index is becoming too large. The ingestion side should continue using the same write name, while writes should automatically move to a subsequent index when the current index reaches a specified size. The old index must be retained for searching. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Set an S3 lifecycle transition action to the same size.
choices.explanation: This does not control OpenSearch index rollover.

choices.text: Only delete the old index when it reaches the size threshold.
choices.explanation: This does not retain the index for searching or provide a new destination.

choices.text: Configure a write alias and an ISM rollover based on a size condition.
choices.explanation: The same name can be used for writing while switching to a new physical OpenSearch index.

choices.text: Manually change the index name in each client configuration.
choices.explanation: This does not maintain a stable write name.

learning.reason: Rollover moves the write alias to the next index while retaining the previous index.
learning.concept: The condition for deleting an old index differs from the condition for creating a new write destination.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Distinguish configuration locations in the same data platform
prompt: An administrator of Redshift Serverless configures database users and an encryption key. Another administrator configures the base capacity for analysis and the VPC connection. Which configuration unit does each setting belong to? Select two.

choices.text: Specify compute capacity only in the namespace.
choices.explanation: Compute capacity is configured at the workgroup.

choices.text: Add the KMS key to the workgroup as a limit on the number of query results.
choices.explanation: Encryption-key configuration and result-count control are separate settings.

choices.text: Define users as a VPC subnet attribute.
choices.explanation: Database users are not defined on a subnet.

choices.text: Manage users and the KMS key for data at rest in the namespace.
choices.explanation: These settings are related to data and storage.

choices.text: Manage the base compute capacity and VPC in the workgroup.
choices.explanation: These settings are related to query compute resources and networking.

learning.reason: A namespace contains data and security settings, while a workgroup contains compute and connectivity settings.
learning.concept: Distinguish the management unit for data from the management unit for the compute endpoint.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Link data that does not fit in one item by reference
prompt: You manage searchable metadata for customer files in DynamoDB. The file contents are several MB in size, and updates and retrieval operate on the entire file; the file contents are not searched by condition in DynamoDB. How should you store the data without exceeding the item-size limit?

choices.text: Create two indexes and project the same large contents into both.
choices.explanation: This does not avoid the item-size limit.

choices.text: Store the contents in S3 and store a reference to them and searchable attributes in DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: This keeps the item within the limit while separating search from retrieval of the file contents.

choices.text: Increase DynamoDB write capacity and store the several-MB item directly.
choices.explanation: The capacity mode does not increase the size limit for a single item.

choices.text: Embed every large file in the key string.
choices.explanation: This would violate key-field and item limits.

learning.reason: Store the large attribute value as an S3 object and reference it from the DynamoDB item.
learning.concept: Place the file contents and the metadata used for search and management in separate data stores.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Reducing the Number of Partitions Retrieved
prompt: An AWS Glue job reads a Glue Catalog table with hundreds of thousands of partitions. S3 reads are already limited, but retrieving the partition list from the catalog before filtering is slow. What combination should be used while preserving the existing metadata? Select two.

choices.text: Retrieve the entire list first and filter it on the client side.
choices.explanation: This does not reduce the latency of retrieving the list.

choices.text: Build a partition index based on the order in which the search is performed.
choices.explanation: The catalog can provide an index for partition searches.

choices.text: Enable partition projection only for Athena and assume that it will automatically be projected in the Glue job.
choices.explanation: This is an Athena-specific setting and does not change how the Glue job retrieves metadata.

choices.text: Change the S3 objects to a different compression format while keeping the same paths.
choices.explanation: This does not change the amount of Glue partition metadata retrieved.

choices.text: Pass conditions that use the index through catalogPartitionPredicate in the Glue job.
choices.explanation: The catalog can narrow the candidates and retrieve only the required metadata.

learning.reason: Glue partition indexes and catalogPartitionPredicate enable partition selection on the catalog side.
learning.concept: Distinguish applying conditions after retrieving the list from selecting candidates on the service side before retrieval.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Compacting Small Files After Writes
prompt: Multiple streaming processes write to the same Glue-managed Iceberg table, creating many small data files. Without adding scheduled processing for each writer, you want small files to be continuously compacted in the active table. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Reduce only the number of local partitions in one streaming job.
choices.explanation: This does not process existing small files or files created by other jobs across the table.

choices.text: Only expire old snapshots.
choices.explanation: This does not combine the contents of current small files into larger files.

choices.text: Enable compaction with the optimizer supported by the target table.
choices.explanation: The table can handle ongoing small-file organization.

choices.text: Delete some small files in S3 based on their names.
choices.explanation: This would cause some table data to be lost.

learning.reason: Glue Iceberg compaction can combine small files in a supported table into larger files.
learning.concept: Distinguish rewriting table data without losing it from expiring old snapshots.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Independently Setting the Destination Storage Class for Replication
prompt: The source S3 bucket uses Standard and is accessed frequently. New objects are replicated to a recovery bucket in another Region, but the recovery bucket is accessed infrequently and should store the objects in a different permitted class from the outset. Where should this be specified?

choices.text: Change the object class using only the destination bucket policy.
choices.explanation: Permissions and storage class specification are separate concerns.

choices.text: Specify a suitable infrequent-access class for the destination in the replication rule.
choices.explanation: The source can remain Standard while replicated data uses the specified class.

choices.text: Change the source to an infrequent-access class and assume that its original access performance and cost will not change.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to keep the source class unchanged.

choices.text: Add the name of the infrequent-access class to the object name.
choices.explanation: A prefix alone does not change the storage class.

learning.reason: An S3 replication rule can specify the storage class for the destination.
learning.concept: Choose the storage class for source and destination data according to their respective roles.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Separating Heavy Read Workloads from the Production Database
prompt: The production application using the associated RDS DB instance continues to write. Analytics is read-only, can tolerate some lag, and must not use the primary connection endpoint. Which feature should be used when replication within the same Region is sufficient?

choices.text: Only enable automated backups for the same primary.
choices.explanation: This does not create a separate read target that is continuously available.

choices.text: Use the synchronized standby of a Multi-AZ DB instance as the analytics target, even though it cannot be used for reads.
choices.explanation: The standby does not accept ordinary read queries.

choices.text: Send all analytics SQL statements to the primary and grant the same database read-only permissions.
choices.explanation: This does not separate the connection endpoint or workload.

choices.text: Configure a read replica and direct analytics connections to the replica endpoint.
choices.explanation: This separates analytics queries from the write destination.

learning.reason: An associated RDS read replica can offload read traffic to a separate connection endpoint populated through asynchronous replication.
learning.concept: Distinguish a standby configuration for high availability from a dedicated instance used for reads.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Include only frequently returned attributes in the index
prompt: A DynamoDB GSI is used for a customer list. In addition to the key attributes, status and display name are needed almost every time, but large attributes should not be included in the index. Additional reads from the base table should be avoided when returning the list. Which projection should be used?

choices.text: Project all attributes using ALL.
choices.explanation: Large attributes that should not be stored in the index would also be copied into it.

choices.text: Set the GSI ProjectionType to INCLUDE and list the required non-key attributes.
choices.explanation: The data needed for the list can be retrieved using only the index query.

choices.text: Use KEYS_ONLY and assume that the required non-key attributes are retrieved automatically.
choices.explanation: Non-key attributes are not projected into the GSI by default.

choices.text: Specify the required attributes in the list's SQL and assume that columns not in the index are returned from the base table at the same time.
choices.explanation: A GSI does not automatically retrieve non-projected attributes from the base table.

learning.reason: With INCLUDE projection, a GSI can retain specified non-key attributes in addition to its key attributes.
learning.concept: Separate the columns required for list reads from large columns that are rarely used.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Continue using the same warehouse's compute in another Availability Zone
prompt: You use a provisioned Redshift cluster with a supported RG or RA3 node type. To prepare for an Availability Zone failure, you want to use compute resources in another Availability Zone to access the same warehouse's data without changing the analytics application's connection endpoint. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Manually create a cluster with a different name in another Region.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to continue using the same Redshift connection endpoint.

choices.text: Configure Multi-AZ deployment for the supported cluster.
choices.explanation: Compute in another Availability Zone can be used while the connection endpoint is maintained.

choices.text: Add more compute nodes to a cluster in the same Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: The dependency on a single Availability Zone remains unchanged.

choices.text: Only extend the snapshot retention period.
choices.explanation: This does not provide compute in another Availability Zone that can operate immediately.

learning.reason: Redshift Multi-AZ provides compute resources in multiple Availability Zones for one warehouse and allows them to be accessed through the same connection endpoint.
learning.concept: Launching a new cluster from another snapshot is a different recovery path from using Multi-AZ compute.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Keep an existing view after rebuilding its dependency
prompt: A Redshift view references an intermediate table used for analytics. A batch job rebuilds an intermediate table with compatible columns every day. The view should be created before the referenced object exists, without creating a fixed definition-time dependency on that object. Which specification should be used?

choices.text: Change it to CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW and assume that the base table is not checked until runtime.
choices.explanation: Precomputation does not specify late binding for a view definition.

choices.text: Do not create a view; notify users of the table name each time.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve references to the same view.

choices.text: Keep a regular view and delete the dependency table with CASCADE each time.
choices.explanation: The view may also be deleted.

choices.text: Reference the table with a schema qualifier and define the view with WITH NO SCHEMA BINDING.
choices.explanation: This separates the view definition from the table's creation or replacement.

learning.reason: A view defined with WITH NO SCHEMA BINDING does not check for dependencies on underlying objects when it is created.
learning.concept: The table and columns must be valid at runtime, and the schema name must be specified explicitly in the reference.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Verify why small objects are not covered by the rule
prompt: Small logs written to S3 are several KB per object. In a newly created lifecycle transition rule, only large files transition to an infrequent-access storage class, while small ones remain even after the specified number of days has passed. The prefix and tag conditions are the same. What should be checked first?

choices.text: Assume that stopping SSE-KMS will make the small files transition automatically.
choices.explanation: The encryption method does not change the specified size restriction.

choices.text: Change the file-name extension to bypass the size restriction.
choices.explanation: The actual object size does not change.

choices.text: Expire all current versions to obtain the same effect.
choices.explanation: Expiration is not a storage-class transition.

choices.text: Check the minimum object size for the transition and whether a size filter overrides it.
choices.explanation: This can verify why small files remain under the default conditions even with the same number of days and tags.

learning.reason: A new S3 lifecycle configuration does not transition objects below a certain size by default.
learning.concept: Because transition requests also incur charges for small objects, compare the size conditions before explicitly setting them.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Expire Only Temporary Outputs in a Shared Location
prompt: Temporary files and final outputs that must be retained are mixed under the same S3 prefix. The path cannot be changed, but temporary files can be tagged when they are created. You want to automatically clean up only those files after 30 days. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Write a description in the metadata of the temporary outputs and treat Lifecycle as automatically evaluating the description.
choices.explanation: This does not configure a tag that can be used in the filter.

choices.text: Apply a dedicated tag to the temporary outputs and create a 30-day expiration rule that uses the tag as its condition.
choices.explanation: The final outputs that must be retained can be excluded.

choices.text: Configure every object under the shared prefix to expire after 30 days.
choices.explanation: The final outputs that must be retained would also be affected.

choices.text: Only write “temporary output” in the bucket-level AWS tags.
choices.explanation: This does not classify individual objects in the same bucket.

learning.reason: S3 Lifecycle can use tags to target only part of the objects in a shared location.
learning.concept: A bucket-level configuration can remain shared while processing is limited by classifications assigned to individual objects.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Detect Mismatched Rows After Migration
prompt: In a corresponding DMS migration, the numbers of rows in the source and target are similar, but you want to check whether any contents do not match. The table meets the key requirements for the validation feature. Without creating custom comparison logic, what should you enable?

choices.text: Treat the data as matching when the DMS task runs for a short time.
choices.explanation: Transfer time and data contents are independent.

choices.text: Record only the total number of rows in the source and destination.
choices.explanation: The values can differ even when the counts are the same.

choices.text: Check only the completion status.
choices.explanation: A successful transfer does not indicate that corresponding values match.

choices.text: Enable data validation on the task and check the validation status and mismatches.
choices.explanation: The corresponding rows can be compared.

learning.reason: DMS data validation can compare corresponding rows in the source and target and report mismatches.
learning.concept: Task success or table row counts alone cannot verify that the values match.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Restore Cumulative State After an Application Update
prompt: You are updating a Managed Service for Apache Flink application to a compatible version. You want to preserve customer-specific state after startup. To avoid replaying all original events after the restart, what should you do before the planned stop and when resuming? Select two.

choices.text: Create an application snapshot that records the state before the stop or update.
choices.explanation: This saves the planned restoration point.

choices.text: Start with a stateless configuration.
choices.explanation: Cumulative values are not carried over from the previous run.

choices.text: When starting, specify a configuration that restores the application from that snapshot.
choices.explanation: The snapshot's corresponding state can be used as the starting point for the new version.

choices.text: Specify only the existing CloudWatch logs as the restoration source.
choices.explanation: Logs cannot be restored as a state snapshot.

choices.text: Assume that using the same output S3 path as the old version also carries over the state.
choices.explanation: An output location is not a restoration point that stores operator state.

learning.reason: Create a persistent application snapshot and select it in the restoration configuration at startup.
learning.concept: Distinguish checkpoints used during ordinary failures from the state starting point explicitly selected for an update.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Identify and Rerun the Remaining Output from a Failed CTAS
prompt: An Athena CTAS operation failed while writing to S3. The data manifest for the failed destination is available. Before retrying to the same location, you want to identify only the partial output from this attempt while retaining other data. Which procedure should you use?

choices.text: Delete all objects in the output bucket without identifying the failed run.
choices.explanation: Other data would be lost.

choices.text: Register every file in the failed destination as valid output without further inspection.
choices.explanation: Incomplete data would be mixed into the valid output.

choices.text: Review the data manifest for the failed query and clean up only the output objects listed for the remaining target.
choices.explanation: This avoids deleting unrelated data and removes files that could be duplicated by the retry.

choices.text: Assume that hiding the query history also deletes the S3 output.
choices.explanation: Query history display and objects are separate.

learning.reason: A CTAS operation that fails partway through can leave orphaned output files, and the manifest can be used to identify them.
learning.concept: Do not delete the entire output location; reconcile the objects associated with this execution.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Measure the Breakdown of Read Capacity Used by a Query
prompt: Optimize a DynamoDB Query. In a validation environment, you want the response to show the capacity consumed by the call, broken down by table or index used. Do not infer it only from time-averaged metrics. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Select one edit event in DynamoDB Streams.
choices.explanation: Read-operation consumption is not recorded in the change stream.

choices.text: Assume that reducing the returned attributes will always include consumed capacity in the response.
choices.explanation: Projection and the setting that returns consumed capacity are separate.

choices.text: Set INDEXES for Query's ReturnConsumedCapacity.
choices.explanation: The response for the operation provides details about the capacity used.

choices.text: Set COUNT in Select and treat the number of returned items as capacity units.
choices.explanation: The item count alone does not show the capacity breakdown.

learning.reason: With INDEXES for ReturnConsumedCapacity, the response returns the capacity consumed by the operation and details for the table and indexes involved.
learning.concept: Distinguish metrics averaged across all traffic from consumption for a specific call.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Refresh Only the Analytical Data That Includes Recent Corrections
prompt: A large SPICE dataset uses a corresponding SQL source, and corrections occur in the previous 7 days. You want to set the date range to refresh without re-ingesting all records every time. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Delete the previous 7 days of SPICE data and continue using the dataset as is.
choices.explanation: This removes data that must be retained to include recent corrections.

choices.text: Only set a date filter on the dashboard.
choices.explanation: This does not change the range or freshness of data ingested into SPICE.

choices.text: Add only a schedule that always performs a full refresh.
choices.explanation: This does not avoid re-ingesting all records.

choices.text: Choose incremental refresh and specify the date column and a lookback that covers the correction period.
choices.explanation: This reflects recent corrections without re-ingesting the entire history.

learning.reason: Incremental refresh for the corresponding SPICE dataset uses a date column and lookback period to ingest the target range.
learning.concept: Incremental refresh replaces the specified period instead of unconditionally appending only to the end.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Understand Column Distributions and Missing-Value Trends Before Transformation
prompt: You are investigating new external data with Glue DataBrew. Before changing the input, the operator wants to review missing-value counts, value distributions, and statistics together to determine which processing is needed in the recipe. What should be run?

choices.text: Determine column quality only from the number of tags on the S3 objects.
choices.explanation: This does not examine column-value distributions or missing-value counts.

choices.text: Check only the last run time of the AWS Glue crawler.
choices.explanation: The schema-inference time does not show value distributions or missing values.

choices.text: Run a profile job on the target dataset and review the statistics.
choices.explanation: Missing values and distributions can be examined without applying formatting.

choices.text: Use a recipe job to replace missing values in all columns with zero in advance.
choices.explanation: This changes the result before the actual missing values in the input are investigated.

learning.reason: A profile job calculates statistics and characteristics of the input.
learning.concept: Separate executing a transformation recipe from measuring the properties of the data.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Reserve Dedicated Compute Capacity for Heavy Processing Periods
prompt: For monthly closing work involving Athena queries, you want to reserve dedicated query compute capacity separately from interactive workloads. A per-query scan-bytes limit alone does not meet the requirement. What should you configure?

choices.text: Increase only the account budget and treat the capacity as reserved as well.
choices.explanation: A billing budget and Athena execution capacity are separate.

choices.text: Increase only the storage capacity of the S3 bucket that stores query results.
choices.explanation: This does not reserve Athena execution compute.

choices.text: Only raise the scan limit for individual queries.
choices.explanation: Although the permitted input size changes, dedicated capacity is not allocated.

choices.text: Create an Athena capacity reservation and assign the workgroup used for the closing process.
choices.explanation: The target workload can run with the specified compute capacity.

learning.reason: An Athena capacity reservation assigns dedicated compute capacity to a workgroup.
learning.concept: A setting that limits scanned data and a setting that reserves and assigns compute capacity are different.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Terminate an unused cluster after the last processing job
prompt: In a shared EMR on EC2 development cluster, the cluster incurs charges for several hours after temporary debugging because no one uses it. The results are already stored in S3. In the target release, how can you configure the cluster to terminate automatically only when it is determined to be idle?

choices.text: Shorten the cluster's log retention period.
choices.explanation: This does not define a condition for terminating compute resources.

choices.text: Configure an automatic termination policy with the allowed idle time, and verify how the cluster is treated while it is in use.
choices.explanation: This can terminate a cluster that was left running while idle.

choices.text: Terminate the cluster at a fixed time every day regardless of whether it is running an active workload.
choices.explanation: This could stop the cluster while it is in use.

choices.text: Only reduce the minimum number of core nodes by one.
choices.explanation: This does not terminate the cluster when it is idle.

learning.reason: An automatic termination policy can terminate the cluster when the release-specific idle condition persists for the specified time.
learning.concept: A setting that scales down nodes and a setting that terminates the entire cluster after prolonged inactivity are different.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Reprocess data without affecting the normal incremental position
prompt: A bookmark-enabled Glue batch job must reprocess the input corresponding to past runs for a specific period into a separate output. The bookmark position used by the current scheduled processing must not be advanced or deleted. Which operation should be used?

choices.text: Reset the existing bookmark and load all records into the production output.
choices.explanation: This changes the normal processed position and does not limit processing to the specified range.

choices.text: Set the bookmark to Pause, specify the required run ID range, and write to a separate output.
choices.explanation: Rerunning the job does not update the processed position used during normal operation.

choices.text: Leave the bookmark set to Enable and update the reference point.
choices.explanation: This does not separate the reprocessing position from the normal continuation point.

choices.text: Delete the input for the period to be examined from S3 and reprocess it.
choices.explanation: This removes the data required for reprocessing.

learning.reason: The Pause setting for a job bookmark does not update its state and allows the corresponding run range to be specified.
learning.concept: A full reset must be distinguished from a limited rerun that does not affect the original continuation point.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Replay archived arrival notifications after correcting the rule
prompt: Because of a missing EventBridge rule configuration, notifications for a certain interval did not reach the data pipeline. An archive for the original event bus was already active at the time. You want to replay the specified period only to the corrected rules. What should you use?

choices.text: Replay the archive for the target time range and select the target rules.
choices.explanation: This can restart only the required processing from the archived events.

choices.text: Assume that configuring a new delivery-time DLQ will cause past nonmatching notifications to enter it retroactively.
choices.explanation: Notifications that did not match a rule in the past are not retroactively placed in that rule's DLQ.

choices.text: Delete the original S3 content and rewrite the files from scratch.
choices.explanation: This does not use the archived notifications and changes the original data.

choices.text: Reconfigure EventBridge Scheduler while leaving its normal schedule unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not republish archived past events.

learning.reason: An archive replay returns events from the specified period to the original bus and allows the rules used for replay to be selected.
learning.concept: Events that did not match a rule are not placed in that rule's delivery-failure DLQ.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Accept read charges for another organization's public dataset
prompt: An S3 bucket in another account uses Requester Pays. The required permissions and the Athena table for the source have been prepared, but queries fail because the read charges have not been accepted. Where should this be configured?

choices.text: Allow queries against Requester Pays buckets in the target workgroup.
choices.explanation: When the required permissions already exist, the data can be read under the requester-pays model.

choices.text: Use only an IAM administrator role and do not configure the billing condition.
choices.explanation: Broad access permissions alone do not accept requester-pays charges.

choices.text: Disable encryption for the query-results bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not accept the source bucket's billing condition.

choices.text: Always delete the source data so that request charges cannot occur.
choices.explanation: This makes the target data unavailable for querying.

learning.reason: Enabling Requester Pays queries in the applicable Athena workgroup allows the querying party to assume the request and data-transfer charges.
learning.concept: IAM access permissions and the setting that makes the requester responsible for charges are separate requirements.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Distinguishing idle periods from failures
prompt: A scheduled batch emits failure metrics only while it is running. Not running on holidays is normal, and missing metrics alone should not transition the alarm to a failure notification. Positive failure values should trigger a warning. Which setting should be used?

choices.text: Treat missing data for the failure alarm as notBreaching.
choices.explanation: Missing data alone will not be treated as a threshold violation.

choices.text: Shorten only the dashboard display period.
choices.explanation: This does not change the alarm evaluation rules.

choices.text: Remove the failure metric completely from notification monitoring.
choices.explanation: Actual failures would no longer generate notifications.

choices.text: Configure all missing data as breaching.
choices.explanation: A holiday with no execution could be judged as a failure.

learning.reason: CloudWatch alarms allow you to specify how missing data is handled.
learning.concept: When separately monitoring whether the workload runs as scheduled, periods with no failure metric can be treated as non-breaching.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Stopping queries when serverless analytics usage exceeds a limit
prompt: A single Redshift Serverless workgroup is used to manage consumed RPU hours during a specified period. After the limit is exceeded, the requirement is not only to record usage but also to prevent new user queries from starting during that same period. What should be used?

choices.text: Reduce the number of automatic snapshots.
choices.explanation: This does not manage the cumulative RPU hours of user queries.

choices.text: Set a usage limit for the period and specify the action that stops user queries at the limit.
choices.explanation: This controls execution when usage exceeds the budget for the specified period.

choices.text: Lower only the base RPU.
choices.explanation: The total usage during the period will not necessarily stop at the limit.

choices.text: Only write an alarm to CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: Sending a notification does not configure queries to stop starting.

learning.reason: Redshift Serverless usage limits can cap RPU hours and configure the action taken when the limit is reached.
learning.concept: Setting the compute scale at a point in time with base capacity is different from limiting cumulative usage over a period.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Comparing volume anomalies that include seasonal variation
prompt: A Glue ETL job checks the daily number of ingested records with Data Quality. The expected range should be calculated from previous runs to follow long-term changes in volume, without manually updating thresholds. In an environment that supports dynamic rules, what should be used?

choices.text: Use the crawler's partition count instead of the row count.
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate the distribution or history of the ingested-record count.

choices.text: Configure a dynamic RowCount rule that derives a range from historical evaluation counts.
choices.explanation: The current count can be compared with the evaluation history that is continuously retained.

choices.text: Set RowCount statically to 100 or more and use the same standard every day.
choices.explanation: The standard will not follow long-term changes in record volume.

choices.text: Add only IsComplete checks for missing columns.
choices.explanation: This does not compare record counts based on historical values.

learning.reason: Dynamic DQDL rules can reference previous evaluation results with constructs such as last.
learning.concept: A fixed RowCount threshold differs from a range calculated from historical values.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Restricting the execution role that job creators can specify
prompt: The analytics team may create Glue jobs, but the execution role passed to a job must be limited to one approved role. A creator must not be able to specify a different administrator role for the job. Which permissions should be configured?

choices.text: Limit only the creator's permission to read CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: This does not change which role can be passed to the job.

choices.text: Grant permission to create Glue jobs and allow PassRole for all roles.
choices.explanation: An unapproved role could be specified.

choices.text: Limit the creator's iam:PassRole permission to the ARN of the approved role and, when necessary, restrict the service that can receive the role to Glue.
choices.explanation: The creator can create jobs without being able to pass another execution role.

choices.text: Treat any role with the same name prefix as approved.
choices.explanation: This does not limit the permission to a single role ARN.

learning.reason: Passing an execution role to a service requires iam:PassRole, and the roles that may be passed can be restricted with Resource.
learning.concept: Separate permission to manage jobs from permission to delegate arbitrary permissions through a job.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Connecting ETL from a private subnet to S3 in the same Region
prompt: A Glue job uses a private subnet to connect to JDBC. It must read reference data from S3 in the same Region, but no internet egress may be created. Permissions are already configured. What should be configured in the network?

choices.text: Configure only a default route to the internet in the target subnet.
choices.explanation: This does not provide an S3 path without internet egress.

choices.text: Further expand the job's IAM permissions.
choices.explanation: This does not configure a network path.

choices.text: Place only a Glue API interface endpoint in the VPC.
choices.explanation: This provides a path to the Glue API, not the data path for the job to read from S3.

choices.text: Create an S3 gateway endpoint and associate it with the route table used by the subnets for Glue.
choices.explanation: This routes traffic to S3 without internet egress.

learning.reason: An S3 gateway endpoint provides access to S3 through the VPC route table.
learning.concept: Creating an endpoint alone does not necessarily associate it with the route table for the target subnets.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Encrypting communication paths within a cluster
prompt: For the relevant Amazon OpenSearch Service domain, HTTPS with clients and encryption at rest are enabled. An audit additionally requires protecting data transmitted between nodes within the same domain. What should be enabled?

choices.text: Rotate the encryption keys and treat the key update for encryption at rest as also protecting internal communication.
choices.explanation: Updating keys for data at rest does not configure encryption for node-to-node communication.

choices.text: Reapply a client endpoint configuration that allows only HTTPS.
choices.explanation: This controls connections from external clients but does not add the requirement for internal communication.

choices.text: Enable node-to-node encryption for the domain.
choices.explanation: This encrypts the traffic exchanged between nodes.

choices.text: Enable compression for search responses.
choices.explanation: This affects the amount of data transferred but does not protect communication with TLS.

learning.reason: Node-to-node encryption protects communication between supported OpenSearch nodes with TLS.
learning.concept: Encryption at the client entry point, internal communication, and data at rest are separate settings.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Aligning permissions for both the data and the key with an external role
prompt: Data that requires decryption in S3 is to be provided to an approved analysis role in another account. The objects are protected with a customer managed KMS key, and read permission on the bucket is already configured. In the standard AWS account-delegation configuration for KMS access, what two permissions must be configured? Select two.

choices.text: In the key policy in the owning account, allow the required key operations for the external account.
choices.explanation: The key-owning account must permit use by the other account.

choices.text: Grant the external role kms:Encrypt instead of decryption permission.
choices.explanation: This does not allow the decryption required to read the data.

choices.text: Edit the policy of the AWS managed key for S3 to add the external role.
choices.explanation: Users cannot edit the key policy of an AWS managed key.

choices.text: Allow the target role in the external account to perform kms:Decrypt on the key.
choices.explanation: The specified IAM role can decrypt with the key for which access was granted.

choices.text: Change only the S3 policy and make no KMS configuration changes.
choices.explanation: KMS permissions are evaluated separately.

learning.reason: Cross-account KMS use requires permissions on both the key-owning side and the external IAM side.
learning.concept: A policy that permits retrieving an S3 object does not by itself grant decrypt permission for the KMS key.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Restricting the partitions that each tenant can access
prompt: A single DynamoDB table uses the tenant ID as its partition key. A user's role should be able to perform only GetItem and Query operations on items for the corresponding key. Without relying only on an application-specific WHERE condition, what should be configured in IAM?

choices.text: Make the condition depend only on the value of the capacity mode.
choices.explanation: This does not control which tenant's partition the item belongs to.

choices.text: Allow reads against the table ARN without adding a partition-key condition.
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish among multiple tenants in the table.

choices.text: Add a dynamodb:LeadingKeys condition to the permitted GetItem and Query actions, allowing only the target tenant values.
choices.explanation: This restricts the permitted partition-key range even within the same table.

choices.text: Allow all items in IAM and ask users to specify conditions in Query.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for IAM to deny out-of-range requests made outside the application.

learning.reason: The dynamodb:LeadingKeys condition can restrict the permitted partition-key values for the applicable API actions.
learning.concept: The tenant identifier should correspond to trusted session information, and operations outside the tenant's scope should not be permitted.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
