title: Separate Input Values from SQL Structure
prompt: Through the Redshift Data API, a dataset ID must be passed as a condition value to an approved SELECT statement. Which specification should be used so that client input cannot change the SQL structure during execution?

choices.text: Place a named placeholder in the SQL and pass the input value separately as a parameter.
choices.explanation: The value is treated as a condition value and is not concatenated directly into the SQL structure.

choices.text: Only extend the retention period for audit logs.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent the input from becoming part of the SQL.

choices.text: Concatenate the client value directly into the SQL statement.
choices.explanation: This does not separate the input value from the SQL structure.

choices.text: Allow any client to embed a table name freely in the SQL.
choices.explanation: This would not preserve the approved SQL structure.

learning.reason: The Redshift Data API supports named parameters for condition values.
learning.concept: Identifiers such as table and column names should be managed as approved fixed definitions and kept separate from user-provided values.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Verify the Integrity of Stored Audit Logs
prompt: For CloudTrail logs from an analytics platform that have been retained long term, you need to verify after collection that the records were not changed and that no logs were lost. Which feature should be enabled at collection time, and which operation should be performed during the audit? Select two.

choices.text: Assume that all logs are unchanged if only the final file size matches.
choices.explanation: This cannot detect changes to files with the same size or missing other logs.

choices.text: Enable trail log file integrity validation from the time of collection.
choices.explanation: The digest files required for validation are delivered.

choices.text: Use the digests for the audit period to validate the log files.
choices.explanation: This can check for changes and deletions.

choices.text: Treat enabling integrity validation after the period ends as generating digests retroactively for earlier logs.
choices.explanation: Logs from before validation was enabled are not signed retroactively.

choices.text: Use only Amazon S3 default encryption to prove that the files match those delivered.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest alone does not compare the files with the original log information.

learning.reason: CloudTrail log file integrity validation uses signed digests delivered with the logs to verify log integrity.
learning.concept: Encryption protects content, whereas detecting changes or omissions during an audit requires a separate integrity check.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Restrict Verified Load Permissions to the Designated Role
prompt: Analysts and load operators for a provisioned Redshift cluster use the same database. The IAM role that reads from Amazon S3 is attached to the cluster, but only approved load operators should be able to use it with COPY. Which permission should be controlled on the database side?

choices.text: Grant the target IAM role's ASSUMEROLE permission for COPY only to the load operators, and remove any broad existing grants.
choices.explanation: Even though the role is attached to the cluster, this prevents other users from using it with COPY.

choices.text: Set the IAM role's display name to loader.
choices.explanation: This does not configure permissions for individual database users.

choices.text: Allow only the load operators to SELECT from the table.
choices.explanation: This does not control the IAM role specified for COPY.

choices.text: Allow all database users to use the target IAM role's ASSUMEROLE permission.
choices.explanation: This does not restrict use to the load operators.

learning.reason: Redshift's ASSUMEROLE permission controls which IAM roles and commands can be used for external operations.
learning.concept: Database connection permissions, table INSERT permissions, and permission to use an AWS-side role must be evaluated separately.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Continuously Identify Sensitive Data Across All Managed Buckets
prompt: You do not know what is stored in many S3 buckets. Initially, an administrator does not want to enumerate every individual bucket, but wants to continuously analyze representative samples to determine whether sensitive data is present. Which feature provides this capability?

choices.text: Determine whether data is sensitive by looking only at the storage class recorded in S3 Inventory.
choices.explanation: The content cannot be identified from the storage class.

choices.text: Determine whether content is present from the number of object operations recorded by CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: API activity history does not classify object content.

choices.text: Enable Macie automated sensitive data discovery and review the scope and discovery results.
choices.explanation: It can analyze a broad scope without manually defining jobs for every bucket.

choices.text: Scan one known bucket once.
choices.explanation: This does not continuously analyze many buckets whose contents have not been identified.

learning.reason: Macie automated sensitive data discovery selects representative objects from the target scope for analysis.
learning.concept: A batch job with an explicitly specified scope has a different purpose from a feature that continuously samples a broad scope.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Verifying that ciphertext matches the data being processed
prompt: An application independently encrypts sensitive data using the corresponding KMS symmetric key. If ciphertext is mistaken for ciphertext from another dataset, you want decryption to fail when the specified dataset ID is used. The ID itself is not sensitive. What should you use?

choices.text: Use only the key alias as the dataset ID and change it every time.
choices.explanation: This does not verify the match between the ciphertext and the dataset ID during decryption.

choices.text: Pass the business-validated dataset ID as the encryption context during both encryption and decryption.
choices.explanation: The same ciphertext cannot be decrypted with that context if the IDs do not match.

choices.text: Put the entire sensitive payload in the encryption context.
choices.explanation: The encryption context is not treated as secret and is not a place to store the payload.

choices.text: Write the ID only in the filename without encrypting it.
choices.explanation: A filename value is not cryptographically authenticated and bound to the ciphertext.

learning.reason: The encryption context is bound to the ciphertext as authenticated additional data, so the same value is required during decryption.
learning.concept: Use non-sensitive information, and do not place secrets in a value that may appear in CloudTrail.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Aligning access for principals in the organization
prompt: A dedicated data-platform bucket should be usable only by IAM principals from accounts that belong to the authorized AWS Organizations organization. You do not want to manually edit a list of account IDs in the bucket policy whenever an account joins or leaves. Which condition should you use?

choices.text: Write the organization ID in a bucket tag and rely on that alone to deny access.
choices.explanation: A tag alone does not evaluate whether the requesting principal belongs to the organization.

choices.text: Assume that limiting the AWS Region excludes principals outside the organization.
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish another organization in the same Region.

choices.text: Add a bucket-policy condition that specifies the organization by using aws:PrincipalOrgID.
choices.explanation: The organization membership information can be used to determine the permitted access scope.

choices.text: Enumerate all member account IDs as a fixed list.
choices.explanation: Manual editing is still required when the organization changes.

learning.reason: aws:PrincipalOrgID can be used as a condition on the organization to which the requesting principal belongs.
learning.concept: Handle service-integration exceptions and any principal-specific permissions according to the requirements.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Obtaining data credentials while preserving catalog permissions
prompt: Analysts have the required SELECT permission on a table registered with Lake Formation. They also have the IAM permissions needed to use Athena, but the diagnosis says they lack permission to obtain data-access credentials from Lake Formation. Do not grant direct access to the S3 source data. What should you add?

choices.text: Run a Glue crawler to re-infer the column types.
choices.explanation: This does not change the analyst's IAM permission to access data.

choices.text: Grant SELECT again on the same table.
choices.explanation: This does not grant the IAM permission for the missing credential-acquisition operation.

choices.text: Allow lakeformation:GetDataAccess for the analysis role while preserving the existing table permissions.
choices.explanation: The role can obtain permission-compliant data access without adding direct access to the source data.

choices.text: Grant the analysts full S3 read access to the registered source bucket.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement not to grant direct access and does not provide the specified API permission.

learning.reason: Users who access Lake Formation permissions through Athena need lakeformation:GetDataAccess in the corresponding IAM policy.
learning.concept: Lake Formation table permissions and the IAM API permission required on the user side are separate.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Reading before-and-after values in one stream record
prompt: A Lambda function receives DynamoDB updates and compares the status before and after the change. Reading the main table after the update does not provide the previous value. Which stream view type should you use for future updates?

choices.text: Use NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES.
choices.explanation: A single change record can include the item images before and after the update.

choices.text: Use OLD_IMAGE and always treat the current table value as the value immediately after that update.
choices.explanation: A later update may occur, so the current value may not be the post-update value for the target change.

choices.text: Use KEYS_ONLY.
choices.explanation: This identifies the item but does not provide the before-and-after values for comparison.

choices.text: Use NEW_IMAGE and derive the previous value from the result.
choices.explanation: The previous value cannot be reconstructed for arbitrary updates.

learning.reason: The stream view type specifies which item images are included in a change record.
learning.concept: Keys alone are insufficient when the values themselves must be compared.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Preventing the destination from being changed at startup
prompt: Multiple operators start the same Glue job with arguments. The input date can be changed at runtime, but for production runs, the destination must always be fixed to an approved value. Where should the destination be placed in the job configuration?

choices.text: Put the recommended destination only in the execution Arguments.
choices.explanation: The caller can replace it every time.

choices.text: Put the destination in NonOverridableArguments.
choices.explanation: The destination cannot be overridden by arguments for an individual run.

choices.text: Put the destination only in DefaultArguments.
choices.explanation: An execution argument with the same name takes precedence over the default value.

choices.text: Put the destination only in the job tags.
choices.explanation: This does not enforce the precedence of job arguments.

learning.reason: In Glue, NonOverridableArguments take precedence over execution-level Arguments.
learning.concept: Only arguments that must be fixed need to be non-overridable; other inputs can remain under the control of the execution.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Dividing user activity by periods of inactivity
prompt: Use Managed Service for Apache Flink to aggregate clicks by user. Instead of fixed calendar intervals, treat the next event as belonging to a separate group when 30 minutes have been quiet since the last event. Which window should be used?

choices.text: Use fixed 30-minute tumbling windows.
choices.explanation: Activity is split at fixed boundaries even when it continues.

choices.text: Put all users into one global window.
choices.explanation: The inactivity gap is not evaluated independently for each user.

choices.text: Key by user and use a session window with a 30-minute gap.
choices.explanation: Aggregation can be separated according to each user's inactivity period.

choices.text: Use a 30-minute sliding window that advances at short intervals.
choices.explanation: This creates overlapping time intervals rather than boundaries based on inactivity.

source.label: Apache Flink公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A session window uses a period of inactivity between events as its boundary.
learning.concept: It is useful for data in which activity does not start or end at fixed times.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Not waiting for the size limit during low traffic
prompt: An untransformed Data Firehose delivery stream to S3 delivers small files periodically during low-traffic periods. You had assumed that delivery would wait until a specified size was reached. What is the basic behavior of the buffering hints?

choices.text: Firehose waits until S3 automatically combines the received files.
choices.explanation: S3 does not automatically combine received files.

choices.text: Delivery can occur when the time condition is met even if the size is not reached.
choices.explanation: This explains why small files can be generated during low-traffic periods.

choices.text: No delivery occurs until both the size and time conditions are met.
choices.explanation: This cannot explain the described low-traffic behavior.

choices.text: The hint's number of seconds is used only for the client's connection timeout.
choices.explanation: The setting controls data accumulation before delivery.

learning.reason: Firehose has size and time buffering hints, and delivery normally begins when whichever condition is reached first.
learning.concept: The hints do not guarantee an exact data-arrival deadline.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Verifying a large object's contents on the receiving side
prompt: The sender has calculated the full-object CRC64NVME checksum for a file uploaded using multipart upload. You want to pass that value to S3 and have S3 verify it against the complete received object when the upload is completed. Which specification should be used?

choices.text: Only append the checksum value to the file name.
choices.explanation: S3 does not verify the contents against the checksum.

choices.text: Assume that the ETag is always the MD5 of the complete object and compare it with CRC64NVME.
choices.explanation: The algorithm and the meaning of the value for multipart uploads are different.

choices.text: Specify the corresponding full-object checksum and pass the precomputed value to S3 when completing the upload.
choices.explanation: The server can compare it with the completed object contents.

choices.text: Delete the pre-upload value after transmission and compare only the sizes.
choices.explanation: This cannot detect content changes when the size remains the same.

learning.reason: S3 multipart uploads support validation with the corresponding full-object checksum.
learning.concept: Do not treat a multipart ETag as a single hash of the object's contents.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Reduce a task response while preserving the original input
prompt: A Step Functions JSONPath state receives a batch ID as part of its input. The integrated task returns a large response. You need to extract only jobId, add it under the input's details, and pass the result to downstream states. Which two settings should be combined? Choose two.

choices.text: Use only InputPath to extract jobId from the task execution result.
choices.explanation: InputPath selects from the input before execution and does not reference the task result.

choices.text: Omit ResultPath and assume that the input is preserved by default.
choices.explanation: By default, the entire input is replaced by the task result.

choices.text: Set ResultPath to null and assume that jobId is added to the input.
choices.explanation: This setting discards the task result.

choices.text: Use ResultPath to store the result at $.details.
choices.explanation: This preserves input such as the existing batch ID and adds the result.

choices.text: Use ResultSelector to select only jobId from the returned value.
choices.explanation: This reduces the result to only the required attribute.

learning.reason: ResultSelector transforms the task result, while ResultPath adds the transformed result to a specified location in the original input.
learning.concept: Selecting input for a task and combining the result returned by the task are separate stages.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Choose an execution type for a high volume of short processes
prompt: Independent transformations for individual events finish within a few seconds, and all actions produce the same result when retried. The workflows will be started asynchronously at high volume, and a .sync integration that waits for job completion will not be used. Which Step Functions workflow type should be used?

choices.text: Use an Express workflow with a .sync job execution integration and assume that it is always available.
choices.explanation: The stated Express workflow cannot use that integration pattern.

choices.text: Use an asynchronous Express workflow.
choices.explanation: This matches short-duration, high-frequency processing where retries are acceptable.

choices.text: Use the same Express configuration with processing waits lasting several days.
choices.explanation: This exceeds the execution time limit intended for short-running workflows.

choices.text: Choose asynchronous Express because exactly-once execution is required.
choices.explanation: This contradicts the execution model of asynchronous Express workflows.

learning.reason: Express Workflows are intended for short-duration, high-volume workflows, and asynchronous execution uses an at-least-once execution model.
learning.concept: Confirm that the workload can be retried and verify the execution-duration and integration requirements.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Pass large intermediate data between tasks
prompt: An MWAA transformation task creates a data frame that is several GB in size. The downstream task runs on a different worker. Which design avoids putting the large payload in Airflow's metadata database while allowing the downstream task to receive only the output for a specific run?

choices.text: Overwrite one fixed S3 key for every run.
choices.explanation: Multiple runs could cause the tasks to use the wrong payload.

choices.text: Send the several-GB data frame in its entirety through the default XCom.
choices.explanation: This does not avoid a large write to Airflow's metadata database.

choices.text: Pass only the /tmp path from the upstream worker.
choices.explanation: A different worker is not guaranteed to be able to access the same file.

choices.text: Write the payload to a run-specific S3 key and pass only its URI through XCom.
choices.explanation: The payload stays out of the database, and the downstream task can identify the corresponding data.

source.label: Apache Airflow公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: Default XCom is intended for small values, while intermediate payloads can be stored in an external data store.
learning.concept: Distinguish files in a process-local directory from data that can be accessed by a different worker.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Perform large-scale string transformations with built-in expressions
prompt: A Glue Spark job runs a Python UDF on every row to perform simple trim and lowercase operations on a column. Spark has equivalent built-in functions, and no custom processing is required. What should be changed?

choices.text: Change the S3 storage class and run the same UDF.
choices.explanation: This does not improve the execution cost of the transformation function.

choices.text: Use the built-in trim and lower functions as column expressions.
choices.explanation: This preserves the value transformation while allowing Spark to process it.

choices.text: Collect all rows on the driver and process them in a Python loop.
choices.explanation: This eliminates distributed processing and concentrates the load on the driver.

choices.text: Change only the UDF name to alphanumeric characters.
choices.explanation: The path that invokes Python once per row remains unchanged.

learning.reason: Using Spark built-in functions in expressions avoids invoking a Python UDF once per row.
learning.concept: Reduce processing between the JVM and Python while preserving the meaning of the transformation.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Counting unique values while allowing some estimation error
prompt: You want to see an approximate number of devices in a very large click table in Athena. An estimate is acceptable for the dashboard, but do not substitute the total number of event rows. Which function should you use?

choices.text: Return only the proportion of rows whose device ID is not NULL.
choices.explanation: This does not estimate the number of distinct devices.

choices.text: Count the input rows with COUNT(*).
choices.explanation: Multiple events from the same device are counted separately.

choices.text: Apply approx_distinct to the device ID.
choices.explanation: This can return an estimated unique count even when duplicate records exist.

choices.text: Count distinct devices in each file and add the counts together.
choices.explanation: The same device appearing in multiple files would be counted more than once.

learning.reason: approx_distinct can estimate the number of unique values.
learning.concept: The count of records including duplicates is different from the number of distinct values when some estimation error is acceptable.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Recording published rows and completion status in the same transaction
prompt: You want a procedure in Redshift to ensure that writing the processed results and updating the completion status in a control table always succeed together. No explicit intermediate commit is needed, and exceptions may be returned to the caller. How should you configure it?

choices.text: Write the processed results and immediately issue COMMIT, then update the completion status.
choices.explanation: The operations become part of separate transactions.

choices.text: Use NONATOMIC to automatically commit the two statements in sequence.
choices.explanation: If the later operation fails, the earlier operation may still be committed.

choices.text: Perform both operations in a normal atomic procedure without placing an operation that ends the transaction between them.
choices.explanation: This prevents a failure from committing only one of the two operations.

choices.text: Commit only the completion status in the control table first, and record any failure to process the results separately.
choices.explanation: The completion status can become inconsistent with the actual publication.

learning.reason: A corresponding default atomic stored procedure can process the operations as one transaction.
learning.concept: The same atomicity does not hold if a boundary such as TRUNCATE or an explicit commit is introduced.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Converting monthly columns into rows of a common structure
prompt: You are processing sales data in DataBrew with separate columns named jan, feb, and mar. You want to retain the customer ID and convert the data into multiple rows with the month name and amount in columns. Which transformation should you use?

choices.text: Remove duplicate rows for each customer ID.
choices.explanation: The monthly columns are not expanded into rows.

choices.text: Specify the monthly columns and apply UNPIVOT while retaining the customer ID.
choices.explanation: This expands the fixed columns into rows represented by a month name and a value.

choices.text: Add all monthly values and retain only the total.
choices.explanation: The values for individual months are lost.

choices.text: Use PIVOT to add columns for each month name.
choices.explanation: This is the opposite of the required column-to-row transformation.

learning.reason: UNPIVOT can transform multiple specified columns into name-and-value pairs.
learning.concept: Distinguish an operation that combines columns into one string from an operation that expands them into rows.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Checking for replacement of a data-bearing resource before applying a change
prompt: You are changing a DynamoDB table used for ingestion and managed by CloudFormation. Before deciding whether to proceed, an operator wants to determine whether the change would replace the existing table without applying the update. What should be used?

choices.text: Create a change set for the current stack and check the table's Replacement status.
choices.explanation: This lets you check before application whether the existing resource may be replaced.

choices.text: Apply the update immediately and then investigate whether the table name changed.
choices.explanation: The change is applied before replacement is checked.

choices.text: Assume that changing only the stack tags prevents replacement of the table.
choices.explanation: Tags do not determine the nature of the planned update.

choices.text: Run only a template syntax check.
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate the specific result of the update to the existing table.

learning.reason: A change set provides a way to inspect planned changes and replacements before an update is executed.
learning.concept: In addition to validating template syntax, inspect the concrete impact on the existing stack.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Restore a key containing spaces or plus signs from a notification
prompt: A Python application processing S3 notifications fails on GetObject only for keys whose names contain spaces or plus signs. The received object.key is URL-encoded in form format. What preprocessing should be applied?

choices.text: URL-encode the key from the notification again before looking it up.
choices.explanation: This double-encodes a value that is already encoded.

choices.text: Remove all plus signs and percent characters.
choices.explanation: This also removes characters required by the original key.

choices.text: Apply an unquote_plus-equivalent operation once to the received key string.
choices.explanation: This restores escaped symbols and spaces represented by plus signs.

choices.text: Pass the string from the notification directly to GetObject without decoding it.
choices.explanation: It will not become the actual key string containing spaces.

learning.reason: The key in the notification is URL-encoded, and spaces are represented by plus signs.
learning.concept: Because an original plus sign is itself escaped, pay attention to the order and number of decoding operations.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Generate many partitions in separate batches
prompt: Create a new daily table with an Athena CTAS statement. The engine allows at most 100 partitions to be written at once, and the target covers 300 days. How can you prepare it using only Athena without writing the same data twice?

choices.text: Increase only the query-results location for the Athena workgroup.
choices.explanation: This does not change the partition limit for a single write operation.

choices.text: Pass the same 300 days repeatedly to a single CTAS statement.
choices.explanation: The partition limit for one statement remains unchanged.

choices.text: Create the first range with CTAS, then use INSERT INTO for the remaining non-overlapping ranges, each containing no more than 100 partitions.
choices.explanation: This outputs the entire period while respecting the limit for each statement.

choices.text: Include the same range in INSERT INTO for every batch.
choices.explanation: The ranges overlap, so the data may be written twice.

learning.reason: CTAS and INSERT INTO can be separated so that each statement writes a limited number of partitions.
learning.concept: Dividing the period into exclusive ranges prevents the same day from being created in multiple batches.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Distinguish files written to S3 from committed output
prompt: A Flink FileSink using the supported S3 file system continuously writes to S3. An operator understands that even when a file being written has rolled, it must be committed before downstream consumers can read it. Under what condition is a file committed in streaming mode?

choices.text: Enable checkpointing and commit pending files when a checkpoint succeeds.
choices.explanation: This links processing state with completion of the published file.

choices.text: Treat every file past its roll time as committed regardless of checkpointing.
choices.explanation: A file can remain uncommitted after rolling.

choices.text: Disable checkpointing and change only the file name.
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee commit behavior during streaming.

choices.text: Treat the file contents as complete whenever a filename resembling an in-progress file appears in an S3 listing.
choices.explanation: Being visible in a listing is different from being committed.

source.label: Apache Flink公式ドキュメント

learning.reason: A streaming FileSink commits pending files in coordination with checkpoints.
learning.concept: File completion caused by rolling and the commit that makes a file safe for downstream readers are separate events.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Use the same Python dependencies without network connectivity
prompt: An AWS Glue job cannot connect to external package repositories. Approved S3 storage can contain wheels for the supported Python version. How should the approved library be added for each job?

choices.text: Assume that placing the wheel in S3 automatically installs it in every job.
choices.explanation: This does not configure which dependency should be loaded.

choices.text: Place the approved wheel in S3 and specify its URI with --additional-python-modules for the job.
choices.explanation: This uses the specified dependency without requiring an external repository.

choices.text: Place binaries for another operating system at the same path without checking compatibility.
choices.explanation: There is no guarantee that the Glue runtime can use them.

choices.text: Specify only the package name and retrieve it from public PyPI.
choices.explanation: This requires access to an unauthorized external network.

learning.reason: A supported Glue job can specify additional Python modules from a wheel stored in S3.
learning.concept: Prepare a wheel compatible with the execution runtime and the complete dependency set in an accessible location.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Make container artifacts available as on-demand processing output
prompt: Use SageMaker AI Processing to periodically generate offline features from S3 input. The container can write results to a designated local path. The results of each run must remain in S3 after the instance terminates. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Use the processing script's exit code as the feature file name.
choices.explanation: The feature contents are not stored in S3.

choices.text: Declare the destination as an input channel and treat it as synchronization in the reverse direction.
choices.explanation: An input configuration does not save local artifacts to S3.

choices.text: Map the designated path under /opt/ml/processing where the processing job writes output to a run-specific S3 destination by using ProcessingOutput.
choices.explanation: The artifacts remain available after the run ends.

choices.text: Write only to the container's /tmp directory and rely on it for persistence.
choices.explanation: The files are unavailable when the temporary execution environment ends.

learning.reason: Processing job output settings map a local container path to an S3 destination.
learning.concept: Files that exist only in the execution environment do not remain as artifacts after the job ends.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Do not repeatedly process successfully handled queue items
prompt: Lambda reads 10 messages at a time from an SQS standard queue, and only some of the transformations fail. Which two settings should be combined to return only the failed items to the queue without retrying the successful ones? Select two.

choices.text: Only increase the visibility timeout.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a response that distinguishes successful items from failed items.

choices.text: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures in the event source mapping.
choices.explanation: Lambda can recognize a partial batch response.

choices.text: In the handler, put only the IDs of failed messages in batchItemFailures and return it.
choices.explanation: Successfully processed messages are not included in the retry set.

choices.text: Put only the IDs of successful messages in batchItemFailures.
choices.explanation: This specifies the retry set in the opposite way.

choices.text: Return the first failure as an exception outside the function's normal response.
choices.explanation: The entire batch may be treated as failed.

learning.reason: A partial batch response returns the IDs of failed items so that successfully processed items can be excluded from retries.
learning.concept: An exception that fails the entire batch is handled differently from an item-level failure reported in the response.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Create regional, product-level, and overall aggregates in one SQL query
prompt: In Athena, aggregate sales data containing region and product. Only three types of results are needed: by region alone, by product alone, and overall. All combinations of region and product should not be returned. Which specification should you use?

choices.text: Specify region and product together in a standard GROUP BY clause.
choices.explanation: This produces the combined grouping level, not the separate regional, product, and overall aggregates.

choices.text: Add LIMIT to the results to reduce the number of aggregation types.
choices.explanation: This does not explicitly generate the required grouping levels.

choices.text: Use CUBE to include all combinations of region and product.
choices.explanation: This also calculates the unnecessary grouping level containing both region and product.

choices.text: Use GROUP BY GROUPING SETS to specify region, product, and the empty set.
choices.explanation: The query returns the three specified grouping levels in one query.

learning.reason: GROUPING SETS explicitly defines the aggregation levels that are required.
learning.concept: The grand total across all rows is represented by the empty grouping set.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Send only fully uploaded SFTP files for validation and storage
prompt: An AWS Transfer Family SFTP server receives input in S3. For every fully uploaded file, you must perform business validation and copy it to a designated location. The receiving client must not be required to call any additional APIs. What should you configure?

choices.text: Add a step to the client's operating procedure requiring validation to be run manually.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement for automatic execution on the receiving side.

choices.text: Configure validation and copy steps in a workflow for fully uploaded files, and associate the workflow with the SFTP server.
choices.explanation: Post-processing can run when a file is received.

choices.text: Associate processing for partially uploaded files as the complete business input.
choices.explanation: This could send an incomplete file through the normal processing flow.

choices.text: Make only the connecting user's home directory name identical to the validation destination.
choices.explanation: No post-upload steps are executed.

learning.reason: A Transfer Family managed workflow can be associated with the server to perform post-upload processing.
learning.concept: Processing for fully uploaded files must be distinguished from processing for partially uploaded files.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Gradually switching to a new version of a transformation function
prompt: A Lambda function managed with SAM performs input transformation and is invoked through a production alias. You want to first route some invocations to a compatible new version and roll back to the previous version if a specified CloudWatch alarm fires. How should this be configured? Select two.

choices.text: Publish versions with AutoPublishAlias and use a canary deployment with DeploymentPreference.
choices.explanation: This routes some invocations to the new version initially.

choices.text: Specify only an increased timeout in the SAM template.
choices.explanation: This does not configure traffic allocation to the new version or alarm integration.

choices.text: Specify the relevant CloudWatch alarm in DeploymentPreference's Alarms.
choices.explanation: This can initiate a rollback when an anomaly occurs during deployment.

choices.text: Switch all invocations to the new version first and stop monitoring.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirements for gradual deployment and automatic control when an anomaly occurs.

choices.text: Ask clients to delete the old alias.
choices.explanation: This would not preserve existing references or control traffic allocation.

learning.reason: SAM's DeploymentPreference can use CodeDeploy to manage switching an alias that points to published versions.
learning.concept: Provide both gradual traffic allocation and monitoring conditions that can initiate an automatic rollback.

category: データストア管理

title: Filtering documents by tenant while scanning a time range
prompt: In an Amazon DocumentDB order collection, every query specifies an equality condition on tenantId and a range condition on createdAt. Documents from multiple tenants are mixed together. In what order should the fields be placed to support both conditions with one compound index?

choices.text: Convert createdAt to a regular-expression string and search it with a full-text index.
choices.explanation: This is not a compound index designed for the date range and tenant equality conditions.

choices.text: Put an arbitrary document ID that is not used for equality filtering first in the index.
choices.explanation: The leading field would not correspond to the target equality condition.

choices.text: Index only tenantId and exclude the creation time from the search criteria.
choices.explanation: This does not handle the date condition with the same compound index.

choices.text: Create a compound index with tenantId first and createdAt second.
choices.explanation: This narrows the range by tenant and then applies the date condition within that tenant.

learning.reason: A compound index can narrow the leading field with an equality condition and scan a range on a subsequent field.
learning.concept: Consider whether the leading fields in the index order match the query pattern.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Representing multilevel dependencies as graph relationships
prompt: For dependency discovery, you need to list downstream consumers at any depth by following a dataset to a job and then to further consumers of that job's output. Store dependencies as edges, rather than expanding and storing every path in advance. Which data store should you use?

choices.text: Search for graph edges using only CloudWatch metric dimensions.
choices.explanation: This does not provide traversal between graph nodes.

choices.text: Store only dependency counts in DynamoDB counters.
choices.explanation: This cannot reconstruct individual nodes or paths.

choices.text: Store datasets and jobs as nodes and dependencies as edges in Neptune, then traverse them with the corresponding graph queries.
choices.explanation: This supports multilevel exploration of relationships as a data model.

choices.text: Export all JSON paths to a single S3 object every day.
choices.explanation: This can result in an operation that expands every path before exploration.

learning.reason: Amazon Neptune can run graph queries against nodes and relationships.
learning.concept: You can explore by traversing relationships without deciding on a fixed number of joins in advance.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Reducing database administration while retaining the application's CQL
prompt: An application uses Cassandra-compatible CQL for business access with a partition key. The data types and APIs it uses are supported by the target, and you do not want to manage node scaling or patching. Which data store should you use?

choices.text: Configure a CQL port on Amazon S3 and query it directly.
choices.explanation: Amazon S3 does not handle the CQL database protocol.

choices.text: Use Redshift as a native CQL connection target without changes.
choices.explanation: Redshift is not a data store that supports the existing CQL calls.

choices.text: Install Cassandra on EC2 and manage the cluster yourselves.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to reduce administration work.

choices.text: Create the appropriate keyspace and tables in Amazon Keyspaces and use a compatible CQL connection.
choices.explanation: This reduces the need to operate a custom cluster.

learning.reason: Amazon Keyspaces is a managed store compatible with Apache Cassandra.
learning.concept: Before migrating, confirm that the CQL features already used are supported by the target.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Persisting a High-Speed State Store
prompt: An online workload uses Valkey- or Redis OSS-compatible data structures. The state is primary data rather than a cache that can be discarded after each use, and it requires low latency and durability across multiple AZs. Which service should be used?

choices.text: Store the writes only in Lambda local memory.
choices.explanation: The state is not preserved if the execution environment is lost.

choices.text: Deploy only a temporary cache that tolerates data loss without an external source of truth.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the durability requirement for primary data.

choices.text: Use S3 Glacier Deep Archive as a low-latency compatible API.
choices.explanation: It does not provide immediate Valkey-compatible operations.

choices.text: Configure a durable store in Amazon MemoryDB using compatible APIs.
choices.explanation: It can provide low-latency reads and writes while meeting the required durability.

learning.reason: MemoryDB complements in-memory access with transaction logs stored across multiple AZs.
learning.concept: Distinguish a disposable cache backed by another source of truth from the requirements of a durable primary store.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Managing Iceberg Tables in Table Namespaces
prompt: A team manages Iceberg tables with S3 Tables. Instead of manually organizing business data as object keys, the team wants to separate orders and audits into namespaces within one table bucket. Under what should the tables be created?

choices.text: Create business-specific namespaces in the table bucket and create the tables inside them.
choices.explanation: The tables can be identified by namespace.

choices.text: Create an empty object under a standard bucket name and treat it as if S3 Tables automatically converts it into a table.
choices.explanation: This does not create a table resource.

choices.text: Use an Athena workgroup as the physical storage location for each table.
choices.explanation: A workgroup is not a table namespace.

choices.text: Group the ARNs of each table into a namespace with S3 Lifecycle.
choices.explanation: Lifecycle does not create a table hierarchy.

learning.reason: With S3 Tables, create namespaces inside a table bucket, then create tables under those namespaces.
learning.concept: A table bucket resource uses a different management model from prefixes in a general-purpose bucket.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Choosing an Indexing Method That Can Be Created Before Ingestion
prompt: You are preparing similarity search on Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector support. The index will be created before most of the vectors are loaded. Additional memory during construction is acceptable, and you want to avoid a stage that learns clusters from existing data, as IVFFlat does. Which two options should be combined to use an index for cosine distance? Select two.

choices.text: Train IVFFlat with no data and always obtain the optimal lists.
choices.explanation: This does not match the requirement that groups be built from representative data.

choices.text: Create a date-based B-tree index that has no distance definition.
choices.explanation: It does not order vector neighbors.

choices.text: Choose HNSW, which does not require data training.
choices.explanation: The index can be created before most of the data is loaded.

choices.text: Store only the number of elements in a regular column and use it to select neighbors.
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate distances between vectors.

choices.text: Use HNSW on the vector column with vector_cosine_ops for cosine distance, and use the corresponding distance operator in the query.
choices.explanation: The distance used by the workload and the index operator can be aligned.

learning.reason: HNSW is a graph-based approximate index and, unlike IVFFlat, does not require a training step before construction.
learning.concept: Evaluate the trade-offs among search accuracy, construction time, and memory using actual data.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Synchronizing Inputs That Predate a New Replication Rule
prompt: You added live S3 replication to another Region this month. Objects targeted from now on are replicated, but objects that have been stored since before the rollout must also be sent according to the same policy. What should you use without rewriting the objects?

choices.text: Add an expired rule to the existing objects.
choices.explanation: This could delete the source data without synchronizing it to the destination.

choices.text: Read the bodies of all existing objects and overwrite them from the application each time.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement not to rewrite the objects.

choices.text: Disable the existing live rule once and enable it again with the same contents.
choices.explanation: Toggling the rule does not batch-transfer objects from the past.

choices.text: Run S3 Batch Replication for the required existing objects.
choices.explanation: This can add objects from before the live-replication rollout without rewriting their bodies.

learning.reason: S3 Batch Replication can replicate existing objects listed in a manifest on demand.
learning.concept: Live replication for new writes and replication for data that already exists use different initiation methods.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Handling list visibility for a successfully created object
prompt: You confirmed that PutObject succeeded in the same general-purpose S3 bucket. You are considering whether to add a fixed wait because the new object might not yet appear in a list operation for the same prefix immediately afterward. Cross-Region Replication and client-side caching are not involved. Which understanding is correct?

choices.text: After the successful write, you can expect the new object to be present in a LIST operation on the same S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: No fixed delay is needed merely to wait for the object to appear in the listing.

choices.text: A new object will not appear in the listing until a specific amount of time has passed.
choices.explanation: This contradicts S3 strong consistency after a successful write in the same bucket.

choices.text: Only GetObject is strongly consistent; LIST operations are always delayed.
choices.explanation: Current S3 provides strong consistency for listing operations as well.

choices.text: Parts from an in-progress multipart upload are always included in the normal object listing before the upload succeeds.
choices.explanation: Incomplete parts are different from a completed object.

learning.reason: S3 provides strong read-after-write and LIST consistency after a successful write.
learning.concept: The arrival time of event notifications and replication to another Region are separate from this consistency guarantee.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Reading infrequently accessed data immediately
prompt: Large audit files are retrieved only a few times a year, but when requested, they must be readable within milliseconds without waiting for restoration. The files will be stored for a long time, and retrieval charges are acceptable. Which S3 storage class intended for archival data should you choose?

choices.text: Treat preemptively moving the object to another tier before every retrieval as immediate access.
choices.explanation: This does not eliminate the wait after the request.

choices.text: Choose S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
choices.explanation: Although it is intended for archival data, it does not require waiting for restoration before retrieval.

choices.text: Choose S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and assume that every retrieval will take milliseconds.
choices.explanation: Restoration time is normally required before retrieval.

choices.text: Choose S3 Glacier Deep Archive and read the object body immediately with GetObject.
choices.explanation: The object must be restored in advance.

learning.reason: Glacier Instant Retrieval is intended for long-term storage of data that is accessed infrequently and supports retrieval in milliseconds.
learning.concept: Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive involve restoration before retrieval.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Preserving an undated validation point
prompt: You need to preserve an important recovery point before a major upgrade of a provisioned Redshift cluster. Automatically created snapshots are deleted after a short period, but this particular point must be retained until an operator deletes it. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Create a manual snapshot before the upgrade and specify indefinite retention.
choices.explanation: This preserves the validation point independently of the daily automated snapshots.

choices.text: Assume that the automated snapshot with the same name will remain forever.
choices.explanation: Automated snapshots have a retention period.

choices.text: Export the Redshift query history.
choices.explanation: Query history is not a database recovery point.

choices.text: Create a manual snapshot later for any required past time.
choices.explanation: Without a preserved recovery point, a past state cannot be secured retroactively.

learning.reason: Redshift manual snapshots can have a retention period separate from that of automated snapshots.
learning.concept: Do not extend the general scheduled-backup policy; preserve the specific point independently.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Evaluating explicit compression options from data
prompt: You loaded a large amount of historical data into Redshift as a representative sample. You want to compare the current defaults and review recommended compression for each column before deciding on the physical configuration. You do not want to change the current table automatically. Which command should you use?

choices.text: Run only VACUUM and output the recommended encoding for each column.
choices.explanation: VACUUM is not the command for recommending column compression.

choices.text: Run ANALYZE COMPRESSION on the representative data and review the recommendations.
choices.explanation: It allows you to compare compression recommendations without automatically replacing the current column encodings.

choices.text: Change DISTSTYLE to obtain recommended column-compression results.
choices.explanation: Distribution layout and column-compression analysis are different operations.

choices.text: Use the compression ratio of an empty table to obtain representative values.
choices.explanation: An empty table cannot be evaluated based on the distribution of the target data.

learning.reason: ANALYZE COMPRESSION examines the data and can report column-level compression candidates and estimated reduction ratios.
learning.concept: Distinguish an operation that performs analysis from one that rewrites the actual data to apply compression.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Read with strong consistency by bypassing the cache only when needed
prompt: A normal DynamoDB screen that uses DAX can tolerate a short delay. Immediately after some operations, verification requires strong consistency, and the target is the base table rather than a GSI. What should the corresponding DAX request do?

choices.text: Permanently reuse only the first result that remains in the cache.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy consistency immediately after the operation.

choices.text: Set ConsistentRead to true for the target read and use pass-through to DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: This prevents an operation requiring strong consistency from relying on a cached result.

choices.text: Only extend the DAX TTL.
choices.explanation: This could retain a potentially stale value for longer.

choices.text: Treat the same option on a GSI as enabling a strongly consistent read.
choices.explanation: GSIs do not support strongly consistent reads.

learning.reason: DAX passes reads that require strong consistency to DynamoDB and does not store that response in the cache.
learning.concept: Separate reads that should use a cache hit from reads that must verify the latest value immediately.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Enable strongly consistent reads from a remote Region
prompt: With a DynamoDB global table, completed writes in another Region must be reflected in strongly consistent reads. The available Region group and cost have already been confirmed. How should replication and reads be configured? Select two.

choices.text: Specify ConsistentRead for GetItem and similar operations on the corresponding base table in the reader application.
choices.explanation: This uses the contract for a strongly consistent read when the request requires consistency.

choices.text: Create a new global table in the corresponding Region group and select MRSC mode.
choices.explanation: This allows completed updates to be read with strong consistency from the supported Regions.

choices.text: Create independent tables in each Region and periodically export them to S3.
choices.explanation: This does not provide real-time strong consistency.

choices.text: Assume that setting ConsistentRead in one MREC Region makes the same behavior apply across all Regions.
choices.explanation: Asynchronous changes from remote Regions can still be delayed.

choices.text: Only shorten the DynamoDB Accelerator TTL.
choices.explanation: This does not change global-table replication consistency.

learning.reason: MRSC supports strongly consistent reads across multiple Regions.
learning.concept: With MREC, changes between Regions are replicated asynchronously.

category: データストア管理

title: Diagnose a type mismatch between partitions

choices.explanation: This does not correct an input column-type mismatch.

learning.reason: Athena can report a mismatch error when a partition schema is incompatible with the table schema.
learning.concept: Compare the table-wide types with the types and column order of partitions registered separately.

category: データストア管理

title: Reproduce historical business attributes in analytics
prompt: Even after a customer changes departments, historical sales must be aggregated by the department to which the customer belonged at the time of the transaction. Which design preserves historical reports when the dimension is corrected?

choices.text: Use a history-tracking SCD Type 2 for customer attributes, giving each version an effective period and a distinct surrogate key.
choices.explanation: Historical transactions can reference the attribute version that was valid at the time.

choices.text: Always overwrite existing rows with the customer’s latest department.
choices.explanation: The new attribute would be applied to historical transactions.

choices.text: Always set the department value to NULL and eliminate department-level analysis.
choices.explanation: This contradicts the requirement to aggregate by the historical department.

choices.text: Rewrite existing sales dates to the new department-change date.
choices.explanation: This loses the time of the historical fact.

learning.reason: A history-preserving dimension creates a new version whenever an attribute of the business key changes.
learning.concept: Effective periods and surrogate keys identify the attribute version corresponding to when the fact occurred.

category: データストア管理
examDomain: データストア管理
title: Changing the Cost Profile of a Large Table with Low Access Frequency
prompt: An internal records table in DynamoDB is several TB in size. It must support immediate queries through the standard API, but associated access is very infrequent and storage accounts for most of the cost. Which table class should be evaluated?

choices.text: Move all data to Deep Archive and query it immediately through the same API.

choices.explanation: The table class is not changed.

learning.reason: DynamoDB Standard-IA has relatively lower storage costs, while its read and write request pricing differs from Standard.
learning.concept: Choose based on the ratio of storage costs to request costs, and calculate whether the class fits the workload.

category: データストア管理

choices.explanation: You can use the data without copying all of it to your own bucket.

category: データ運用とサポート

prompt: An AWS Batch transformation job returns exit code 75 for a transient access failure and 65 for an invalid schema. You want to retry only the former up to a defined number of attempts and stop immediately for the latter. Which combination should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Use only the job queue priority to select which exit codes are retried.
choices.explanation: Queue priority does not determine the cause of a failure.

choices.text: Configure a finite retry count for the job.
choices.explanation: This limits the number of attempts for the transient failure.

learning.reason: AWS Batch retry strategies can use EvaluateOnExit to select RETRY or EXIT based on conditions.
learning.concept: Define the retry count separately from the classification of errors that should be retried.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Preventing Capacity Exhaustion Without Changing Log Retention
prompt: A provisioned MSK cluster uses compatible brokers, and its log retention period cannot be changed. A temporary increase in ingestion is causing disk utilization to approach its limit. choices.text: Set a target utilization and maximum capacity for storage scaling on the cluster.
choices.explanation: This can expand disk capacity while preserving the retention policy.

choices.text: Change the key used for encryption.
choices.explanation: This does not manage capacity according to utilization.

choices.text: Shorten the log retention period.
choices.explanation: This violates the condition that the retention period must be preserved.

choices.explanation: The number of readers does not configure disk capacity.

learning.reason: MSK's supported automatic storage expansion allows you to specify a target utilization and an expansion limit.
learning.concept: Distinguish shortening the retention period from increasing storage in response to consumption.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Extending visibility for a long-running message
prompt: After receiving a message from SQS, a processing worker waits for an external operation to finish before deleting the message. choices.text: Use DelaySeconds to control the message after it has been received.
choices.explanation: The setting for when a message first becomes visible after being sent is different from visibility after receipt.

choices.text: Call DeleteMessage first and ignore any failure in the external operation.
choices.explanation: The message cannot be recovered if processing fails.

choices.text: Resend the same input to the queue with a new business ID.
choices.explanation: This creates another message and does not change the original message's visibility.

choices.text: Use the ReceiptHandle obtained at receipt time to extend the visibility timeout of the message while it is being processed.
choices.explanation: This delays redelivery of that message and allows it to be deleted after successful processing.

learning.reason: ChangeMessageVisibility can change the visibility timeout of a message that has already been received.
learning.concept: There is no need to change the queue's default setting for every message.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Reducing queued queries during a short workload spike
prompt: A corresponding provisioned Redshift cluster experiences a short-term surge in dashboard reads. When the waiting queue grows, you want to use additional compute only at those times while keeping the current number of always-on nodes unchanged. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Cancel all read queries when they begin waiting.
choices.explanation: The requests still need to be processed.

choices.text: Change only the compression method used for data storage.
choices.explanation: This does not allocate additional capacity to the affected queries.

choices.text: Enable concurrency scaling for the target WLM queue.
choices.explanation: It can use additional capacity for temporary bursts of the applicable queries.

choices.text: Permanently increase the number of all nodes.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to add capacity only temporarily.

learning.reason: Redshift concurrency scaling can use additional capacity for applicable queries based on workload demand.
learning.concept: Additional capacity to reduce queueing serves a different purpose from fixed data placement or canceling queries.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Understanding WAL retention when change capture stalls
prompt: DMS performs CDC from PostgreSQL logical replication. While the task is stopped, WAL is consuming disk space on the source. What should you check before deciding on a recovery approach that does not lose changes?

choices.text: Only shorten the backup retention period at the target.
choices.explanation: This does not investigate the progress of the source's logical replication slot.

choices.text: Change only the connection name.
choices.explanation: The accumulated WAL will not be processed.

choices.text: Compare the progress of the relevant logical replication slot, accumulated WAL, and the stopped DMS task.
choices.explanation: This identifies why retention continues and which changes must be processed when the task resumes.

choices.text: Delete all replication slots without checking anything.
choices.explanation: This could also remove the restart point needed for the required changes.

learning.reason: When a replication slot is not consuming changes, WAL can remain on the source.
learning.concept: To preserve the restart point for changes, check slot progress and source capacity before deciding how to respond.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Monitoring the error rate for one ingestion prefix
prompt: Multiple pipelines use the same S3 bucket. You want to view the request count and errors for one input prefix separately in CloudWatch. A daily aggregate of object size is insufficient. What should you configure?

choices.text: Look only at the bucket's daily storage metrics.
choices.explanation: This does not measure API errors for the specified prefix.

choices.text: Create a request metrics configuration that specifies the target prefix.
choices.explanation: This lets you view requests and errors for the target scope separately in CloudWatch.

choices.text: Set the CloudWatch Logs retention period using only the prefix name.
choices.explanation: This does not enable S3 request metrics.

choices.text: Shorten the object lifecycle.
choices.explanation: This does not configure request measurement.

learning.reason: S3 request metrics support configurations with conditions such as a prefix.
learning.concept: The metric for total storage bytes differs from metrics that evaluate API request activity.

category: データ運用とサポート

title: Combining Two Failures into One Notification Condition
prompt: A data job has separate metric alarms that detect delayed input and a backlog in downstream writes. Operations must be notified only when both alarms are in the ALARM state, while the individual states must remain available on the console. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Configure notifications on a composite alarm that evaluates both alarms with AND.
