choices.explanation: A notification is sent even when only one alarm is in the ALARM state.

choices.text: Delete one of the alarms.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to retain the individual states.

choices.text: Add the values of both metrics regardless of their meaning or units.
choices.explanation: This does not represent an AND condition for the two alarm states.

learning.reason: A composite alarm can combine the states of other alarms with a logical expression.
learning.concept: Separate the rule that combines alarm states from the thresholds of the individual metrics.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Checking the Cause of a Failed Ingestion
prompt: An AWS Quick Sight SPICE refresh failed. The target dataset and ingestion ID are known. You need to investigate the failure reason through the API rather than merely seeing that the current display is outdated. What should you consult?

choices.text: Change only the dashboard name.
choices.explanation: This does not retrieve the reason for the ingestion failure.

choices.text: Treat the S3 bucket capacity as the reason for the ingestion failure without further investigation.
choices.explanation: This does not check the specific error for the ingestion.

choices.text: Start the same ingestion repeatedly without conditions and do not check the previous results.
choices.explanation: This does not identify the cause of the failure.

choices.text: Call DescribeIngestion with the target dataset and ingestion ID, and check ErrorInfo.
choices.explanation: This identifies the failure information for the specified ingestion.

learning.reason: DescribeIngestion returns the ingestion status and available error information.
learning.concept: Distinguish the dashboard display from the result of the ingestion process that supplies its data.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Reducing the Cost of Retaining Searchable Old Logs
prompt: In the corresponding provisioned OpenSearch Service, you need to continue searching old logs that are no longer updated. You want to reduce costs compared with keeping them in the hot tier and avoid restoring a snapshot every time you search. Where should you move them?

choices.text: Move qualifying old indexes to UltraWarm.
choices.explanation: The indexes can be moved out of the hot tier and remain searchable as read-only indexes.

choices.text: Duplicate the hot indexes and search both copies.
choices.explanation: This does not reduce the cost of retaining old logs.

choices.text: Unconditionally exclude all indexes from search.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to search the historical logs.

choices.text: Delete the indexes and retain them only in a snapshot.
choices.explanation: The indexes would have to be restored whenever they are needed for use.

learning.reason: UltraWarm can retain infrequently updated, read-only indexes in a searchable state.
learning.concept: Distinguish a tier that preserves ordinary index search from a backup that must be restored before use.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Aggregating Ingestion Costs by Team
prompt: The corresponding team tags have been added to resources used by Glue and supporting services. To track new costs by tag in Cost Explorer and similar tools, what must be done on the billing side?

choices.text: Use the tag values only as dashboard headings.
choices.explanation: The values are not imported as billing classification information.

choices.text: Manually move the tagged resources to another Region.
choices.explanation: This does not activate cost allocation tags.

choices.text: Only set an overall budget in AWS Budgets.
choices.explanation: This does not enable aggregation by team tag.

choices.text: In the billing management console, activate the applicable user-defined cost allocation tags.
choices.explanation: After activation, the corresponding costs can be classified by tag.

learning.reason: Activating user-defined tags as cost allocation tags enables classification of the corresponding charges.
learning.concept: Tagging resources alone does not necessarily make them available for aggregation in billing reports.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Reclaiming Unused Space After Mass Deletions
prompt: A large portion of old data was deleted from a large table in provisioned Amazon Redshift. There is a maintenance window during which you cannot wait for automatic reclamation, and the remaining data is sufficiently well sorted. What should you use to prioritize manually reclaiming only the space from deleted rows?

choices.text: Run VACUUM SORT ONLY, which always also reclaims space from deleted rows.
choices.explanation: This operation specifies sorting only and does not reclaim space from deleted rows.

choices.text: Run ANALYZE only.
choices.explanation: This updates statistics but does not manually reclaim space from deleted rows.

choices.text: Shorten the backup retention period.
choices.explanation: This does not reclaim deleted-row space in the active table.

choices.text: Run VACUUM DELETE ONLY on the target table.
choices.explanation: This reclaims space that is no longer needed without sorting the table.

learning.reason: VACUUM DELETE ONLY reclaims space from deleted rows without performing a sort operation.
learning.concept: Updating statistics, sorting rows, and reclaiming space are separate operational objectives.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Recording Processing Stages Separately from Input Data
prompt: You enrich SQS events with EventBridge Pipes before sending them to a target. During the investigation period, you need to see detailed stages such as enrichment, not only the time when an error was recorded. The input body contains sensitive values and must not be written to logs. Which settings should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Assume that setting the logging level to record only errors provides the execution history for every stage.
choices.explanation: It does not include details about successful intermediate steps and other stages.

choices.text: Increase the SQS message retention period.
choices.explanation: This does not create a record of the Pipe's processing stages.

choices.text: Configure a log destination for the Pipe and set the log level to TRACE for the required period.
choices.explanation: This provides detailed records about the execution stages.

choices.text: Leave the setting that includes execution data disabled.
choices.explanation: This prevents sensitive input bodies and other execution payloads from being added to execution logs.

choices.text: Assume that outputting all execution data is also required to enable TRACE.
choices.explanation: The logging detail level and inclusion of execution payloads can be configured separately.

learning.reason: The Pipes log level controls execution detail, while recording execution data is configured separately.
learning.concept: Detailed processing records do not require the event body to be output as well.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Diagnosing Unused Compute Capacity in a Spark Job
prompt: You are investigating the cost of a Glue Spark job with Auto Scaling enabled. The job configuration limit alone does not show the difference between the executors that existed during execution and the executors requested by Spark. What should you compare?

choices.text: Estimate the number of executors only from the number of storage bytes in S3.
choices.explanation: This does not show the number requested by Spark or the number provisioned.

choices.text: Count only the number of CloudTrail events for failed runs.
choices.explanation: This does not measure executor utilization within the job.

choices.text: Look only at the account's Glue quota.
choices.explanation: This is a maximum limit, not the capacity actually used by the job.

choices.text: Compare the corresponding Auto Scaling metrics in CloudWatch for the number of executors and the number of executors needed.
choices.explanation: This shows the difference between allocated capacity and requested capacity over time.

learning.reason: Glue Auto Scaling provides metrics for the current number of executors and the number required by Spark.
learning.concept: The initially configured maximum alone cannot be used to evaluate the resources actually operating.

category: データ運用とサポート
examDomain: データ運用とサポート
title: Monitoring the Impact on Production Writes During Index Creation
prompt: You are adding a provisioned GSI to an active DynamoDB table. After backfilling begins, you need to determine whether the index-processing work is throttling writes during creation and adjust capacity if necessary. Which metrics should you use to track index creation and its impact on users? Select two.

choices.text: Rename the index to avoid insufficient capacity.
choices.explanation: Renaming the index does not change the backfill computation or capacity.

choices.text: Check only the number of expired TTL items.
choices.explanation: This is not a metric for index creation or write throttling.

choices.text: Monitor OnlineIndexPercentageProgress for the target GSI.
choices.explanation: This shows the progress of index creation, including the backfill.

choices.text: Look only at OnlineIndexThrottleEvents and conclude that there is no application throttling if it is 0.
choices.explanation: This metric can be 0 during backfill and cannot by itself determine the impact on writes to the base table.

choices.text: Check WriteThrottleEvents and ThrottledRequests for the base table during the same period.
choices.explanation: These metrics help identify throttling experienced by application writes.

learning.reason: OnlineIndexPercentageProgress shows index-creation progress, while write throttling on the base table is monitored through base-table metrics.
learning.concept: Correlate application access with the impact of index backfill along the same timeline.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Changing data permissions by processing step on the same cluster
prompt: On the corresponding EMR on EC2 cluster, Spark steps from different teams run sequentially. Each step must access only the S3 inputs it needs, without sharing all teams’ permissions through a single EC2 instance profile. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Combine all teams’ permissions in the cluster’s EC2 instance profile.
choices.explanation: This cannot maintain permission separation by job.

choices.text: Configure the cluster to use runtime roles, and specify a runtime role with the required scope when starting each step.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes AWS access for steps running on the same cluster.

choices.text: Include the team name in the step name.
choices.explanation: A name alone does not change the access scope.

choices.text: Pass credentials for a shared administrative role to every step.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to restrict access to only the necessary S3 inputs.

learning.reason: An individual IAM role for accessing AWS resources at runtime can be specified for the corresponding EMR step.
learning.concept: Separate the permissions of the cluster-wide EC2 execution environment from those required by each analysis job.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Restricting transfer permissions for multiple users from one role
prompt: A Transfer Family deployment uses an S3 home directory for each partner. The base IAM role supports multiple folders, but each SFTP session must access only its assigned prefix. What should be added to the corresponding S3 server configuration?

choices.text: Allow the entire bucket through the shared role and only write a prefix in the user’s display name.
choices.explanation: A display name does not control S3 access permissions.

choices.text: Use a per-user session policy that allows only the assigned S3 prefix and operations on the applicable objects.
choices.explanation: This limits the scope of the session even when the shared role is used.

choices.text: Specify only the default starting directory in the FTP client.
choices.explanation: This does not grant the server permission to reject requests outside the allowed scope.

choices.text: Change the bucket retention period for each user.
choices.explanation: A retention policy does not limit the access scope.

learning.reason: With S3 in Transfer Family, a session policy can further restrict the permissions of the role assumed by the user.
learning.concept: Configure the home path shown to the user together with the operations permitted in S3.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Collecting an organization’s compliance status centrally
prompt: AWS Config rules have already evaluated their targets across multiple accounts and Regions. A central operations team wants to view a list of the results. Aggregation should not require changing rules or resources in the individual accounts. What should be used?

choices.text: Stop all recording settings in the member accounts.
choices.explanation: This would remove the current prerequisite data that aggregation relies on.

choices.text: Integrate only the email destinations for CloudWatch alarms.
choices.explanation: This does not create a single list of Config configuration history and compliance status.

choices.text: Configure a Config aggregator centrally that includes the organization’s targets.
choices.explanation: This aggregates the evaluation results from the accounts for review.

choices.text: Assume that creating a central Config rule evaluates resources in every account with one rule.
choices.explanation: A central local rule does not aggregate results from other targets.

learning.reason: A Config aggregator collects configuration and compliance results from multiple accounts and Regions.
learning.concept: Centrally viewing data is separate from deploying evaluation rules to each account.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Sharing only a published visualization for viewing
prompt: An author in AWS Quick Sight publishes a dashboard from an analysis. Internal users should see the completed view but must not be allowed to edit the analysis. Which sharing method should be used?

choices.text: Share the published dashboard with the target users as viewers.
choices.explanation: They can view it without receiving permission to edit the analysis.

choices.text: Grant full access to the source bucket of the dataset and do not share the dashboard.
choices.explanation: This does not make the completed view available to users.

choices.text: Grant all users co-owner permissions on the original analysis.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with preventing edits before approval.

choices.text: Change only the dashboard display name and give everyone edit permissions.
choices.explanation: Viewing and editing are not separated.

learning.reason: A published dashboard can be shared with view-only permissions.
learning.concept: Separate permission to co-edit an analysis from permission to view its published version.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Temporarily stop decryption while preserving a recovery path
prompt: A test application for protected resources directly requests Decrypt from a customer managed KMS key. For an investigation, the existing policies must remain unchanged, but the key must be temporarily prevented from being used for any new cryptographic operations. After the investigation, the same key must be usable again. Which action should be taken?

choices.text: Delete only the key alias.
choices.explanation: Requests that specify the key ID may still succeed.

choices.text: Delete the key and create a new key with the same name.
choices.explanation: A different key cannot continue decrypting existing ciphertexts.

choices.text: Remove IAM permissions only from some callers.
choices.explanation: Other authorized principals would not be restricted uniformly.

choices.text: Disable the target key, then re-enable the same key after approval.
choices.explanation: This stops use without deleting the key and allows use to resume.

learning.reason: Disabling a customer managed key stops cryptographic operations while allowing the same key to be re-enabled later.
learning.concept: The recovery premise differs from deleting a key and losing its key material.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Delegate permission grants with limited authority
prompt: A Lake Formation administrator wants to delegate granting SELECT on a table to a table owner for some users. Without broadly giving the owner other administrative permissions, what should be granted so the owner can grant the permission again?

choices.text: Only add the table ARN to the owner's tag.
choices.explanation: A tag alone does not grant permission.

choices.text: Make the owner an administrator for the entire data lake.
choices.explanation: This is broader than delegating SELECT on the target table.

choices.text: Grant the owner SELECT on the target table with the grantable permission.
choices.explanation: The owner can delegate the specified resource permission.

choices.text: Grant ordinary SELECT only.
choices.explanation: The owner could query the table but could not grant access to other users.

learning.reason: A grantable permission in Lake Formation allows the recipient to delegate the received resource permission to other principals.
learning.concept: Being able to query data is different from being able to authorize others to query it.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Separate index permissions by team in a shared domain
prompt: Authentication settings inside and outside OpenSearch are already configured, and multiple teams use the same domain. Each team must be able to search its own log indexes but must not be able to read another team's indexes. Which combination should be used? Choose two.

choices.text: Configure each team role with permissions limited to the allowed index patterns and search operations.
choices.explanation: Each role's permitted scope of operations can be defined.

choices.text: Rely on node-to-node encryption alone to separate search results by team.
choices.explanation: Encryption does not evaluate a user's permitted access scope.

choices.text: Only instruct users to use their own index names in each search interface.
choices.explanation: Requests specifying another index would not otherwise be controlled.

choices.text: Map the authenticated principals for each team to the corresponding roles in OpenSearch.
choices.explanation: Users can be given permissions limited to their own indexes.

choices.text: Distribute a shared master user to everyone.
choices.explanation: This does not provide permissions restricted by index.

learning.reason: Fine-grained access control allows index-level permissions to be assigned to roles and authenticated principals to be mapped to those roles.
learning.concept: Permission to connect to an endpoint does not determine which indexes all teams can read.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Find potential external exposure from policies
prompt: The data lake buckets are intentionally shared within the organization. Instead of examining past GetObject activity, you need to continuously find buckets that policies make reachable by principals outside the trusted boundary. What should you use?

choices.text: Determine all external permissions solely from successful CloudTrail GetObject events.
choices.explanation: This would not find permissions that exist for external principals but have not been used.

choices.text: Use Macie to search only for personal information in file contents.
choices.explanation: Content classification does not analyze who can access a bucket under its policy.

choices.text: Configure external access analysis with the organization as the trust zone and review findings for S3.
choices.explanation: This identifies policy-based access allowed to principals outside the organization.

choices.text: Aggregate S3 capacity metrics across the organization.
choices.explanation: This does not detect external sharing defined by policies.

learning.reason: IAM Access Analyzer external access analysis detects policy-based resource sharing outside the trusted boundary.
learning.concept: Access recorded as used and access permitted by policy are different things.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Record management operations from new members centrally
prompt: Members are regularly added to an AWS Organizations organization. You need to record data-platform management API activity in a central audit destination, without requiring each member to create its own trail, and prevent members from deleting the configuration. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Manually create one independent trail in each account.
choices.explanation: Configuration work would still be required whenever a new member joins.

choices.text: Assume that the event history in the central account automatically displays records for all members.
choices.explanation: The event history in the central account alone does not collect management events from each member.

choices.text: Create an organization trail with the required permissions and deliver the relevant management events to a central destination.
choices.explanation: This configures organization-wide auditing without manual work in member accounts.

choices.text: Write the organization name in a tag on the central S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not configure CloudTrail delivery to start from each member account.

learning.reason: An organization trail can be configured from the management account or another authorized account and applied to member accounts.
learning.concept: A trail managed by an individual account and a trail applied across an organization have different configuration authorities.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Prevent settings that accidentally create public buckets
prompt: Protect both the existing and future buckets in a private analytics account. If a public ACL or public policy is specified accidentally, public access must still be blocked, while approved private sharing should continue to be evaluated normally. What should you configure?

choices.text: Enable account-level S3 Block Public Access and configure the permissions required for private sharing in each bucket.
choices.explanation: This can block public-access settings, including for new buckets.

choices.text: Include the word private in the file name.
choices.explanation: A name does not prevent a public policy from being evaluated.

choices.text: Configure a public-access denial only on one existing bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not apply to other buckets created in the future.

choices.text: Only encrypt the S3 data.
choices.explanation: Encryption alone does not block public ACLs or public policies.

learning.reason: Enabling S3 Block Public Access at the account level applies public-access controls to the account's buckets and related resources.
learning.concept: Blocking public access is separate from configuring permissions that allow specific approved principals to access resources privately.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Make it easier to maintain database connections during rotation
prompt: An ETL process for the associated database opens connections frequently. You want to avoid a rotation method that changes the password for the same user first while the password is being updated. You can manage two database users with the same business permissions. Which rotation strategy should you use?

choices.text: Use only one user and assume that the database and secret are always updated simultaneously.
choices.explanation: This does not address the possibility of updating the two at different stages.

choices.text: Only copy the current password to multiple secrets.
choices.explanation: This does not switch between two database users.

choices.text: Rotate only the KMS key used to encrypt the secret on a regular basis.
choices.explanation: The database credentials are not rotated.

choices.text: Use the alternating-users rotation strategy for the associated database and prepare the required administrative credentials.
choices.explanation: You can update the value for the user that is not currently in use and switch to it for subsequent connections.

learning.reason: With the alternating-users strategy, you can update the password for the other user and then switch the current credentials used by the application.
learning.concept: The application should also retrieve the secret when it is updated instead of relying on a fixed value.

category: データセキュリティとガバナンス
examDomain: データセキュリティとガバナンス
title: Prevent replacement of images with the same release tag
prompt: In an ECR production repository, approved release tags must not be overwritten. Only the development tag dev-latest in the same repository should remain mutable. Which two ECR settings should you combine to support tag-exclusion rules? Select two.

choices.text: Enable image scanning only and allow pushes to the same tag.
choices.explanation: Scanning does not prevent a tag from being replaced.

choices.text: Set the repository's tag mutability to IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION.
choices.explanation: Existing tags that are not excluded can be protected from overwriting.

choices.text: Only add the word approved to the tag.
choices.explanation: A name alone does not prohibit overwriting the same tag.

choices.text: Limit the exclusion filter for immutable settings to dev-latest only.
choices.explanation: This makes only the development tag mutable.

choices.text: Only add a deletion rule for untagged images.
choices.explanation: This does not control overwriting an existing tag.

learning.reason: When ECR image-tag immutability is configured, overwriting an existing tag covered by the setting is rejected.
learning.concept: This setting fixes release identifiers; it is separate from retaining unused images or scanning for vulnerabilities.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Reading split shards while preserving order
prompt: Kinesis Data Streams is processed with KCL. After a shard is split, you want to process the records at the end of the old shard for the same partition key before processing records in the new child shards. What should the consumer do?

choices.text: Use KCL leases and checkpoints to process through the parent’s ending position, and let KCL start the children.
choices.explanation: This preserves ordering for the same key across resharding.

choices.text: Process the children first as soon as they are discovered, and reread the parent later.
choices.explanation: This would process child records before older records.

choices.text: Delete all checkpoints for the parent at the time of the split.
choices.explanation: This removes the basis for determining whether parent processing is complete.

choices.text: Order all records only by the time the consumer accepts them.
choices.explanation: This does not necessarily produce the same order as before the split.

learning.reason: KCL uses the relationship between parent and child shards and processes the children after the parent has finished.
learning.concept: Independently prioritizing the children can disrupt processing order for the same key.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Processing retained Kafka input from the initial startup
prompt: Several days of events remain in an MSK topic. You are creating a new Lambda connection with a dedicated consumer group that has no offset yet, and you want to process the retained events from the beginning. Which starting position should you use?

choices.text: Specify TRIM_HORIZON for the new consumer group.
choices.explanation: Processing can begin with the oldest events within the retention range.

choices.text: Reuse the consumer group ID used for another existing purpose.
choices.explanation: Its previously committed position could affect reading.

choices.text: Specify LATEST and assume that all input from before startup will also be processed.
choices.explanation: This normally starts with newly arriving events.

choices.text: Enable versioning on the output S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: This does not change where Kafka reading starts.

learning.reason: For a Kafka event source, TRIM_HORIZON starts processing from the oldest available position.
learning.concept: Distinguish a new group’s initial position from the committed position of an existing group.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Reloading only one incorrect table during a running migration
prompt: The corresponding DMS full-load and CDC task is running. Only one table is in an incorrect state, and you want changes to continue being applied to the other tables. The reload conditions for the target have been confirmed. What should you do?

choices.text: Select only the affected table in the task and run ReloadTables.
choices.explanation: There is no need to reload the healthy tables from the beginning.

choices.text: Stop the entire task and restart loading all tables from the beginning.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to continue operating the other tables.

choices.text: Leave the affected table removed from the table mappings.
choices.explanation: This does not reload the data that is currently missing from the table.

choices.text: Only extend the log retention period.
choices.explanation: This does not instruct DMS to reload the selected table.

learning.reason: DMS can reload only the selected tables in the corresponding running task by using the table reload operation.
learning.concept: Distinguish reloading the entire existing task from selecting specific tables for reload.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Limiting integrity verification to incrementally transferred data
prompt: You regularly synchronize a large set of files with DataSync. You want to verify the integrity of the transferred data at the end, without scanning all files that were not transferred during the current run every time. What should you specify in the task?

choices.text: Set only a bandwidth limit.
choices.explanation: This does not determine which files are verified.

choices.text: Perform no additional verification after the transfer.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to verify the transferred data afterward.

choices.text: Specify ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED for VerifyMode.
choices.explanation: This limits verification to the data transferred during the current run.

choices.text: Use POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT to compare the entire dataset.
choices.explanation: This also compares data outside the current transfer.

learning.reason: DataSync provides a verification mode that targets only the data transferred during the current run.
learning.concept: Choose between the scanning cost of full verification and verification that covers the current transfer.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Exclude Input Matching Processed Keys
prompt: A Glue Spark job processes the day's transactions. The input contains multiple detail records with the same transaction ID. Exclude all detail records whose IDs exist in a table of processed transaction IDs, while preserving the remaining records with the same count and columns as the input. Transaction IDs are not NULL. Which join is appropriate?

choices.text: Perform a LEFT ANTI JOIN from the day's details to the processed-ID table on transaction ID.
choices.explanation: Only detail records with no match on the right side remain.

choices.text: Perform an INNER JOIN between the two tables and project only the detail columns.
choices.explanation: Only details matching processed IDs are output.

choices.text: Compare the transaction IDs from the two tables with EXCEPT and output the difference set directly.
choices.explanation: A difference set of IDs cannot preserve the required detail columns and record count.

choices.text: Perform a LEFT SEMI JOIN from the day's details to the processed-ID table on transaction ID.
choices.explanation: Details matching processed IDs remain.

learning.reason: A left anti join returns input rows whose transaction IDs have no match on the right and does not aggregate the left-side details.
learning.concept: Selecting nonmatching rows is separate from removing duplicate output rows.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Do Not Leave Transformation Fields to Free-Form Model Output
prompt: Extract fields from documents in S3 with a Bedrock-supported model and pass them downstream using a predefined JSON schema. You do not want to interpret free-form model text manually, and Converse can be configured for schema-compliant output. What should you specify?

choices.text: Only lower the temperature.
choices.explanation: Reducing response variability does not guarantee required fields and types.

choices.text: Only instruct the model in natural language to “return JSON” and omit structural validation.
choices.explanation: No schema is specified to define the structure.

choices.text: Change only the S3 file extension to .json.
choices.explanation: This does not constrain the structure of the model response.

choices.text: Specify a JSON Schema containing the required fields and types in Converse structured output.
choices.explanation: This constrains the format so downstream systems can process it mechanically.

learning.reason: For supported models, structured output can constrain the result structure by specifying a JSON Schema.
learning.concept: Even when the structure is valid, the extracted values must be separately checked against the source text.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Break Up an Execution Plan Expanded by Repeated Transformations
prompt: In a Spark batch job, a process repeatedly applies another transformation to the previous DataFrame many times. The logical plan becomes large, and you want to record intermediate state reliably in specified available storage and shorten the plan. What should you use?

choices.text: Set the appropriate checkpoint directory and checkpoint the DataFrame at the required iterations.
choices.explanation: The saved state can become the starting point for the next iteration.

choices.text: Change only the data output path name on every loop iteration.
choices.explanation: The DataFrame dependency chain is unchanged.

choices.text: Only reduce the number of log lines recorded by the application.
choices.explanation: This does not shorten the logical plan created by the iterations.

choices.text: Only reduce the value of spark.sql.shuffle.partitions.
choices.explanation: Changing the number of processing partitions does not truncate the logical plan.

learning.reason: DataFrame checkpointing saves an intermediate result and truncates the logical plan.
learning.concept: In-memory caching alone does not create a break in a logical plan that continues to grow.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Redistribute Data into Range-Friendly Output Groups
prompt: In Spark, you want to separate the key ranges assigned to each output. The current input partitions are unordered, and all timestamps are mixed in the same file. Shuffle required for sorting is acceptable, and you want to partition the data by time ranges. Which operation should you use?

choices.text: Only add the date to the output file names of the existing partitions.
choices.explanation: The actual time range within each file does not change.

choices.text: Only use coalesce to combine the existing partitions.
choices.explanation: This does not redistribute data based on value ranges.

choices.text: Hash-partition on a column that has the same value for every row.
choices.explanation: Time ranges are not separated and data is likely to concentrate in one place.

choices.text: Specify the time column in repartitionByRange and output the range-partitioned data.
choices.explanation: Rows can be placed by key range without relying on the input order.

learning.reason: repartitionByRange creates partitions based on the value ranges of the selected columns.
learning.concept: Reducing the number of partitions is different from redistributing data using key ranges.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Do not hold later input behind one slow lookup
prompt: An asynchronous API is called to enrich Flink events. The number of concurrent lookups must be limited, input order does not need to be preserved, and results should be emitted as responses arrive. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Use orderedWait to keep all output in input order.
choices.explanation: If the first request is slow, later results must wait before being emitted.

choices.text: Use Async I/O with unorderedWait, and configure capacity and timeout.
choices.explanation: This reduces the need to wait for the first slow result.

choices.text: Call the watermark the output-completion URL.
choices.explanation: Watermark progression does not produce results from external lookups.

choices.text: Make synchronous calls one at a time.
choices.explanation: This does not provide the required concurrent enrichment.

learning.reason: With Flink Async I/O in unordered mode, completed results can be emitted as they finish.
learning.concept: Capacity and timeout settings control both the number of concurrent lookups and delays.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Handle monetary rounding errors according to the calculation specification
prompt: A Python ETL process adds decimal monetary amounts received as strings and applies the rounding required by policy at the second decimal place. The process must not introduce error by converting to binary floating point first. How should it process the values?

choices.text: Always truncate the digits after the decimal point manually without specifying the rounding policy.
choices.explanation: This does not implement the business rounding specification.

choices.text: Create Decimal values from the original strings, perform decimal arithmetic, and then call quantize with the required rounding mode.
choices.explanation: This avoids introducing float approximations at input time.

choices.text: Concatenate the monetary strings as they are.
choices.explanation: Concatenation is not numeric addition.

choices.text: Convert to float first and then put that value into Decimal.
choices.explanation: This may carry an existing binary approximation into the calculation.

learning.reason: Decimal represents decimal values directly when created from strings, and quantize applies a rounding rule.
learning.concept: Use an accurate monetary representation consistently for input and intermediate calculations.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Stop ineligible input before enrichment
prompt: SQS order events are received through EventBridge Pipes. Only events of the target type should invoke Lambda to retrieve information from an external API; all other events must be filtered out without calling the enrichment API. Where should the condition be configured?

choices.text: Run enrichment for all events and filter them at the target.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to avoid unnecessary external API calls.

choices.text: Lower the pipe target's retry count.
choices.explanation: The events entering the initial enrichment are unchanged.

choices.text: Disable execution logging for the enrichment destination.
choices.explanation: This does not reduce the actual external calls.

choices.text: Specify the required order type in the pipe source filter.
choices.explanation: Events outside the target set can be filtered before they reach enrichment.

learning.reason: A Pipes event filter is applied before enrichment.
learning.concept: Filtering at the target cannot prevent an enrichment call that occurs earlier.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Export changes in a specified history-table interval to S3
prompt: A full export of a DynamoDB table with PITR enabled has already been stored in S3. This run must retain only the changes within a time range as files, relative to the previous snapshot. It must not consume read capacity. What should be used?

choices.text: Use an incremental export specifying the previous completion time and the current end time.
choices.explanation: This retrieves the changes without scanning the table directly.

choices.text: Give the bucket a new name and assume that the differences will be obtained automatically.
choices.explanation: No read range is configured on the DynamoDB side.

choices.text: Scan the table every time and use only a filter expression to produce the differences.
choices.explanation: This consumes read capacity and cannot detect deleted items.

choices.text: Disable PITR and manually copy all items to S3.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the conditions for exporting changes for a specified time range.

learning.reason: DynamoDB incremental export can write changes from a specified period to S3.
learning.concept: Distinguish the initial full snapshot from the range of updates applied afterward.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Retaining Existing Artifacts After Stack Deletion
prompt: A CloudFormation stack for a temporary data pipeline is being decommissioned. An S3 bucket containing production data must continue to be retained by another operator. The bucket must not be included for deletion when the stack is deleted. Which setting should be used?

choices.text: Empty the bucket, then delete the stack normally.
choices.explanation: This would lose the data and bucket that must be retained.

choices.text: Enable termination protection for the entire stack, then delete it.
choices.explanation: This prevents deletion of the stack itself instead of retaining the bucket.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy to Retain on the target bucket.
choices.explanation: The bucket remains after the stack is deleted.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy, which applies only to replacement during updates.
choices.explanation: This attribute does not apply to the stack deletion in this scenario.

learning.reason: DeletionPolicy Retain on a resource can keep the actual resource when the stack is deleted.
learning.concept: This differs from the policy applied when a resource is replaced during a stack update.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Converting Valid Rows While Distinguishing Unparseable Amounts
prompt: In Athena, monetary amounts are provided as strings. A small number of values cannot be converted, but the query for valid rows must not fail. Treat unconvertible values as NULL at that point and pass them separately to a data-quality metric. Which expression should be used?

choices.text: Always replace even valid monetary amounts with NULL.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to convert valid values.

choices.text: Convert the original input to an amount based on its length.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the monetary amount represented by the string.

choices.text: Run a regular CAST on every row.
choices.explanation: The query may fail when it encounters an unconvertible value.

choices.text: Convert the amount column to DECIMAL with TRY_CAST and evaluate failed rows separately.
choices.explanation: The entire query does not stop even when some inputs fail conversion.

learning.reason: TRY_CAST returns NULL when conversion fails.
learning.concept: Replacing failures with zero would make them indistinguishable from valid zero amounts.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Matching Aggregated Values Without Expanding Detailed Rows
prompt: Daily regional sales counts are aggregated with Glue Spark. Referential integrity has been verified, and the regional master contains one row per region. The final output only needs the total for each region. How can you obtain the same result without sending all detailed fact rows into the join?

choices.text: Aggregate only the regional master by region key.
choices.explanation: This does not reduce the large fact table before the join.

choices.text: Aggregate the fact table by region key first, then join the aggregated result to the regional master.
choices.explanation: This reduces the rows sent to the join while adding the regional information.

choices.text: Keep only the first row from each region in the fact table.
choices.explanation: This loses the required totals.

choices.text: Perform a Cartesian join of every fact detail row with all master rows without a region key.
choices.explanation: This cannot calculate correct regional values.

learning.reason: Aggregating first against a unique mapping table allows the smaller aggregated input to be joined.
learning.concept: Because the master key is unique, the aggregation does not introduce duplicate amounts or counts.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Specifying Capacity for Temporary Extraction Before Writing to S3
prompt: A corresponding AWS Batch Fargate job extracts a compressed file into temporary storage. It needs 35 GiB of working space, writes the result to S3, and does not need to retain the temporary disk after the job ends. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Use S3 Lifecycle to change only the storage class of the output.
choices.explanation: This does not increase local capacity during the transformation.

choices.text: Increase only the vCPU in the job definition.
choices.explanation: This does not directly change temporary disk capacity.

choices.text: Set ephemeralStorage in the job definition to at least 35 GiB within the supported range.
choices.explanation: This provides the temporary capacity required for extraction during execution.

choices.text: Assume that the same temporary files can always be retrieved after the job stops.
choices.explanation: Ephemeral storage is released with the lifetime of the job.

learning.reason: For the corresponding Fargate job, the amount of ephemeral storage can be specified in the job definition.
learning.concept: The capacity for working space and the persistence of output artifacts in S3 are managed separately.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Explicitly mapping nested JSON fields to table columns
prompt: You need to load nested JSON from S3 into Redshift. The required values are in inner fields, and the input keys have different names from the target columns. What should you use to specify the COPY mapping without recreating the files?

choices.text: Prepare a JSONPaths file containing paths that match the column order and specify it in COPY.
choices.explanation: This loads values from the corresponding nested paths into the intended columns.

choices.text: Change only the target distribution key.
choices.explanation: This does not change the target columns for JSON fields.

choices.text: List only the file names in the COPY manifest.
choices.explanation: This selects the input files but does not specify the mapping between columns and nested paths.

choices.text: Leave the key names different and rely only on the JSON auto setting to match them.
choices.explanation: This does not explicitly map fields with different names to the required columns.

learning.reason: A JSONPaths file specifies the JSON paths used to extract input values and their column order.
learning.concept: This differs from automatic mapping, which assumes applicable matching names.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Testing connectivity to a private JDBC endpoint before running a job
prompt: You created an AWS Glue connection. Before running ETL that connects to a private database, you want to test the network and credentials once using the same connection definition and role. You do not need to produce output data. Which check should you perform?

choices.text: Connect from a development terminal in another VPC using the same JDBC URL and consider the Glue connection valid if it succeeds.
choices.explanation: This does not test the subnet, security group, and execution role that Glue uses.

choices.text: Check whether the ETL role can read the secret in Secrets Manager and consider the database connection established if it succeeds.
choices.explanation: Successful access to the secret does not verify the JDBC path or database authentication.

choices.text: Analyze the path with Reachability Analyzer and consider the credentials valid if the destination is reachable.
choices.explanation: It can analyze network configuration, but it cannot verify that the database accepts the credentials.

choices.text: Select the connection in Glue Data Catalog and test the connection using the IAM role for ETL.
choices.explanation: This verifies communication and authentication using the target connection settings and role, separately from the existing transformation process.

learning.reason: The Glue connection test verifies connectivity using the specified connection and role.
learning.concept: Isolate connection prerequisites before proceeding to data transformation or output validation.

category: データの取り込みと変換
examDomain: データの取り込みと変換
title: Configuring a merge after branching with no failures
prompt: An MWAA DAG selects only certain input formats. Branches that are not executed become skipped. When a selected branch succeeds, you want the merge task to run as long as there are no other failures. Which trigger rule should you use?

choices.text: Set none_failed_min_one_success on the merge task.
choices.explanation: The merge can run when at least one branch that should execute succeeds and no branch has failed.

choices.text: Set it to all_done so that it always continues even when an upstream task fails.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid merging when an upstream task has failed.

choices.text: Use one_success alone to determine that the other branches have not failed.
choices.explanation: This rule does not prohibit failures in the other branches.

choices.text: Use the default all_success and treat skipped branches as successful.
choices.explanation: The condition may not be satisfied because unselected branches are skipped.

learning.reason: none_failed_min_one_success can be used when no upstream task has failed and at least one upstream task has succeeded.
learning.concept: Distinguish intentionally skipped branches caused by branching from upstream failures.

category: データの取り込みと変換

title: Aligning ingestion latency with the processing unit
prompt: In Glue streaming micro-batches, each batch finishes soon after processing starts, but the batches are large and the intervals between start times are long. The additional load from smaller processing units is acceptable, and you want output to be reflected at shorter intervals. What should you review?

choices.text: Shorten the corresponding windowSize and measure whether processing keeps up at the shorter interval.
choices.explanation: If processing capacity is sufficient, this can reduce the wait before results are reflected.

choices.text: Reset the Glue job bookmark used for batch jobs.
choices.explanation: This does not specify the interval between streaming micro-batches.

choices.text: Only extend the S3 export retention period.
choices.explanation: This does not change how frequently transformation starts.

choices.text: Shorten the display name of each job.
choices.explanation: This has no effect on the processing unit.

learning.reason: The streaming window size affects the interval between micro-batches.
learning.concept: Ensure sufficient processing capacity while balancing latency against the overhead of smaller batches.

title: Periodically Retrieve Files from an External SFTP Server to S3
prompt: The provider places the input on its own SFTP server and cannot send files to your SFTP server. You want to ingest selected files into S3 without maintaining a custom client host on your side. Which two components should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Write the external SFTP URL in an S3 Lifecycle filter.
choices.explanation: Lifecycle does not retrieve files from external systems.

choices.text: Configure a Transfer Family SFTP connector that can connect to the provider.
choices.explanation: This creates a managed path for connecting from your side to the external SFTP server.

choices.text: Synchronize the external files using only S3 replication.
choices.explanation: An external SFTP server is not an S3 bucket.

choices.text: Specify the target remote path and the S3 destination, then start a transfer that retrieves the files externally.
choices.explanation: This imports only the required files into the designated input location.

choices.text: Publish your own Transfer Family server and wait for uploads from the provider.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the condition that the provider cannot send files.

learning.reason: A Transfer Family SFTP connector can initiate transfers from an external SFTP server and use S3 as the destination.
learning.concept: Distinguish between a server on your side that accepts connections from the provider and a connector that connects from your side to the external server.

category: データの取り込みと変換
